(The Dharma Master visualizes: The Buddhas of the ten directions sit in a circle around the site of enlightenment, together emitting the light from between their brows—the white tuft of hair—which enters this water to manifest its supreme efficacy.)
The Master of the Treatise says in verse: A single thought-moment of mind, the Buddhas of the ten directions— Picked up, it is this very thing;
Suddenly blown down, the peach blossoms are red. Fragrant rain falls in misty profusion, beyond measure.

(From the *Zhengbiao*: Thus far we have offered our invocation to the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vidyārājas, and Honored Deities. May each, by means of their majestic spiritual power, bestow grace upon us.
As we reverently recite the mantras without violating the ritual rules, this empowered pure water possesses great efficacy.
Now, with this pure water consecrated by mantra, I sprinkle it upon this site—both inside and outside the maṇḍala, throughout the central area and the four directions.
Wherever the water reaches, it shall all become a consecrated boundary (*sīmā*). One should then make this aspiration:

"May the offerings of incense, flowers, and food at this site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) arise one by one through the power of this [consecration], without limit. May those who practice the Dharma likewise receive the power of this [consecration]."

There was not a single sense organ or object that was not purified. By virtue of this power, there was not a single person among those attending to affairs whose body and mind was not radiant and clean.
Even reaching as far as beyond the boundaries, the bodies and robes of those who came and went were no longer unclean.

Should one consume pungent or garlicky foods, whether intentionally or by mistake, and thereby enter the *dharmadhātu* (place of practice), they shall be transformed into purity through the power of the mantra.
All malevolent spirits and those of the *icchantika* nature—who revile the Triple Gem and delight in creating obstacles—shall all give rise to the Bodhi-mind through the power of the mantra.
Whether praised or slandered, both serve as conditions for awakening; only when the mundane and the sacred are fused as one does [true realization occur].
For the sake of universal benefit (to assist in manifesting shared mindfulness), we further rely on the power of the assembly to recite the mantra together and sprinkle the Dharma-water everywhere.

(Strike the chime and ring the bell; at this time, after the small cups have been used to distribute the water, the altar keeper waits for the assembly to exit before locking the gate. He then waits for the assembly to return before unlocking the gate.)

(Namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva; recite three times. The Great Compassion Mantra is not limited by the number of recitations. (The two ritual masters perform the same inquiry of well-being. They exit their positions and proceed to the station before the Buddha. Together they present incense.

Each holds a small water cup and places a little sandalwood within it, sprinkling it for purification as they go. They exit through the lattice gate. One person leads the way, followed by the lamp-bearer, then the banner-bearer, then the incense-burner, then the small fish-shaped chime, then the ritual master holding the water, and finally the presiding master holding the incense burner.

Whenever they encounter a station for a Buddha, a Celestial Honored One, or a deity, the ritual master first performs an inquiry of well-being, and the presiding master performs it afterwards. After sprinkling for purification at each station one by one, they return.)
Inner Altar. (Ring the chime. Shake the bell.

(The Director of the Tableau holds the incense burner and says: Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Śākyamuni Tathāgata. (Bows down. (Rises. Opens. (Inquires after his well-being. Commences. (Ring the chime and shake the bell.)

(Homage states: I take refuge in the Teachers who Guide throughout the ten directions, who proclaim the pure and subtle Dharma, and the assembly of Sages and Worthies of the Three Vehicles and One Vehicle.

I pray that you grant compassion and graciously accept me. I look up to the Triple Gem, entreating them not to forsake their compassion, but to occupy the high seat of the Dharma assembly and bear witness to these merits.
Now, I offer this Right Dharma to construct for all beings of the Dharma-realm, both holy and ordinary, [altars] for those on water and land.

The Great Fast. The Universal Benefit Bodhimanda is now about to be opened. For those who intend to propagate [the Dharma], may you graciously grant clear discernment within the radiance of the Triple Gem.
(Kneel and recite the intent once; strike the chime, ring the bell, rise, and perform three prostrations.)

(The Master of the Dharma proclaims: "Since you have resolved upon the Great Mind, you shall together assist in this sublime undertaking. You must clarify the fundamental principle and bring the site of practice to fulfillment.

What is called the 'Dharmadhātu'? Upon the single Reality, it manifests in layers of profundity; phenomena and principle, phenomenon and phenomenon, and principle and principle are all mutually unimpeded."
Sentient beings emerge from this gate; though they pass through a thousand kalpas, they do not return. Yet within their fundamental station, they do not depart from a single thread.

The Great Compassionate Bodhisattva contemplates nature and characteristics, profoundly awakening to the subtle and the manifest. Within the light of a single thought, all things appear vividly and simultaneously.
They are neither sentient beings nor Buddhas; they are both existent and non-existent. Principle is fully present in wisdom, and the objective realm is fully present in the mind. Mind...
Because Buddhas and sentient beings are truly equal, what is meant by "sages" and "ordinary beings"? Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas are called the Four Sages.
Devas, humans, asuras, animals, hungry ghosts, and those in the hells are called the Six Ordinary Beings. When a sage enters among ordinary beings, they manifest as an ordinary being;
when an ordinary being enters among sages, they manifest as a sage. It is like the azure of autumn waters or the crimson of morning clouds.
Within equality, distinct reflections appear. What are "water and land"? These refer to the supporting environments (*niśraya-vipāka*) of the noble ones and ordinary beings.
Body and mind are the primary [subject], while the world is the support. There are six such loci of support: earth, water, fire, wind, space, and wood.
By means of "water and land," the remaining four are subsumed. The Noble Ones cannot be named; they abide in non-abiding, their compassionate minds manifesting as reflections.

This demonstrates that there is something upon which one relies. With the Buddha-eye observing universally, all noble ones and ordinary beings take non-reliance as their reliance, because the unobstructed realm does not hinder reliance.
What is meant by the "Great Fast" (*upoṣadha*)? At the hour of the Rabbit on the celestial calendar, it is the hour of the Horse in the human world.

The Buddha, in accordance with the ways of humans and devas, accepts offerings at the time of eating. That which occurs before the hour of the Rat or after the hour of the Horse is not called a fast. Ten.
At that time, all followed the Dharma of the fast. The reason for this was that all sentient beings abide by means of food.
Out of compassionate pity, the Sages manifest in the world and enter various places of practice (maṇḍalas) to demonstrate the acceptance of offerings.
Once the Buddhas have demonstrated their acceptance, the offerings of the Bodhisattvas arise; the assembly gathered from the ten directions appears like space, an inexhaustible multitude.
Clouds of multi-storied pavilions and the wondrous jewels of the six sense-objects serve as offerings.

For those who have resolved upon the Great Mind, through the power of contemplation, the power of mantras, and the powers of faith, precepts, and diligence, they perfectly respond to the Dharma-realm within a single thought-moment.
Thus, infinite and complete offerings can all be universally manifested within every single atom; while the single mind remains unmoving, a multitude of wonders are imbued with radiant splendor.
With precious moonstones and lapis lazuli, and nets of *muni* pearls, he offers these supreme gifts to both the holy and the ordinary, leaving not a single person behind.
Thus the Dharma assembly is perfectly completed; yet within the ritual of the vegetarian feast, no aspect of the practice is neglected. In essence, in form, and in function, all are great.

This constitutes the Great Fast. The minds of the assembly were unified as one, such that they could not distinguish Cunda from the Honored One who is uniquely worthy of offerings; for how could he be merely an Arhat?
Since the Buddhas of the ten directions have no *nirvāṇa*, and since the sages and ordinary beings of the three periods of time all partake in the same offering, what is meant by "universal benefit"?
It means that the sages mutually influence one another to produce wondrous seeds. Regarding the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*), compassion is held foremost. [The precepts...]

The marks are perfectly luminous; the light of the Dharma flows with moistening grace. Within this, there are instances of disparaging the partial and rejecting the small, extolling the Great, and praising the Perfect.
Nevertheless, every drop and every speck of hair returns to the Ocean Seal (Sāgarāmudrā). Transverse and longitudinal distinctions are entirely stilled, and equality manifests before one.

The sense organs and their objects dissolve away, transforming into a single flavor. When the limits of conceptual mind are exhausted, one enters freely into the True Thread. Ten mirrors reflect each other’s light.

It is not called a single virtue; it is auspicious and brings no disadvantage. This is the true *dharma-cakra* (place of practice). To fall into duality or to fall into triad is not the concern of today.

(Having finished speaking, the assembly exits the *dharma-cakra*. At this site of boundary-binding, celestial deities are densely arrayed; one should cultivate reverence and awe. When the matter is concluded, the gates are locked.)

Dispatching Messengers and Raising the Banner on the First Day at the Fifth Watch (The messengers' altar is established at the entrance of the gate. Six types of offerings are prepared: two tables; one for the ten spirit-tablets of the *khang-saṅ* (space-farers), and one for the ten spirit-tablets of the *gnam-saṅ* (sky-farers) and *sa-saṅ* (earth-farers) of the underworld.
A large banner is prepared in advance, complete with its pole and lamp, upon which the four characters "Water and Land Ritual Site" (*shui lu dao chang*) are inscribed).
(The Master of the Dharma arrives. He offers incense, inquires after the well-being [of the assembly], strikes the chime, and rings the bell.

(The Director of the Incense Burner says: "With a sincere heart, we take refuge in the Buddhas, Dharmas, and Sanghas of the ten directions and the entire Dharma-realm. (The assembly joins in: "To the eternally abiding Triple Gem" (no prostration;
simply inquire after their well-being, strike the chime, and ring the bell).
(As the assistant holds the incense burner: The fragrant smoke first rises; the mind attains wondrous penetration. Abiding nowhere within the three temporal limits, it pervades the ten directions.
Sentient beings receive its permeation here, and the Buddhas hear it and grant their protection. Anticipating supreme benefit, the secret mantra is recited once more.
(The Ritual Manual states: "Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses the Mantra for Communicating through Incense. I shall now reverently recite it. (Thereupon, burn incense and recite as follows.)
Oṃ śvalitadamanī aprakoṭa suparṇi vikacche huṃ. (The Dharma Master visualizes:
these clouds of incense fill the entire Dharmadhātu; all ordinary beings and sages alike perceive them and give rise to hearts of joy.)

(Using the *zhengbiao* vessel to pour out a small amount of water, place it upon the table, join the palms, and say: The precious vessel is filled to overflowing; the spiritual source is cleared and purified. Through the three secret additions, [the ritual is completed].

A single sprinkling brings refreshing coolness, augmenting the majestic adornment of light upon the seat; it unifies the quarters and directions in purity, distancing one from dust and departing from defilement.
It moves the sages and summons the worthy, reaching the brilliance of single-minded concentration and encompassing the entire dharma-realm of the ten directions.
(The Assistant says: Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for sprinkling purification.
I shall now reverently recite it: Oṃ vaśira śameye huṃ phaṭ śrīmahe svāhā.
(Strike the chime and ring the bell.)
(Perform the ritual sprinkling once. The Dharma Master visualizes that wherever the water reaches, it becomes a realm of solemn purity and radiance, thereby constituting the boundary.
(The Ritual Manual states: We humbly observe that the Buddha, King of Awakening, out of compassion for those who perform the *Yankou* rite, first commanded the offering of the *hu* (vessel).

Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty, moved by the dream of a divine monk, subsequently instituted the practice of performing vegetarian feasts (*zhai*). Although the names "Water" and "Land" were briefly established, this is in fact a universal offering to both the holy and the mundane.
The assembly: That is to say, they extend reverence toward the Triple Gem; when speaking of the myriad classes of beings, they give rise to compassion.

From the highest heavens to the lowest earth, there is nothing left out; how could there be any distinction between those realms and this domain? For all who dwell in different destinies, they manifest true cultivation.
Therefore, by relying on these matters through manifold rituals, they ensure that the great vow is successfully fulfilled. Now, we look up to and follow...
Regarding the Buddhist scriptures, I respectfully follow the sacred regulations to open this supreme assembly for the salvation of the deluded masses;

this task rests firmly upon the presiding master (to whom we express our shared devotion). To universally move the spirits throughout the Dharma-realm, one truly relies upon the messenger. Therefore, with sincere intent, I welcome you;
may you hear this call and arrive immediately (ringing the chime and shaking the bell).

(The Master presides over the incense burner. The two assistants chant in unison: With single-minded devotion, we respectfully invite the messengers who hold the talismans, whose supernatural powers are sovereign and whose majestic virtue is immeasurable, who traverse the void of the ten directions with swiftness, together with all their retinues.

We pray that you will not violate your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, grace this Dharma assembly on this very day and at this very hour. (Ring the chime and shake the bell.)

(The Master presides over the ritual fire. The two representatives chant in unison: With single-minded devotion, we respectfully invite those who possess sovereign supernormal powers and immeasurable majesty;
the swift-moving spirit-holders of talismans who travel through the heavens from this world and other realms; the swift-moving spirit-holders of talismans who travel upon the earth;
and the swift-moving spirit-holders of talismans of the underworld, together with all your retinues. We pray that you will not violate your original vows and take pity upon us.
[The Master] said: "At this very day and hour, you have graced this Dharma assembly" (the chime and bell are struck).

The Commentary states: Generally, when the spirits who are to be properly delivered according to their capacity appear, they do not reside in a fixed location, nor are they limited to a single individual.
Therefore, [the Master] descended from the hall with more than ten attendants, unified them under ten written instructions, and entrusted them to three messengers to harmonize [the proceedings].
This is thorough and definitive; there shall certainly be no omission or error.
(The Assistant’s Statement: The Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for invocation; I shall now reverently recite it.
Oṃ pūrvakāritā tathāgatāya. (Ring the bell and strike the chime. [The Dharma Master visualizes:
the messengers, each accompanied by hundreds of thousands of retinues, descend from the sky and take their places.]
(The *Zhengbiao* states: Clouds enshroud the banners and standards; the wind moves through the ranks. It seems as if [the envoy] has descended from the Nine Heavens, lingering amidst the four seats.
We hope that your radiant presence will pause for a moment, so that our sincere sentiments may be fully conveyed.

We respectfully contemplate the Envoy: self-strengthening without ceasing, attaining the One to become divine; when employed, his influence is manifold; majestic yet not fierce. With frost-like integrity, he possesses silent insight.

Having already woven the myriad regions with your wisdom, your noble steps have traveled far; you have galloped through hundreds of millions of shrines, diligently maintaining the awareness of one who respectfully offers these words, all the more so as you possess the talent for diplomatic missions.
Now, however, the holy and the mundane hold different thoughts, and the realms of the unseen and the manifest follow divergent paths.
Since it is not through borrowed spirits that one can achieve universal penetration, at this juncture we invoke all the deities.
Relying on your sagacity, you will surely be able to understand the full details. (Strike the chime and ring the bell.)
(The Auxiliary Explanatory Text states: This mind creates food; the entire food is nothing but mind. Because essence and function are not distinct, one attains mastery over contraction and expansion.
Thus, the six sense-objects mutually pervade one another, and the three virtues are eternally fused. Subtle and wondrous beyond thought, they give rise to the inexhaustible.
Relying on the methods of contemplation, one darkly accords with the influence of mantras. This shall lead the way for ritual practices, so that they may be perfectly accomplished.
Regarding this Dharma-offering: I now recite the *Aparimitāyur-jñāna-vaśitā-prabhāsa-viśeṣa-bala-dhāraṇī* to consecrate this Dharma-food, causing it to pervade everywhere.
Namo sarvatathāgatāvalokite | Oṃ | Prasara prasara hūṃ || (Recite fourteen times by the assembly.
At the conclusion of the mantra, strike the chime and ring the bell. Formally sprinkle the consecrated water upon the food.
The Dharma Master visualizes that this food produces all manner of sublime offerings, which are simultaneously presented in full abundance.)

(At the point of formally presenting the food, say: Exquisite incense wafts its fragrance; the water of samādhi is clear and still. The lamp of wisdom shines brightly, and the food of dhyāna-joy is complete.
The flower of causal practice has first blossomed, and the fruit of the true nature is already perfected. One who can contemplate thus is performing a Dharma-offering.
Then, proclaim the secret words to hasten the arrival of the spirits, granting them a brief moment of leisure to graciously partake.
Offering to our Buddha, the Tathāgata: There is a mantra for the presentation of offerings which I shall now reverently recite.
Oṃ gaganasvabhāva vajra hūṃ. (Ring the chime and shake the bell. [The Dharma Master visualizes:
May these presented offerings be fully sufficient and manifest; may all the deities partake of them, none failing to be filled with joy.]

(The Master of the Dharma vibrates the bell for a short while, then says: "The bodies of ordinary beings and sages are identical; it is only their minds—awakened or deluded—that differ. Now, as we perform this ritual of purification and extend our invitation, some may say that the responses to these entreaties are inconsistent.
Yet, regarding the abodes of the Triple Gem and the various devas, they can surely be reached in a single thought."
If one belongs to the various classes of animals or the intermediate states of existence, they may call out repeatedly yet remain unheard;

this is because those with heavy evil karma are beset by the obstacles of suffering, while those with much wrong view create their own hindrances—it is not a matter of relying on the agility of a messenger.

How can one communicate with the diligent efforts of those who practice giving? It must be through the single limit of empty spirituality, where the ten directions are not separated by even a hair’s breadth.

Thus, wondrous function may penetrate the divine, and the myriad transformations may be fully encompassed within the Dharma-realm. The radiant light of the highest grade of wholesome dharmas is simultaneously fused and unified;
while those bound by the karmic conditions of the lowest grade of faculties respond to their thoughts with opening and expansion, all are brought to fulfillment.

Rush forward; do not allow them to retreat. In this way, those among the devas, humans, and asuras, as well as the ranks of ghosts, animals, and those in the hells, shall borrow the merit of this single moment of crossing over to resolve the suffering of saṃsāra for billions of kalpas. Thus they shall greatly honor the supreme transformation and meet with this wondrous, auspicious condition.
I hope you will skillfully employ your intelligence and be able to perfectly fulfill what has been entrusted to you, without transgressing.
In an instant, they reach every sealed command. Those who understand the ritual respond with their whole hearts and surely arrive;

those who are confused by the text, the presiding leader summons them and they immediately appear. Whether in the distinct realms of the Buddha-lands and celestial palaces, each maintains its respective jurisdiction;
or in the divergent paths of the human world and the underworld, each fulfills its appointed duty. To those who are mired in torpor and lack discernment, they offer encouragement.

By means of the Way of Principle, those who are stubborn and dull-witted and do not awaken are gathered through majestic spiritual power; they shall all come in their full number, with not one failing to arrive.
All subtle intentions are fully set forth in the commentary; I command that it be separately recited and proclaimed—please deign to listen (strike the chime and ring the bell).

(The *zhengbiaoxian* for the ascent to the hall; the *zhubiaoxian* for the descent from the hall; the *zhengbiaoxian* for the notification to the *kōngxíng*; the *zhubiaoxian* for the notification to the *tiānxíng*, etc., completed in sequence).
The Treatise says: "The fourteen lower realms are included within the invitation, as are human beings. Why would humans invite? By what means would they invite?
If they were indeed able to invite, why are they not seen coming? If they truly do not come, what is the use of inviting them in vain?

To illustrate this by the ten lands (*kṣetra*): it is so for one land; it is so for every land. To illustrate this by the seven destinies (*gati*): it is so for one destiny; it is so for every destiny.
It is likewise so. If one understands this capacity [of the recipient], one may be free from regret; otherwise, one will have needlessly burdened the site of enlightenment (do-ch'ang).
(Zheng-biao says: I reverently contemplate the Messenger: internally cultivating the practices of a Bodhisattva, externally manifesting the body of a Divine King.

Clad in golden armor, he adds luster to the postal road; mounted upon a precious steed, the phoenix-bells ring out their resonance. Without being summoned, he arrives with speed; when there is a response, he appears.
Your majestic bearing is like the radiance of the rising sun, and your divine power is as robust as the movement of the heavens. It is fortunate that you have not abandoned your life;

you must skillfully compose your parting words. Though this matter involves much toil and fatigue, it is only right that we see you off. Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for seeing one off;
I shall now reverently recite it.
Oṃ māraya mukhya muḥ. (Ring the bell while striking the chime. [The *Zhengbiao* states: I take refuge in the Buddha;
I take refuge in the Dharma; I take refuge in the Saṅgha. Having completed the taking of refuge in the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha.

The preceding dispatch of the messenger and the completion of the prostrations are concluded. The ritual texts have been refined and funds raised to assist the messenger on his journey across the clouds, reaching throughout the entire realm of *sāhasra-lokadhātu*.
I pay homage to the assembly of saints. (Ring the chime and shake the bell. (Burn the ritual texts, the official documents, the spirit tablets, precious incense, paper, and silk.)

(The Dharma Master visualizes: The messengers receive their orders and immediately depart; there is no world throughout the ten directions they do not penetrate. ○ (At the location facing the banners, set up another altar complete with incense, candles, and offerings.)
(The Master of the Dharma proceeds to the altar of the banners. After one prostration of inquiry, he says: "The mission sent previously has completed its rites of homage.

Now, as we raise the precious banner, we first invite the Four Holy Ones to grace this occasion with their presence, and subsequently summon the Six Classes of Beings to attend this assembly. (Having finished hanging the banners.)

(The Ritual Master announces: "The hanging of the banners has been completed above. This is an immeasurable cause for goodness, its grace extending throughout the entire universe. I pay homage to the assembly of sages.
(The Ritual Master performs one inquiry of greeting. He turns his body and proceeds to the desk of the messenger, where he performs another inquiry of greeting, then returns to the inner altar.)
(The Master of the Dharma offers incense. The Ritual Director strikes the chime. The Master of the Dharma performs three prostrations. (The Ritual Director says:

"The mission of dispatching the messenger is completed; the banners are raised across the waters and lands. Grace encompasses the entire realm of space. I pay homage to the assembly of sages. (He bows in greeting and exits the altar.)

Inviting the Sage; Bathing the Sage (For the bathing, there is an altar. One carries the banner frame while proceeding. Two people protect one side of the frame. First, one person leads the way; next, the lamp; next, the banner; next, the incense burner; next, the ritual proclaimer; next, the frame; and finally, the presiding master).

Proceeding to the front of the altar, banners are displayed upon a table and the six offerings are arranged. Once the bathing is complete, the banners are supported and returned to the purification path to be reinstalled in their positions. There are two bathing pools, one at the front and one at the rear of the altar; outside the pools hang curtains with hooks and tassels, and the pools are filled with warm water.

Mix camphor, saffron, and sandalwood powder together. Place another basin filled with hot water within the pool, also mixed with these three substances. Inside the basin, place ten white cloths; outside the basin, ten blue cloths. Do the same for both pools. The cloths are over a foot long;

the basins are several inches in diameter; the pools are over a foot in diameter. The pools are constructed of wood, square in shape, and equipped with "flying chairs" (portable stands). There are separate frames for the canopies, which cover the exterior of the pools. Each pool is supported by a large table. For the purification path, use three pieces of new cloth.

This is placed inside the railing at the base of the inner altar steps, secured by crossbeams at both ends. The crossbeams have pillars at each end, which are buried in the ground. The banner-frames are placed upon the cloth. [This is done] for fear that...

It is unstable; place a cloth underneath and support it with a small table so that it does not shake. While there is no ritual for accompanying the position with a lamp-stand to escort [the image], it is not prohibited to have banners to welcome and escort the bathing ceremony, as this serves as a means for certain individuals with karmic affinity.
From this point on, the maturation through the refinement of light is indispensable.
The second day, at the fourth and fifth watches. The Treatise says:

The bathing pools are divided into two to distinguish between males and females. Their bodies possess radiance; as soon as these celestial beings, male and female, are born, they are already clever and intelligent.

This radiance envelops their bodies so that their forms are not exposed. They go by themselves to the clothing-trees to take garments. When they see one another, their physical appearance is fully perfected. Such supreme excellence does not equal even a ten-thousandth part of the Three Jewels. Their bodies are without...

Obstacles are manifested through the display of compassionate mind; possessing both majesty and decorum, they accord with the common path of both ordinary beings and sages, establishing a standard for all time—this is surely how it is.
When Danxia split the Buddha and Nanquan slew the cat, they had already entered the Great Sameness.

What prevents one from shattering views? Yet, the extraordinary is not extraordinary, and the ordinary is likewise not ordinary. Alas! How few are those who understand this! (The Dharma Master enters.

The表白 [ritual officiant] and the assembly chant in unison: With a sincere heart, we take refuge in the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm. (One prostration. Ring the chime. Shake the bell.)

(Properly representing the holding of the incense burner, he recites the verse: The source from which wondrous fragrance arises is itself without arising. Primordially devoid of substance, it is the very voidness of emptiness (*śūnyatā*). Pervading the great void, it forms clouds of fragrance;
without departing from the void, it manifests as wondrous conventionality (*prajñapti*). Neither existent nor empty, it is doubly free from dependence.

Neither completely obscuring nor completely illuminating—do not speak of "the middle" (not speaking of "the middle" is most excellent). Relying solely on the incense of a single thought of faith, perform the offering with diligent devotion according to the Dharma.
The Commentary says: The three contemplations are exceedingly rare and should not be used frequently; if one encounters them repeatedly, the flowers of the Buddha will wither.
Even when retaining only one or two instances of these, one must surely purge away all traces of the "smoke and fire" from within language.

One should know that the essence (*zong*) is the essence of the teaching (*jiao*), and the teaching is the teaching of the essence. Only by ensuring that not even a single thread of lingering flavor remains can one [attain this].
The true spirits are moved and inspired.
(The Ritual Manual states: Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for burning incense.
I shall now reverently recite it: Oṃ śvalla-damana-apratigha-suparṇi.
Vikāji. (The tiger [bellows] as the chime and bell vibrate).
(The Dharma Master visualizes clouds of incense filling the Buddha-fields of the ten directions; all the sages and worthies together protect and mind him.)
The Commentary says: At this point, one who applies their mind with focused attention truly distinguishes between life and death; it is not merely a matter of skill versus clumsiness.
Alas! If one should encounter a true knower, one must wait for them even at the cost of one's life.
(Main Inscription: Contemplating the mind, the waters of the Dharma merge; in a single thought, all defilements are purified. Both the primary and secondary realms are adorned with light;
throughout the ten directions, there is no obstruction. (Auxiliary Inscription: Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for sprinkling purification. I now reverently recite it.
Oṃ śavara śmāye huḥ phat śrīmahe svāhā. (Ring the bell and strike the chime. [Recite the prose offering while scattering flowers to purify the path.

Then sprinkle water to purify the path. The Dharma Master visualizes that wherever the water reaches, it becomes a consecrated boundary—vast, majestic, and pure, giving rise to clouds of radiant pavilions, layer upon layer, inexhaustible.]
