Flowers were spread upon the ground. Flying banners led the way, and sounding pendants followed behind. It was hoped that [the deities] would condescend to attend the site of practice (*dōjō*), so that the rites of the fast (*saiji*) might be solemnly accomplished.

(Strike the chime, ring the bell, draw back the curtains, offer incense, inquire after their well-being, and lead them back into the inner altar, settling them upon the pure path. (At this time, the positions of the presiding officials and the representatives all turn upward.)
(The *Zhengbiao* states: Now that the Sages and Worthies have arrived, we consider that the seats and mats have not yet been solemnly prepared.

Illuminating the subtle contemplation of the mind through the Middle Way, one realizes that the Dharma-nature has no abiding foundation. The entire body is fully manifested and arises in every thought-moment.
Lion thrones fill the void, and jeweled light-platforms pervade all lands; none are not lofty and vast, and all possess radiance. We look up with hope.
Out of compassion, please deign to accept this. The Tathāgata, our Buddha, possesses a mantra for offering the precious throne;
I now respectfully recite it: Oṃ kāmuka padma-sūnari dhara dharaṇi maṇḍa.
NARA HŪṂ (Ring the chime and shake the bell).
[The Dharma Master visualizes that the maṇḍala is vast, expansive, and pure; immeasurable jewel thrones fill the entirety of space, and all the sages and worthies dwell upon them.]

(Chanting the Auxiliary Verses: Faith arises from the mind; phenomena emerge following conditions. This vital energy is neither wood nor space; manifest before us, it is both concentration and wisdom.
Like clouds encompassing ten billion pavilions, its canopy covers the three thousandfold world-system. This golden light shines universally upon the precious royal throne.
Through this modest offering, may our sincere devotion reach You. We recite the sacred texts with spiritual resonance.
This further serves as an excellent support for practice. Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for burning incense; I shall now reverently recite it:
Oṃ akara akara sarvabuddhādhyeṣaṇīye svāhā. (Sound the chime and ring the bell.)

(The Dharma Master visualizes these clouds of incense as producing immeasurable palaces of the seven treasures, ritual implements, clothing, exquisite music, sublime fragrances, and ambrosial delicacies, which he offers one by one before all the sages and worthies, pervading them all without exception.)
(The *Zhengbiao* states: Only when all the eminent flowers bloom together can they serve as the adornment of the myriad practices.
Therefore, faith and understanding establish the roots, while diligence causes the branches and leaves to flourish.

Having moistened them with the water of meditative concentration and fanned them with the wind of wisdom, one intends to manifest the forest of boundless merit; thus, this serves as a representation of what accords with thought.
Regarding the sign of full blooming: I, [Name], shall now reverently recite the Flower Offering Mantra of our Buddha, the Tathāgata.
Oṃ akara akara sarvabuddhādhipataye svāhā. (Ring the chime and shake the bell. This is done twice for each seat in the upper hall; once the recitation is finished, flowers are scattered.)

(The Dharma Master visualizes the flowers he offers as giving rise to palaces of the seven treasures, exquisite necklaces and robes, celestial music, wonderful incense, and ambrosial delicacies—various articles of offering, layered and inexhaustible. He presents these offerings simultaneously before each of the sages and worthies, such that none are left unattended.)

(The assistant states: A single drop suffices to pervade the Dharma-realm; a mote of dust already purifies the finest hair. Borrowing from this precious moisture and luminous clarity of space to manifest the purity of the true mind:
the sages of antiquity were originally free from defiled habits, and at this site of enlightenment, one further draws in their pure fragrance.
It is not that things hinder the illumination of the inner heart; through self-awakening and the forgetting of emotions, one enters the wondrous. My Buddha, the Tathāgata...
There is a purification mantra which I shall now reverently recite:
OṂ VAŚRA ŚĀMAYE HŪṂ PHAṬ ŚRĪMAHE SVĀHĀ. (Ring the chime. Shake the bell.
Holding water with both hands, sprinkle it over the various seats in the upper hall.)
(The Dharma Master visualizes that water reaches each and every seat; among all the offerings, there is nothing that is not pure and bright. (The Ritual Text states:
We respectfully invite the Triple Gem and have assembled all the devas. Having already taken their places within the *bodhimaṇḍa*, they shall bear witness to this rite of fasting.

It is necessary to rely upon this written petition to convey our sincere devotion. Facing you with reverence, we lay it before you; we pray that you will deign to grant us your attention. (The Presiding Master...)

Both the presiding *biao* (representative) and the assistant kneel. The presiding *biao* proclaims the intent. When finished, the *qing* gong is struck and the bell is rung; they rise. (The assistant *biao* says:
"We look up and offer ourselves to the Honored Realm, briefly revealing our humble sincerity. We trust that in Your Great Compassion, You will be able to forgive the multitude of our transgressions.

We pray that You will grant our request for the offering of our hearts, hoping to fulfill Your resolve for vast salvation. Only those whose merit and wisdom are somewhat weak still fear that [they have not yet...]”
If even those who have heard [the Dharma] find it so difficult, how much more so for those whose transgressions are extremely grave? By what means can they possibly arrive?

I pray that the Brahma King be requested to grant a general amnesty, and that Śakra Devendra be entreated to bestow his grace. Let swift and agile messengers be dispatched, each entrusted with the task of proclaiming this message.

May all beings throughout the seven realms of existence assemble at once. Those who lay down their butcher’s knives shall not fail in their destined time for attaining Buddhahood; let them emerge from the Avīci Hell.
Those who were early transformed belong to the assembly of the Golden Wheel. The celestial beings of the clam-light are radiant and clear;
the dragons of virtuous excellence possess towering merit. If one truly stirs the causal conditions, one will surely achieve the fulfillment of auspicious fortune.
How much more so when the Tathāgatas of the ten directions sit together at the site of enlightenment—how could all sentient beings not receive liberation? One should know that the flow of sound...
This is the light fully emitted from the Tathāgata’s white tuft of hair. Its proclamation and distribution mark the day when the original nature of all sentient beings returns to its source.

We venture to pray that Your Majesty, in Your majestic gravity, will condescend to accord with the capacities of beings; without distinction between inner, outer, or center, You shall directly cause the holy and the mundane to reach a single limit.
Through layer upon layer of transformations, You summon the multitudes of spirits, so that the subtle and true essence may be perfected like jade.
Jiàhuì (Sound the *qìng* stone. Ring the bell. [All] perform three prostrations together. Exchange greetings. Exit. Lock the gates).
*Treatise on the Commonality of Nature in the Ritual Altar for the Universal Salvation of the Holy and the Profane of the Dharma Realm through the Great Water-Land Feast*, Scroll Three.
*Treatise on the Commonality of Nature in the Ritual Altar for the Universal Salvation of the Holy and the Profane of the Dharma Realm through the Great Water-Land Feast*, Scroll Four.
Offering to the Hall by Zheng Yingfang of Zhiguan for the Practitioner of Pure Deeds (including offerings for the general assembly).

On the third day, at the fourth watch: (In advance, prepare offerings for eleven seats, as well as one offering for the general assembly; each consists of one incense burner and two lamps, ten servings of tea and ten servings of rice, one large vegetable dish, one [dish of] *tu*, and one [dish of] *yī*.)

One incense stick, one flower, one fruit, one dharma-treasure, and one small meal—these constitute the six items. Ten pieces of paper-treasure and ten silk brocades are provided; the same applies to the general seating mats. There are ten large vegetable dishes, and within each plate is a dharma-treasure, fashioned as a small scroll.

(The Master of the Dharma takes up the incense burner and makes this invocation: With a sincere heart, I take refuge in the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm. (One prostration. Ring the chime and shake the bell.
(At this time, all the ritual implements are arranged in their proper places; the Master of the Dharma inspects them.)

(The *Zhengbiao* says: Food is this very food; the mind is this very mind. It does not say that all phenomena are eternally fused, for originally the six sense objects have mutually pervaded one another.

This is the supreme flavor beyond clarified butter (*ghṛta*), the flowing fragrance of sandalwood, the resonant tinkling of the seven treasures, and the radiant blossoming of the four flowers. It encompasses the palaces of radiant light and manifests the most sublime...
Litters and carriages move about; celestial music resounds through the void, with the sounds of flutes and pipes playing in leisurely harmony.
Celestial robes are seamless, and pearl necklaces hang down in adornment. Because every thought-moment is complete and without deficiency, these various manifestations of splendor are inexhaustible.
Within this very site of practice (*bodhimaṇḍa*), the ritual observances are brilliantly numerous; thus, there are pure waters, bright lamps, and hanging banners raised aloft.
Indeed, the sound of the golden chimes vibrates through the secluded valleys, and the resonance of the *brahman* chants reaches the highest heavens;
all enter this school, for they are fundamentally nothing other than this. As for realizing the wondrous Dharma right before one’s eyes and contemplating the permanence of worldly phenomena:
the chirping of magpies and the cawing of crows are all profound discourses on *prajñā*; the mountain waters and landscape colors are none other than the complete manifestation of Vairocana.
Throughout past and present, the self-nature spirit remains unclouded; encompassing both the environment and its inhabitants, all become offerings of Dharma.
Herein, I employ a subtle offering of a single mind and uphold the supreme secret mantra, hoping to rely upon the power of manifesting the hidden and thereby express the intent of equal permeation.
Now I recite: *The Dharani of Immeasurable Majestic Virtue, Sovereign Radiance, and Supreme Wondrous Power*.
Nuns, empower the ritual food so that it pervades everywhere (ring the great fish-bell; the assembly recites together twenty-one times):
*Namo sarvatathāgatebhyo vairocaniye oṃ sambhara sambhara hūṃ* (ring the chime and shake the bell).
(The Auxiliary Tablet says: The Sūtra states: "If one wishes to make offerings to the Triple Gem, one should empower incense, flowers, food, and drink twenty-one times;
they will then become celestial delicacies of supreme flavor. To present these to the Triple Gem is to fulfill the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*).
[The second tablet: sprinkle water over the food, ensuring it reaches every part]."

(The Dharma Master visualizes this pure food as arising in various forms of supreme nectar, celestial delicacies, and all manner of offering implements in precious colors. The six sense objects pervade one another, encompassing all in perfect harmony.

He deeply understands that both the primary and secondary adornments—all phenomena—are, when viewed through wondrous contemplation, entirely offerings of the Dharma. Thus he universally presents them to the Triple Gem, the celestial immortals, and all holy sages, so that none remain unsatisfied.)

(Commentary: The Sage does not abide by means of food; rather, conditions serve as the support for the mind. When this mind is integrated, food is likewise integrated. Where the Dharma is equal, food is also equal.
It enters the three periods of time yet remains eternally present; it encompasses the ten voids and is perpetually pervasive.
This constitutes the single source of awakening; ultimately, both are named the *dharmadhātu*. Out of sincere compassion for the sentient beings of the ten directions, I speak thus for their benefit.
For the sake of seeking the Way, one employs one’s internal body and external wealth within the Dharma-realm, maintaining a heart of truthfulness to practice giving and relinquishment.
Yet, encountering non-Buddhists, wicked people, commoners, or various ghosts, these may secretly and deceitfully receive [offerings] and lead one onto deviant paths.
Beings remain unaware, conceiving the thought that they are fields of merit; thus, for many kalpas, they do not escape saṃsāra. Now, I— [The remainder of the text follows this introduction.]
[Recite] "etc. Universally representing all sentient beings of the ten directions, we abandon delusion to return to the truth. With single-minded sincerity, we offer this grand assembly;
we reverently serve the Compassionate Honored One, venturing to express our devotion as donors and emulating the offering of Cunda. (Chant the main liturgy with shared mindfulness.

Greatly compassionate and pitying all beings, you hold your great vows in your heart. For the sake of delivering sentient beings, you manifest the acceptance of this food. (Strike the chime and ring the bell.)

(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this pure and magnificent worship to Vairocana, who manifests throughout the ten directions within the infinitely layered oceans of lotus-worlds.

To all Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, together with their retinues—those who pervade the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm across the three periods of time, possessing the spiritual marks of the ten bodies—we pray that you will not disregard your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, [accept these offerings].
On this day, at this hour, we receive this offering. (Ring the chime. Shake the bell. One prostration. (The Ritual Master says:
With single-minded devotion, we offer this worship to the Great Vaipulya Sutra of the Buddha, the *Avataṃsaka*, and to Mañjuśrī’s Fundamental Wisdom which manifests throughout the ten directions;
to the teachings of the One Vehicle, both common and uncommon; and to the teachings of the Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna, as well as the teachings of the vehicles of humans and devas. Relying upon...

The True Dharma is being expounded: the Sūtras emerge from the void of phenomena; the Vinaya, Śāstras, and Dhāraṇīs, along with the gates of provisional and ultimate truth, are profound and inexhaustible, pervading all of space and the entire Dharma-realm.

All the oceans of the True Wheel of Dharma throughout the three periods of time, together with their respective retinues—may you not disregard your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, accept this offering on this very day and at this very hour. (Ring the chime and shake the bell.)
(One prostration.
(The Master of Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we make offerings to the manifestation of Samantabhadra’s practices throughout the Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean.
Within this, the Perfect and Sudden One Vehicle, the Gradual Mahāyāna, and the sheep, deer, and small vehicles are all fully present at every stage of the holy path.
Worthy Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas— layer upon layer, inexhaustible, pervading all of space and the entire Dharma-realm,
including all Saṃgha-jewels of the three periods of time and their respective retinues— I pray that you will not violate your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings,
accept this offering on this very day and at this very hour. (Strike the chime, ring the bell, and perform one prostration.)

(The Presiding Master says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this worship to the Flower Garland Ocean of Nature, which reflects throughout the ten directions in infinite layers, pervading all of space and the Dharma-realm.
To all those of the three periods of time, the patriarchs of the ten schools, and the great spiritual friends, together with their respective retinues:
we pray that you will not disregard your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, accept these offerings on this very day and at this very hour.
(Sound the chime. Ring the bell. One prostration.

(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we make this offering: within the center of the Flower Treasury World, amidst a great lotus flower, in the Land of Peace and Bliss across thirteen lands as numerous as motes of dust, may those of the three grades and nine ranks be reborn according to the teachings;
may they attain the stage of non-retrogression (*avaivartika*) and become those who will attain Buddhahood in their next life (*ekajātipratibaddha*). Each...
Together with your retinues, we pray that you will not violate your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, accept this offering on this very day and at this very hour.
(Ring the chime, shake the bell, and perform one prostration.)

(The Ritual Master says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this worship to the Flower Adornment Ocean of Nature, which reflects throughout the ten directions and enters the Buddha’s knowledge and vision.
To all the Wondrously Adorned World Rulers of the three periods of time, together with their respective retinues:

we pray that you will not violate your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, accept these offerings on this very day and at this very hour. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell. One prostration.)

(The Ritual Master says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this worship to the Flower Ornament’s Ocean of Nature, which reflects throughout the ten directions and enters the Buddha’s knowledge and vision.

We pray that all the realized sages of the three periods of time, together with their respective retinues, will not fail their original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, accept this offering on this day and at this hour. (Strike the chime, ring the bell, and perform one prostration.)
(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this worship to the Flower Adornment Ocean of Nature, which manifests throughout the ten directions;

where principle and phenomena are darkly interfused, and the mind is free from obstruction. To all the supreme masters of Confucianism of the three periods of time, together with their respective retinues:

we pray that you will not disregard your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, accept these offerings on this day and at this hour. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell. One prostration.)

(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this service to the Flower Ornament Sea of Nature, which reflects throughout the ten directions all the Great Vidyārājas, celestial generals, and the Great Benevolent Goddess, together with their respective retinues.

We pray that you will not fail your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, accept this offering on this very day and at this very hour. (Ring the chime, shake the bell, and perform one prostration.)

(The Ritual Master says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this worship to the Flower Ornament (Avataṃsaka) Ocean of Nature, which reflects throughout the ten directions all the various sites of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) of the three periods of time.
To the assembly of Great Divine Kings who provide secret protection, together with their respective retinues:

we pray that you do not violate your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, accept these offerings on this very day and at this very hour. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell. One prostration.)
(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we present these offerings to the fundamental masters of the Water and Land rites, who universally benefit both the holy and the ordinary.
To all the Great Spiritual Friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) of the three periods of time, together with their retinues:

we pray that you will not forsake your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, accept these offerings this very day and at this very hour. (Strike the chime; ring the bell; perform one prostration. ○ (At this time, all items are displayed, complete and without deficiency.)

The Treatise says: Some may wonder why humans and devas enter the Small Vehicle (Hīnayāna), making it unnecessary to describe them in such detail. The answer is: this site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) encompasses the six realms of existence;
by means of human and celestial forms, beings from the ten realms are gathered into the assembly of the Tathāgata. Therefore, regarding humans and devas, one cannot be too brief.
Others may wonder that monks do not prostrate to devas, yet here we perform individual bows, invitations, and offerings; is this not merely a provisional method (upāya-dharma)?

If one were to treat them as permanent, it would destroy the characteristics of the teaching; this is not permissible. Answer: Those such as heaven and earth, rulers, and parents—whom some do not worship—are the "monks with signs" (*saṃjñika-saṃgha*) whom they revere.
Dragons, seers, spirits, and sages—whom others may worship—are the "monks of ultimate meaning" (*paramārtha-saṃgha*) whom I revere.
Now, those Bodhisattvas of the ten stages who occupy specific positions are "permanent," while the supreme Tathāgatas who manifest according to the capacities of beings are likewise [permanent].

The transformations pervade the vast and expansive Dharma-realm, equally benefiting all sentient beings. While distinctions of high and low are established according to rank and status, it is not necessary that the flowering beard produce knots.
Regarding all the oceans of wheels, the Dharma is applied in accordance with the capacities of those who encounter it; those who leave behind traces of mud are certainly not vessels for it.
(The Ritual Manual states: "Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for making offerings.
I shall now reverently recite it: Oṃ gaganasvabhāvaśuddhe hūṃ. (Strike the chime and ring the bell.

[The Dharma Master visualizes all the holy sages receiving these offerings, all of whom give rise to sympathetic joy and together bestow their protective mindfulness. (The six offerings: incense, flowers, fruit, ointment, light food, and the Dharma Jewel.)

(The assistant recites: "May it be through the secret and inconceivable perfuming that all subtle offerings are transformed into the wondrous Dharma, universally presented to all the sages and worthies without exception.
We take refuge and reverently prostrate. (Strike the chime, ring the bell, and perform one prostration.)

(The *Zhengbiao* states: "Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for offering incense. We shall now reverently recite it. (When offering incense at the general assembly, one recites the mantra.
○ (Whenever making an offering, one specifically holds it aloft with both hands upon the general seating area; this is merely to manifest respect.)
Oṃ sarvatathāgata dhūpa vyūha saṃmudrā spharaṇa samaye hūṃ. (Ring the bell and strike the chime;
the Dharma Master visualizes clouds of incense pervading before each of the holy ones.)
(The assistant says: "The Buddha Tathāgata has a mantra for offering flowers. I shall now reverently recite it. (At the general offering seat for the flower offering, one then recites the mantra.)
Oṃ sarvatathāgata puṣpa pūjāṅga samudra spharaṇa samaye hūṃ. (Strike the chime and ring the bell;
the Dharma Master visualizes clouds of flowers pervading before each of the holy ones.)

(The *Zhengbiao* states: "Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for offering lamps. I shall now respectfully recite it. (When offering lamps at the altar of universal offerings, one recites the mantra.
This applies when there are small lamps at each position on a square altar; it refers specifically to the occasion of changing the wicks.)
Oṃ sarvatathāgata-nīpa-bhuja-miṅga-samudra-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ. (Ring the chime and shake the bell;
the Dharma Master visualizes clouds of lamps filling before each of the holy ones.)

(The Assistant says: Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses mantras for offering food and offering robes. I shall now respectfully recite them. (When offering rice and paper silk, one recites the mantra upon the general offering table.
○ (The paper silk is divided into ten portions for the general seating; each individual portion is offered in this manner. During the universal offering, there are [mantras] for every seat.)
Oṃ sarvatathāgatānurāgaṇarucirasamādhibhāvana-bandhana-pūjana-prokṣaṇa-sammudrā-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ.
(Sound the chimes and ring the bells).
(The Dharma Master visualizes various garments, foods, drinks, teas, and fruits, as vast as clouds, pervading everywhere and appearing in full before all the sages and worthies.)
(The *Zhengbiao* states: "Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses the Mantra for Offering Treasures. We shall now reverently recite it. (Offer one portion each of gold, silver, and precious gems;
place the silk on the left and the coins and jewels on the right. Furthermore, offer one of each of the Dharma-jewels.)
Oṃ sarvatathāgata-mahāpāśur-udvartana-pāramitā-bhuja-miṅga-samudra-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ.
(Strike the chime and ring the bell.)
(The Dharma Master visualizes clouds of jewel-colored light pervading before all the sages and worthies. ○ (This is one small tray of the Dharma Jewel; together with the six small trays.)

(The Master of the Dharma said: "With a mind that aspires to vast salvation, one gives rise to the resolve for great compassion. Without the offering of the Dharma, how could one express the aspirations of the heart?
If one takes up the sublime and wondrous sutras of the Tathāgata to reveal their meaning to sentient beings, one must not slight those who are beginners;

rather, one should teach them solely by means of the One Vehicle. Consider this: at the moment of seeing the seeing, what is the appearance of each and every dharma? Has the conceptualization of the emotional intellect been shattered yet?"
The realization of the entire Dharma-realm is not yet perfected; it must await that single moment of resonance.

Only when all manifold discourses are simultaneously set aside can subtle words and coarse speech alike return to the One Vehicle. Then all insentient things possess Buddha-nature, and all become Tathāgatas.
Taking the Buddha’s own mind as one’s own mind, and daring to take the measure of the Dharma as one’s own measure—this is the truly wondrous offering, which is itself right Bodhi.
(The Master and the two attendants, before the Three Jewels, concentrate their spirits and form the mudrā of meditative concentration; pause briefly.)
(The *Zhengbiao* states: "Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for the Dharma-offering (*dharmapūjā*). I shall now reverently recite it. (The Dharma Master maintains the *dhyāna-mudrā*.
The two [officiants] recite the mantra together. Upon the completion of the third round, the Dharma Master extends both hands and rings the bell to seal the rite.)
Oṃ sarvatathāgata-avahiyā mahāparipūri-pratimad-bhuja-miṅga-samudra-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ.
(Strike the chime and ring the bell.)

(The Dharma Master contemplates that all previously offered offerings are non-contrary to the Dharma-offering (*dharmapūjā*). Even all six sense objects, the phenomena of both the noble and the ordinary, and all superior or inferior practices, together constitute the Dharma-offering. It is neither one nor many; it is entirely my own mind. Since the Dharma does not depart from the mind, the mind itself serves as the offering.
When one forms this contemplation, the sages and worthies of the ten directions will all rejoice.)
(The Master of the Dharma said: "I reflect that our Buddha takes the mind as his fundamental principle. Possessing but one firm and dense body, he manifests within every single atom.

Originally arising from the Dharmakāya and Sambhogakāya, the traces of his transformation then emerge. What sentient beings perceive differs, and the manifestations of the Dharma assemblies vary according to tradition;
yet in reality, there is only this one truth, and the other two are not real. It is simply thus for each and every one..."

All capacities and conditions alike tend toward perfect enlightenment; therefore, among the provisional and ultimate teachings and scriptures, there is not a single one that is not a member of the *Avataṃsaka* family.
Whether it be empty space or a mote of dust, all fully contain the wondrous verses; whether it be sound or the ear, both proclaim the perfect voice.
While names, phrases, and syllables are indeed the means by which the Dharma is expressed, the Vinaya, Abhidharma, and mantras are simply the functional extensions of the Sūtras.
The Dharma contains not a single word; therefore, it is the True Teaching. The mind contains not a single thing; therefore, it is the True Offering.

Now, for the sake of benefiting sentient beings and propagating the Dharma, this assembly has been convened and a vegetarian feast prepared. It is intended to awaken hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of beings to the capacity for entering the Buddha-way.
First, offerings symbolizing the Dharma—incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, and fruits—are spread forth. Now, we receive this through the power of your compassionate virtue.
The offerings in the netherworld follow many rites; having opened the heart for vast salvation, may you surely fulfill your lifelong aspirations.

We pray that all the Sages will together exercise their compassionate minds, so that you may sit peacefully within the *maṇḍala* and await the perfect completion of this Dharma service. (Strike the chime and ring the bell.)
(The Principal Representative kneels and reads the intent of the petition. The Assistant Representative kneels and finishes reading the memorial.
(The Ritual Master kneels and says: "The aforementioned Water and Land Ritual Assembly has completed one full cycle of the Dharma service.
All resulting merit is hereby dedicated to all sentient beings. May all sentient beings quickly awaken their perfect faculties and quickly hear the wondrous [Dharma]."
The Dharma purifies body and mind; day and night it is luminous. Enemies and karmic creditors vanish; one’s kin and followers become harmonious. Spiritual powers are swift;
the lineage of the Dharma is peaceful and stable. All vows are fulfilled; all undertakings are accomplished. One flies to the Land of Ultimate Bliss and joyfully beholds Amitābha.
For anyone who directs even a single thought of faith toward the Buddha, there shall be no suffering or distress; they will proceed directly upon the broad highway.
Whenever one gives rise to practice and cultivation, they fully uphold the central point and do not fall into extremes.
Whenever a single matter triggers the mechanism for defending the Way, a true *kalyāṇamitra* appears before them, so that they do not encounter demons or heterodoxies.

Whenever a single condition coincidentally enters into principle, the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power protects their life, ensuring they will certainly achieve perfect realization. For the sake of the multitude, I—
Life draws forth thread after thread into the resonance. Sentient beings rely upon me; I melt all phenomena into radiant transformation.
If there is anything they seek, I vow to fulfill it through skillful means so that their cultivation may be expedited. If there is anything they perceive...
I shall open them all with compassion and rectitude to lead them back to the correct path. I shall serve as a model for all spirits, bringing them to the same wisdom and vision as the Buddha.
Each shall manifest the principle of dependent origination, and all shall be made to return to the source. Upon those without conditions, I first establish universal conditions;
upon those with weak conditions, I create superior conditions; upon those with hidden conditions, I reveal manifest conditions; and upon those with conditions of suffering—
I act as a condition for the transformation of their happiness. For those who are distant, I lead them into the profound conditions;
for those who are false, I suddenly break through them with true conditions. At all times, in all places, regarding all wealth and all dharmas, I associate with them without suspicion;
I exhort and warn them without leaving a trace; and I serve as their companion.
Yet they do not realize this; they merely give rise to joy. I establish rules for them all, and they do not transgress them;
over time, these become natural. I attend to their every need and offer them comfort, yet their habitual tendencies remain unbroken.
I shift them by means of the two conditions of rigidity and flexibility. Because the root of craving is difficult to uproot, I stir it by means of the two impulses of adversity and favor.

They fall away. If one develops even a single thought of reverence toward the True Dharma, or a single thought of affection for false practices, or performs a single act of offering to celestial deities, or seeks refuge in demons or heretics, the mind-ground remains unclarified.
Hastily coming and going, I have vainly borne good intentions while sinking deeply into evil retributions. Now, by the power of my offerings to the Buddhas,
Dharma, Sangha, and the immeasurable sages and worthies, may I suddenly possess the numinous roots and be able to respond perfectly and completely to such and such sentient beings—
regarding their initial matters, subsequent matters, difficult circumstances, and dreams— with certainty.
In the midst, he manifests as a ripening condition, skillfully expounding the Dharma to fully realize that which is difficult to express, and courageously bestowing the grace of fearlessness.
May the essence of *amṛta* enter the heart, may the nectar of immortality be poured upon the crown, may celestial robes fit the body, and may the jeweled mirror appear in the sky.

We pray that the Triple Gem of Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, as well as the celestial beings, *devas*, *yakṣas*, and *nāgas*, will comprehend the minds of sentient beings and fulfill today’s vow. Whatever is thus contemplated...

May all sentient beings be enabled to cross over. Joyfully following rather than rushing toward [the world], when delusion is exhausted and the truth is fully realized, at the end of this single lifetime, they shall certainly be born in the Pure Land.
Should there be sentient beings who wish to be born in the Pure Land in the same year, month, day, and hour as I, they shall surely obtain their wish;
they shall surely obtain their wish. Within the mirror of empty luminosity, the wondrous emerges from *Sahā*.
Within the light of compassion, the Dharma-realm is perfectly realized. (Strike the chime; ring the bell; withdraw. Requesting forgiveness:
(The altar remains in its original position; the six offerings are without error. Set up ten tablets, all occupying a single station.)

On the third day, at the fifth watch (the presiding Dharma Master arrives at the altar. The Ritual Official holding the incense burner says): With a sincere heart, we take refuge in the Buddhas, Dharmas, and Sanghas of the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm. (The assembly joins in:
To the eternally abiding Triple Gem. (Do not prostrate; simply inquire after their well-being, strike the *qing*, and ring the bell.)

(As the assistant represents holding the incense burner: Dharma arises from the mind; truly, we rely upon incense to facilitate its passage. Its fragrance is so exquisite that it can reach throughout the ten voids.
A single pellet is burned, yet it already encompasses all wonders. Those with the divine eye see it as golden; the Buddha’s crown takes it as a canopy of clouds.
In an instant it ascends to the heavens; in a moment it pervades the entire realm.
(The *Zhengbiao* states: "Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses the mantra for conveying sincerity by burning incense.
I shall now reverently recite it: Oṃ śvalītamani aparokṣa suparāṇi vikāci huṃ.
(Burn the incense, strike the chime, and ring the bell.)

(The Dharma Master visualizes this cloud of incense pervading all lands and the palaces of the great devas, extending throughout the entire dharma-realm; the hearts of the sages rejoice, and the sufferings of sentient beings cease.)
(Place a small cup of pure water on the table. Joining the palms, say: The nectar of the heavens, the foremost in coolness; the supreme cream beyond the realms, boundlessly moistening and refreshing.
By means of these empowered secret words, I sprinkle it upon this true altar. May it increase the pure radiance of this seat and dispel the turbid vapors of the quarters.
Free from all defilement, it reaches the divine spirits. Deeply still, the mirror of the mind becomes perfectly encompassing.
How solemn! The numinous pearl radiates in four directions.

(Assistant’s Statement: Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for sprinkling purification. I shall now reverently recite it. (While performing one circuit of the sprinkling purification, recite while sprinkling.)
Oṃ vaśira śāmye hūṃ phaṭ śrīmahe svāhā. (Strike the chime and ring the bell.)
(The Dharma Master visualizes that wherever the water reaches, it becomes a consecrated boundary (*sīmābandha*), pure, radiant, and majestic.

(Official Inscription: The assembly has opened this unrestricted gathering, bringing together the ordinary and the sacred from the ten directions. Its awe-inspiring spirit is manifest, extinguishing the transgressions and faults of the nine realms.
Having thoroughly cleansed the heart, belly, kidneys, and intestines of the sovereign, all beings are now collectively liberated from the three realms of existence (*tridhātu*).
Once the shackles of prohibitions and fetters are cast off, and the constraints of formlessness are released, the burdens of physicality will surely be eliminated.
With the One Buddha alone as the object of veneration, the response of all the devas is certain; the efficacy of the inner altar’s practices relies entirely upon the light of the mind.

When external affairs reach their full completion, they must rely upon spiritual power (to assist in manifesting shared intention). One knocks at the celestial gate to issue the proclamation and exhausts the entire Dharma-realm to bestow grace.
Relying on this majestic divinity, one penetrates through all mundane lands and buddha-fields.

(As the Master holds the incense burner, he makes the invocation: With single-minded devotion, we reverently invite you: those with supernormal powers acting as they wish, whose wondrous virtue is immeasurable;
the Brahmās, Śakras, and other devas from this realm and other directions; and the swift messengers who carry talismans, together with all your retinues.
We pray that you will not fail your original vows, but out of compassion for sentient beings, grace this Dharma assembly at this very day and hour. (Ring the chime and shake the bell.)
(The assistant says: "The Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for summoning and invitation.
I shall now reverently recite it: Oṃ bhūri-karitari tathāgatāya. (Strike the chime and ring the bell.
(The Dharma Master visualizes: "The messengers, each accompanied by hundreds of thousands of retinues, arrive from the void and take their positions according to rank."
(From the *Zhengbiao*): Banners flutter in the heavens; jingling ornaments ring amidst the clouds. Radiant like moon-lamps shining forth, brilliant as star-standards coming and going.
We pray that you will pause your radiant form to grant us your full instructions. We respectfully consider the Envoy: your majesty follows divine transformation;
your vigor accords with the movement of Heaven. You survey the billions of mountains and rivers within a single mote of dust, and traverse the infinite.
Throughout the trichiliocosm, body and speech are unimpeded, and the mirror of the mind is perfectly round.

Now, as manifold sufferings are about to be dispelled and wondrous grace is about to flow forth, if one does not rely on the sublime function of the summoned deity, who can transmit the spiritual cause of the Dharma-lineage?

We respectfully invoke the honored spirit to descend upon this altar; being singular in intelligence and clarity, how could the resonance be difficult to achieve? (Strike the chime and ring the bell.)
(The Auxiliary Inscription states: The Spirit has no craving; even food is for the sake of Heaven. According to the needs of all classes of beings, to serve the Holy Spirit is filial piety.
A single meal encompasses the four types of nutriment; the myriad minds are wondrously manifested within this one mind.
Through secret empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*), they arise inexhaustibly. Now I uphold and recite this immeasurable, majestic, sovereign, radiant, and sublime [mantra].
The *Bala-dhāraṇī*. May this food of the Dharma be made complete and all-pervading.
*Namo sarvatathāgatānāṃ vairocaniye | Oṃ | Sampara sampara hūṃ* (Recite fourteen times together with the assembly.
Ring the chime and shake the bell. Properly sprinkle the consecrated water upon the food.)
(Visualize as follows: This food produces all manner of wondrous offerings which are presented simultaneously, pervading everywhere without exception.

(The formal declaration for offering the food is as follows: First, the water of the fundamental nature is clarified; momentarily, the incense of the mind is ignited. We light the lamp of radiant wisdom and present the flavors of *sūkhāra*—the essence of meditative joy.
Wondrous flowers bloom in unison, and true fruits are ever-perfect. Through this ritual offering, we express our profound sincerity.
Truly, I hope that the Honored Deities will graciously accept this offering. Regarding the *mantra* for making offerings to our Buddha, the Tathāgata, I shall now reverently recite it:
Oṃ gaganasvabhāva-vajra hūṃ. (Strike the chime and ring the bell.)
(The Dharma Master visualizes that these offerings are sufficient and manifest before him; all the deities descend to partake of them, none failing to rejoice.

(The presiding Dharma Master pauses briefly while shaking the bell and says: "The Dharma-realm is vast and level, fundamentally without limit. The light of the mind penetrates uniquely—whom could it possibly bind?"

Because sentient beings have been deluded regarding the existence of a body since beginningless time, they have consequently fallen into great suffering that is inexhaustible, pressing upon them in a tangled web.
Alas! They have entered a dream from which they cannot wake despite being called. Believing themselves constrained by the retribution for their sins, they see layer upon layer of hells;
believing themselves presided over by a sovereign authority, they encounter scroll after scroll of penal codes. Furthermore, as for the system of the earth...

As for the heavens: the Honored Lord Di (Indra), sovereign of the first dhyāna in the world-system of the Four Great Kings and lord of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, though he perceives them with deep compassion, cannot save them;
within the realm of his radiance, he beholds them clearly, yet they remain difficult to disperse.
For when matters and principles intersect, they become ever more firm; thus, when conditions are slightly sparse, the response does not come.
Now, holding the mirror of a single mind, one receives the Buddha’s light from above; grasping the pearl of manifold wonders, one simultaneously proclaims the power of the Dharma.

One transcribes the earnestness of supplications from the lower realm and invokes the all-encompassing grace of clemency from the heavens. That a favorable decree will be granted is certain. Thus it is verified.
Do not fear the path ahead. Within it, the subtle workings of the numinous mechanism are beyond human capacity; to turn the heavens and revolve the earth is solely the power of the Divine.
It shatters all the hells at once and simultaneously opens all the barriers of the ten directions.
That which is bent is made straight, and no hidden darkness remains unilluminated. Receiving the auspiciousness of the imperial decree, the phoenixes cry and the peacocks sing; rely upon the Dharma.
Through the majestic spiritual power of this assembly, dragons descend and tigers submit; how could there be the harm of the *āpāṇa* demons? It fully bestows the security of the universal path.
For those who practice the conduct of a Bodhisattva, this is surely a source of joy; for those who act as messengers of the Tathāgata, they will surely find fulfillment herein.
With an empty and level mind, throughout heaven and earth, the conditions for peace and happiness arise from the clouds of compassion and the Dharma.
Rain! We pray that today, the sealed message shall be fully understood; it is the suchness of the Dharma-nature, and may Heaven’s workings be harmonious and serene.
All our humble intentions are contained within this memorial; we request that you specifically command its proclamation and deign to grant us your attentive hearing.
(Strike the chime and ring the bell.)
(The primary tablet proclaims the *Fan* commentary; the auxiliary tablet proclaims the *Shi* commentary; the primary tablet proclaims the *Dian*). (The auxiliary tablet says:
We reverently contemplate the messenger, whose mind is one with the Buddha-mind and whose function encompasses all divine activities; having already manifested his body across the nine stages.
Capable of racing side-by-side with the galloping steeds in the layered heavens, it need not wait for a boat to traverse the sun and moon;
it can even allow one to drag their sandals and walk upon the stars above. Entering the Floating Banner King Realm (*Kūṭāgāra-rāja-kṣetra*), it is as if reflected in a lapis lazuli screen;

containing the sublime jewel celestial abodes, it is like a hanging necklace of genuine pearls. Moved by resonance, it responds accordingly; through transformation, it is able to penetrate all sounds.
First, you shall dissolve the five-colored clouds; then, in accordance with the waxing and waning of the double-orbed moon, do not neglect your duties, but surely compose an appropriate verse.
As this matter involves some labor, it is only right that you see me off. Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for seeing one off.
I shall now reverently recite: Oṃ amara mukhaḥ.
(Strike the chime and ring the bell. [The Main Text states: I take refuge in the Buddha;
I take refuge in the Dharma; I take refuge in the Saṅgha. Having completed the taking of refuge in the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha.

The dispatching of messengers is hereby concluded. I refine this written petition to transform these offerings into resources to assist the messengers on their journey through the clouds to reach every corner of the *sāhasra-lokadhātu*.
I pay homage to the assembly of sages. (Ring the chime and shake the bell. (Burn the petitions, the tablets, and the paper treasures and silks.)
(The Dharma Master visualizes the messenger receiving the command and immediately departing. He penetrates all worlds in the ten directions, reporting back in unison.

(The presiding Dharma Master returns to the inner altar. The presiding Dharma Master offers incense, recites the *biaobai* (manifestation of intent), strikes the *qing*, and performs three prostrations.)

(The petitioner announces: "The mission dispatched has been successfully accomplished. Boundless are the roots of goodness; grace extends throughout the entire realm of sand-grains. I pay homage to the assembly of noble ones" (inquiry made as one exits the altar).

The Treatise says: The text serves to assist the spiritual brilliance of those who practice the Dharma, to initiate the resonance between heaven and humanity, to penetrate the vital energy and pulse of the Tathāgata, and to open the numinous mechanism of the Dharma assembly.
Within the ritual manuals, one may sometimes use a written petition to request clemency.
The two petitions are identical in wording; one might say that what is seen repeatedly does not grow stale.

Yet, when sight and hearing fail to convey the full meaning, human efforts render the Dharma dead, and how could the divine response be efficacious? For this reason, those who find themselves in similar circumstances often compose separate formal documents.

This is intended to provide a single insight for even the lowliest grass-cutters and firewood-gatherers, rather than to establish something eccentric; it is simply that I do not dare to conflate them. May this be of benefit.
The multitudes of living beings may dare to flee from their offenses against me; yet I know that there are none who would truly offend me.
When it comes to the desire for goodness, who among men is not like me? Since I have complied with the wishes of sentient beings, even Heaven will not oppose me, let alone human beings.
How much more so for ghosts and spirits!

(On this day at the hour of noon, the monks are provided with a vegetarian meal. If one applies the mind with single-minded effort to the ritual site, then the affairs may be settled with ease. One should simply provide thirty-six wen for the meal and twelve wen for the *dakṣiṇā* (offering). This is practiced at the gate; it is simple and easy to perform.)
A Treatise on the Commonality of Nature in the Great Universal Salvation Altar for the Holy and the Mundane, Beings of Land and Water, within the Dharma Realm. Volume Four.
A Treatise on the Commonality of Nature in the Great Universal Salvation Altar for the Holy and the Mundane, Beings of Land and Water, within the Dharma Realm. Volume Five.
Written by the Practitioner of Pure Karma, Zhi-guan, Zheng Ying-fang.
Please descend from the hall to receive the bath and the recitation of the precepts (if the time is too late, one may take a small meal and sit briefly in the incense-lamp hall).
On the fourth day, during the third, fourth, and fifth watches of the night.

(The Dharma Master enters the altar. One person from among the fourfold assembly follows him in. The presiding master holds the incense burner. The Ritual Text states: With a sincere heart, we take refuge in the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm.
(One prostration; strike the chime; ring the bell.)
(As stated in the *Zhengbiao*: To call it "incense" is to provide the general name for all phenomena (*dharmas*). To take up its substance is to grasp the full measure of the single mind.
If one pellet is burned, it possesses all fragrances; without leaving its immediate location, it pervades the ten directions.
It spreads clouds of incense with inexhaustible light, gathering the multitudes of sentient beings within the *dharmadhātu*. Upon hearing this summons, there is none who hesitates.
I hope that each of you will exhort your followers so that all may attend the assembly without fail. Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for conveying messages by means of incense;
I shall now reverently recite it (as one burns incense and recites): [Insert Mantra Here]
Oṃ śivari-tamani aprakoṭa suparṇi vikāci hūṃ. (The Dharma Master visualizes:
clouds of incense like an ocean, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic power, pervade the entire *dharmadhātu* before the multitudes of sentient beings in the six realms.
They subtly permeate their spiritual consciousness, causing them all to become aware and awaken; they give rise to hearts of joy and hasten to this assembly.)

(Commentary: Observe this single body of water; it must have its source. Flowing incessantly from the Lake Anavatapta of one’s own mind, it enters the ocean of *sarvajñā* (all-knowing wisdom) of the fundamental nature, vast and boundless.
Thus, it fills the vessels of the Dharma and pulses through the recitation of mantras, purifying these seats and cleansing those sense-bases and objects. At each and every place of sitting:
The Radiant Terrace: those who come here one after another are a gathering of wisdom. It surpasses the ice pitcher that washes the soul and shares the brilliance contained within a lamp or mirror.
Abiding in their respective positions, they are fundamentally unmoving. Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for sprinkling purification;
I shall now reverently recite it.
Oṃ śavara śmāye hūṃ phaṭ śrīmahe svāhā. (Recite this twice.
While walking, sprinkle [water] in the four directions, above, below, and upon the path of purification, scattering flowers along the path of purification.)

(The Dharma Master visualizes: wherever the water reaches, it immediately becomes a consecrated boundary (*sīmābandha*), solemn, pure, vast, and expansive, with radiant and brilliant splendor. He further visualizes the Pure Path as clouds of light, from which pavilions emerge, clearly reflected and arrayed one within another in successive layers.)

(From the *Zhengbiao*: "I humbly observe that between the holy and the ordinary there is no distinction, yet their emotions and intellects falsely divide them. It is essential only to not lose one's constancy;

then one can wondrously attain the true essence. As for the simultaneous arising of sense organs and objects, and the mutual collision of self and others—the causes they receive differ, and the fruits of retribution they undergo vary. Their inherent natures may be beautiful or ugly; the suffering they endure..."
There is the heavy and the light; they wander restlessly across water, land, and air, and continue incessantly through death, birth, and the intermediate state (*antarābhava*).
If one does not understand this, where will they ultimately turn? It is therefore fitting to unite the two fields of compassion and reverence, so that they may be perfumed like rain and dew.
Furthermore, the two aspects of resentment and kinship have been unified and transformed into mist and clouds. Now, this auspicious assembly opens in unison and the sublime moment has arrived.
Boundless worthies and sages have gathered like clouds within the *bodhimaṇḍa*, while the Dharma-protecting *śrāmaṇeras* and *devas* are spread out like stars upon the mats.
The Tathāgatas of the ten directions join their hands to guide all sentient beings; the wondrous Dharma of the Three Vehicles...
There are no two capacities; there is only this one matter. Encompassed by majestic spiritual power, the cool clarity reflects the radiance of the moon’s affection.

Its vast measure is entirely inclusive, such that the seams of celestial robes vanish all around. By this, one leaves behind fear, escapes the snare, departs from the boiling cauldron of fire, and ascends to the couch.
One sheds the distinct forms of scales and feathers, manifesting as a human or a celestial being.

The entire body rests from the toils of worldly affliction and returns to take refuge in the Dharma-realm. In every stage, one becomes a child of the Buddha; in every thought, one fully acts as a precious king.
May we swiftly give birth to the lotus of peace and bliss, and joyfully and perfectly realize the fruit of Bodhi. (This is to assist in expressing shared mindfulness.
I only pray that the Buddha’s light will shine upon us and the Jewel of Dharma will guide us. As soon as the words of invocation are heard, may all be gathered with majestic power.

Arrive according to the ritual protocol (strike the chime; ring the bell). ○ (At this time, the Dharma Master’s table is moved to face west. The two *biao* tables are oriented such that one side faces west and the other faces east, so that the upper and lower sections do not turn their backs to one another.)

(The Master stands facing outward. The Ritual Text reads: With single-minded devotion, we invoke the One True Dharma-realm, which manifests throughout the ten directions in infinite, overlapping layers.

All ordinary beings and devas of the three periods of time— whether of the formless realm or the realm of form, those dwelling in clouds or upon the earth, those in the palaces of the sun, moon, and stars,

and all those governed by the Four Heavenly Kings, including celestial generals, celestial officials, celestial youths, and celestial maidens, together with their retinues— I pray that you do not depart from your original nature,
but manifest the bodies of humans and devas at this very day and hour to attend this Dharma assembly. (Strike the chime, ring the bell, and turn the body.)
(Perform one inquiry toward the outside).

(The Dharma Master visualizes: immeasurable devas, with pure radiance, surrounded by their retinues, come through the air and take their place within the pavilions of the Pure Path. Their precious nature is serene and composed, and all give rise to joy.
[They] manifest by scattering flowers upon this seat, before the small banners, and atop the Pure Path).

(The Master stands facing outward. The Assistant Reciter says: With single-minded devotion, we invoke the One True Dharma-realm, which manifests throughout the ten directions in infinite, overlapping layers.
All those throughout the three periods of time— ordinary beings, celestial seers, dharma seers, earth seers, water seers, human seers, ghost seers, masters of seers, disciples of seers,
seer boys, and seer maidens, each together with their retinues— we pray that you will not deviate from your original nature.

Manifesting in the bodies of humans and devas, at this very day and hour, they come to attend this Dharma assembly. (Strike the chime; ring the bell; perform the salutation as in the initial position.
The Dharma Master contemplates according to the occasion; the ritual master recites the prose and scatters flowers, as in the initial position.)

(The Master stands facing outward. The Liturgy for Invocation states: With single-minded devotion, we invoke the True Dharma-realm, which manifests throughout the ten directions in infinite, overlapping layers.

All those throughout the three periods of time who dwell on the stage of ordinary beings—those of the nāga class, the gandharva class, yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍa classes, garuḍa classes, mahoraga classes, and the śrīdevīs; whether lords or ministers, men or women;

from the celestial palaces above to the very limits of the earth below—all you various classes possessing supernatural powers, together with your respective retinues, we pray that you will not fail to honor your original vows.

[The assembly] manifests in the forms of humans and devas. At this very day and at this very moment, they come to attend the Dharma assembly. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell. Inquire after one another’s well-being, as in the first position.
The Dharma Master directs his thoughts according to the occasion; he recites the liturgical prose and scatters flowers, as in the first position.)

(The Master of the Dharma stands facing outward. The Assistant Reciter says: With single-minded devotion, we invoke the One True Dharma Realm, which manifests throughout the ten directions in infinite, overlapping layers.
All those throughout the three periods of time—the wheel-turning kings of gold, silver, copper, and iron;
their precious wheels, precious women, precious horses, precious elephants, generals, treasurers, and wish-fulfilling jewels;

along with their various retinues and attendants—may you, without departing from your original nature, manifest in the forms of humans and devas this very day and at this very hour to attend this Dharma assembly. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell.)
Inquiry after health is the same as at the beginning. The Dharma Master contemplates according to the occasion; the ritual master offers incense and scatters flowers, as in the initial position.

(The presiding master stands facing outward. The formal invocation says: With single-minded devotion, we invite the One True Dharma Realm, which manifests throughout the ten directions, appearing in all beautiful and foul forms and sounds.
High and low mental capacities, abodes in the center or at the periphery, faculties whole or incomplete—layer upon layer, inexhaustible.
All beings of the three times: rulers and ministers, civil and military officials, men and women, old and young;

whether practicing or not, whether correct or deviant—all ordinary persons together with their retinues—may they, without departing from their original nature, manifest as bodies of humans and devas on this very day. Today...

At that time, [the assembly] approaches the Dharma assembly (ringing the chime, shaking the bell, and exchanging greetings as in the first position). The Dharma Master directs his thoughts according to the occasion (the two [attendants] scatter flowers as in the first position).
The Treatise says: Someone asked, "How can a person ever come to respond? It is the constant nature of humans not to undergo transformation;
yet to transform and be able to respond—how close is that to the impossible? I have heard that Zhao Yan saw a very beautiful woman painted on a picture.
He gazed at her for a long time, until the painter laughed at his foolishness and deceived him, saying, "Do you know her name?"

After a hundred days, she called out "Zhen-zhen" (the Real One). Then she emerged from the painting and became a human being; her appearance was exactly as described. Indeed, she came forth and became a person.
Once she had borne a son, her friends discussed her as a supernatural apparition. The beautiful woman then took her child and re-entered the painting.
Within the painting, there were thus two people. During a year of famine in Yizheng, a Buddhist monastery outside the city ran out of firewood for cooking.

The monks continued to strike the fish-bell and recite the Buddha’s name without ceasing. The magistrate heard the sound of the bell in his ears; after a long while, he wondered from where it was coming.

Following the sound, he arrived at the temple and thereupon made an offering. The maiden Shanmiao followed the master to the sea and prayed, saying, "If my heart is sincere, may this chest arrive of its own accord.
She cast the chest into the sea; the wind stirred up the waves, and the chest leapt onto the master's boat.
The woman then made a vow to follow her master and protect the Dharma; she threw herself into the sea and was instantly transformed into a dragon.

She guarded the ship as it traveled across the ocean until they reached a foreign land, where she manifested her spiritual power to protect the Dharma. In ancient times, there was a filial son who entered a forest with his wife and prayed, saying:
"If there is a tree suitable for carving images of our two elders, may that tree move of its own accord. Indeed, one tree moved, so they took it and carved the images.
The image was extremely efficacious. A monk, seeking to raise funds for offerings, arrived at the entrance of a house.

The host said, "If you can strike a bell within this earthen mound so that it produces sound, I shall grant you a donation. He struck it, and it rang out with a clear resonance at his touch. At that moment, a young woman was lost in thought.
Concentrating his spirit, he went at once and caused that woman to give birth to a son; yet he himself never left his mother.
The two boys walked along on opposite sides of a stream. The first (A) took up a blade and said to the second (B), "I shall kill you. Immediately, B’s head fell off.
Jia was immediately executed by the sword. During the official interrogation, he confessed no truth. Water was bailed out to dry the mud, whereupon footprints were found upon the mud;

they matched Jia’s feet, yet Jia had not initially set foot there, and his clothes and shoes remained undampened. When Emperor Ming visited Shu, he saw a living shrine dedicated to a Prefectural Governor.
Upon inquiring as to his name, he learned that this man had deeply received the bounty of the state, yet had recently turned toward the rebels. He then commanded his attendants...
Wei used the Thousand-Ox Blade to sever the head of a statue. Although this man was a thousand *li* away, his head immediately fell to the ground for no apparent reason.

A certain filial and incorruptible official (*xiaolian*) was traveling to the capital for the examinations and stayed overnight at a monastery. Before dawn, a monk was performing a sacrifice to his ancestors.

The official’s soul wandered among them, ascended the monk’s seat, and ate two dates. While the sound of the monk’s chanting still rang in his ears, he suddenly woke up in a startle, and [the dates] were in his mouth.
There was the taste of jujube. Upon rising to inspect the offerings for the monks, he found that two jujubes were actually missing.

The filial son’s mother, because someone had arrived and she could not call her son herself, urgently bit her finger. The son immediately felt pain in his heart and returned home. A mirror one chi long.

It manifests images extending for a thousand *li*; yet the mirror does not increase in size, nor do the images increase in smallness. The site of enlightenment (*dōjō*) is translucent; the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) has no exterior.
It is bound together to manifest that there is nothing obstructed; it is not by means of binding that obstruction is created. Furthermore, this applies to all dharmic activities.
"Benefiting beings in all directions, the mind is beyond the measure of ordinary sentiment. Thus, those who come to this assembly shall also penetrate these three minds;
it is something that cannot be reached through calculation or conceptual discrimination. Is this so? The answer was: "The general is the general; the particular is the particular.
Departing from these two paths, provide another word."

All beings of the three periods of time— those comprised within the realms of devas and humans, those comprised within the realms of pretas and animals, those born from eggs, wombs, moisture, or by transformation, as well as all the asuras,

The same as the first position. The Dharma Master, according to the capacity of the assembly, directs his thoughts. The two [assistants] scatter flowers. (Same as the first position).

Once again, relying on the power of the secret [mantra], may the banner of radiant light be displayed to illuminate the dim alleys of ignorance, so that no loss of direction occurs.
May one proceed securely along the direct path and swiftly realize the way home. Only...

Those sentient beings in the three miserable realms who suffer extreme agony, obstructed by their evil karma and having lost their way—by the power of this mantra, may all obstacles be completely removed, so that they may all tread upon the level path and joyfully arise for the assembly.

(Commentary: Among the six classes of ordinary beings, delusion is most prevalent; they have all arrived together. The Three Honored Ones are majestic and venerable, and it is certain that they inspire both awe and affection.
Unless expedient means are relied upon to comfort and gladden the minds of the multitude, there is fear that they might hesitate or retreat to one side.

Therefore, when the esoteric words are proclaimed to reach those present, it is hoped that their feelings of alarm and terror will be instantly forgotten, so that all may attain tranquility and composure.
And so they abide. My Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for dispelling fear;

(From the *Zhengbiao*: "The Dharma-rite of Radiant Light. The site of practice is perfected. By receiving even the grace of a single speck of dust or a single drop of water, one gains benefit that penetrates from beginning to end.

Necessarily, their physical forms and appearances will be at peace. Those of sharp faculties have already merged their mind and its objects; those with heavy obstructions have not yet transformed their form and spirit.

Like flowers in the sky or the moon in water, suddenly dying and suddenly being born; like reflections in a mirror or the luster of a pearl, they appear as male.

I shall now reverently recite: Oṃ kili kumāri hūḥ hūḥ cāḥ cāḥ svāhā. (Strike the chime; ring the bell.)

(The Auxiliary Gloss states: One does not give rise to discrimination within this; therefore, this place is most auspicious. All phenomena are fundamentally empty;

Each established their own borders; yet, due to slight lapses in intention or a lack of compliance in speech, they would suddenly change countenance in indignation and hastily give rise to irrational anger.

relying on their status as elders, they oppressed the lowly. They encroached upon the lands of their neighbors and elders.

He expanded his new residence by seizing the wealth of the market people to fill his own treasuries; he wantonly inflicted the cruelty of whips and canes and unjustly imposed the grievances of litigation.
Relying on his power, he oppressed others, deceiving their hearts and obscuring the way of righteousness.

The water of nature is vast and inclusive, naturally perfecting the brilliance and purity of the whole body. The wind of wisdom sweeps across and fans it.

Using paper as a substitute for silk, and silk as a substitute for cloth—this wondrous function is innate; what is there of the empty or the real? Thus, one attains [the mastery of] length and shortness.
