Yet, because the majestic radiance of this single mind never ceases, the Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha manifest within the dharma-realm in response to capacities.
These manifestations of the Three Jewels of names and signs are intended to draw forth the mind.
Within this, there is only the single essence of the Three Jewels. The manifestation of the Three Jewels is neither external nor internal;

the interpenetration of the Three Jewels is neither other nor self; the permanence of the Three Jewels is neither extinction nor birth; the perfect containment of the Three Jewels is neither three nor one.
Those who see this, those who awaken to this, those who cultivate this, and those who realize this—this is the resplendent orthodox tradition, far removed from [all conceptual extremes].
Māras and outsiders, since you have come to this site of enlightenment by means of causes and conditions, you should know that the Three Jewels within your own minds shall preach the Dharma for you.

(The Dharma Master strikes the sounding block and says: "I now perform this act of taking refuge for you all, so that those who possess roots of goodness from past lives may thereby reach maturity, and those who have not yet resolved their minds may establish a foundation here.
You should know that the names of the Triple Gem transcend those of humans and devas;
the mind of refuge leads directly to Equal Enlightenment. This is the new letter 'i' [the apex of the *triśūla*], not..."
This ancient medicinal formula is something that those who merely hasten toward the ten wholesome deeds cannot know, and something that those habituated to the immovable cannot practice.
Now, for your sake, relying upon the radiance of the Triple Gem, I perform this supreme deed.

This is because you inherently possess the Three Gems as a single essence, which serves as the cause capable of eliciting a response; it is the Buddhas who manifest and realize the Three Gems as a single essence.
This is the condition that responds to such capacity. Only when the way of resonance and response intersects does the mechanism for liberation manifest.
You should maintain solemn stillness, close your eyes, and clarify your spirit; follow my words as the Three Honored Ones are present before you.

(The Dharma Master strikes the wooden sounding-block and says: I, disciple [Name], from this present life until the attainment of Buddhahood, take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, and take refuge in the Sangha.
(Recite three times; the assembly chants along with each phrase.)
(The Dharma Master strikes the ruler and says: "The conferral of the Three Refuges upon you has now been completed. To further ensure the perfection of the Dharma, we shall add three recitations.
(The Dharma Master strikes the ruler and says: "I, disciple [Name], have completed my refuge in the Buddha; I have completed my refuge in the Dharma; I have completed my refuge in the Sangha."
(Recite three times; the assembly joins in for each line.

(The Dharma Master strikes the ruler and says: Since you have already taken refuge in the Triple Gem and become disciples of the Buddha, you ought to clarify the Bodhisattva’s ground of mind (*citta-bhūmi*) as the foundation for attaining Buddhahood.
Now, the mirror of the mind is empty and luminous, fundamentally devoid of a single thing. From—

The mind manifests forms; the entire form is the mind. As one prepares to reveal the luminosity of the precious nature (*ratnagotra*) and initiate the three trainings (*triśikṣā*), one must first ensure that the inner sanctuary (*citta*) is pure and free from even a single speck of defilement.
Therefore, upon entering the maṇḍala, one should first perform repentance (*pāpadeśanā*).

In the language of China, this is called "repenting of errors" (*huìguò*); in the language of the Buddha, it is called *chàn mó*. When both the Chinese and Sanskrit terms are used together, it is termed "repentance" (*chànhuì*). One repents of one's own transgressions.
I beg the Three Jewels for your forbearance; thus, there is the name "repentance. The pure ritual arena is entirely manifested from the mind.
Since the mind has no form or appearance, both sin and merit are empty. This very mind of yours is the place where one repents of sin.
In principle, this expresses right contemplation; in practice, it encompasses auxiliary conduct. When the primary and the auxiliary reflect one another, the Dharma is not partial or deficient.

With a single true mind, one casts oneself in sincerity to reform one's transgressions—this is the method of repentance (*chánhuì*). From the stage of repentance, it extends downward to the six classes of ordinary beings and upward to the level of Equal Enlightenment (*sànjié*);
as long as the light of the mind is not yet full, there are faults and errors. One should stand before the Buddha and lay them bare.
I offer my apologies. This very act of repentance encompasses boundless meaning; there is no need for further elaboration.
Now, for your sakes, I shall perform this repentance according to the methods of the Mahāyāna sūtras.

You all should purify your body, speech, and mind, so that in every thought-moment you may behold Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and the Buddhas of the ten directions. You must be most earnest and sincere.
Mind, follow what I have spoken.

(The Dharma Master chants: All evil karma created in the past, Arising from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion, Produced by body, speech, and mind— I now repent it all. (Three times; the assembly joins in for each line.)
(The Dharma Master strikes the wooden gavel and says: "All sentient beings are fundamentally equal.

Through illusory perfuming, seeds are formed, each distinct from the others—whether they be the seed-nature of a Tathāgata, a Pratyekabuddha, a Śrāvaka, or one of indeterminate nature, even down to the seed-natures of non-Buddhists and icchantikas.
Now, entering the great furnace, they all return to a single fire; the jars, basins, hairpins, and bracelets are all but gold."
How much more so for the Tathāgatas of the ten directions, who sit together at the site of enlightenment; for the myriad sages and thousand spirits, whose compassionate light protects them in common;

and for those perfumed by the causes of wisdom, who achieve the most supreme state. Having relinquished all manifold things, they perfectly manifest the one true reality. Thus one contemplates all the Tathāgatas.
Throughout the worlds of the ten directions, the ranks and karmic offices of true spirits are distinct in their nature and characteristics, like lamps within a mirror or a mirror within a lamp.
The true mind contains and manifests them all, accommodating both form and emptiness; whether ordinary beings or sages, existence or non-existence, they appear with crystalline clarity.
There is nothing further to be said—this is the bodhicitta. Can you all give rise to this bodhicitta? (The assembly replied: "We have already given rise to it. To give rise to this...
At the moment your mind [arises], the Buddhas of the ten directions rejoice for you; this is the root of attaining Buddhahood and the cause for delivering sentient beings.
Throughout many births across kalpas, it never changes or perishes. Yet, as the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* states: "When the aspiration for benefit arises, one immediately attains perfect enlightenment.
How could [the Buddha] allow you to remain stagnant by suggesting it is achieved only through gradual perfection? The Three Jewels appear before you for your sake.

Realization. (The Dharma Master strikes the sounding block and says: Although this is so, in reality all places are empty. Every single thing is the Way; phenomena can manifest principle, and every dharma is mind.
From a single gate, infinite gates appear; within a single stage, all stages are contained. This must rely upon the power of one's vows.
One shall avoid falling into the state of emptiness and voidness; by performing this rite of filling, the measure of great compassion will be fulfilled.
Those who resolve to attain Bodhicitta should not harbor self-doubt; they should follow my words and present their case before the Buddha.
(The Dharma Master chants: "I vow to deliver all sentient beings, boundless as they are. I vow to sever all afflictions, inexhaustible as they are.
I vow to study all Dharma gates, immeasurable as they are. I vow to realize the supreme Way of the Buddha. (Recite three times; the assembly joins in for each line.)

(The Dharma Master strikes the sounding-block and says: Since you have given rise to the supreme resolve, you are worthy of receiving the wondrous precepts. These grasp the essentials of the Six Perfections and open the source of the myriad practices.
They heal all ailments and liberate one from every suffering. "Precept" (*śīla*) means "to cease. It is to cease evil and practice good; to cease coarse conduct and cultivate the sublime.
Thus, there is no evil that is not severed, no goodness that is not cultivated, and no being that is not delivered. The precepts are called the Three Aggregates (*triskandha*).
This is what is meant by that. Precepts take luminosity as their essence and likewise take luminosity as their function.

The function does not depart from the essence, yet the essence is ever-perfect; the essence does not depart from the function, yet the function is ever-pure. Your mind possesses the precepts; I shall now reveal them for you.
Perform the *karmavācanā* (ritual action); listen attentively to the procedure.
(The Dharma Master strikes the wooden fish and says: "Listen attentively, you sons of the Buddha!

You now seek from me to receive all the training precepts (*śikṣāpada*) of the bodhisattvas, the pure ethical discipline (*śīla*) of all bodhisattvas—namely, the ethical discipline of restraint (*saṃvara-śīla*), the ethical discipline of gathering virtuous dharmas (*kuśala-dharma-saṃgrāhaka-śīla*), and the ethical discipline of benefiting sentient beings (*sattvārtha-kriyā-śīla*).
Regarding these training precepts and these pure ethical disciplines, all bodhisattvas of the past have already [received them]..."
Having received, studied, and understood it; having practiced and accomplished it—so shall all future bodhisattvas receive, study, understand, practice, and accomplish it.
All present bodhisattvas now receive, now study, now understand, now practice, and now accomplish it, destined to become Buddhas in the future.
From this life until the attainment of the Buddha-body, throughout that interval, you [should do likewise].
"You must not violate it. Are you able to uphold it? (The assembly replies, "We are able to uphold it. This first *karmavācanā* is now completed.
Throughout the worlds of the ten directions, the sublime and virtuous Dharma of the precepts causes all things to tremble by the power of the mental karma.
(The Dharma Master strikes the wooden fish and says: "You all, as you have said... are you able to uphold [this]? (The assembly answers: "We are able to uphold it.
This is the second *karmavācanā*; the sublime and virtuous precepts of the ten directions now descend from the void like clouds and canopies, covering your heads.
(The Dharma Master strikes the *shichui* and says: "You all, as you have said... are you able to uphold [this]? (The assembly replies: "We are able to uphold it.

This is the third *karmavācanā*; it is now completed. The wondrous and virtuous precepts of the ten directions shall flow from the crowns of your heads into your bodies and minds, filling your primary retribution and becoming forever the seed of Buddhahood.

(The Dharma Master strikes the wooden fish and says: "I have just performed for you the threefold proclamation of the *karmavācanā* and the transmission of the precepts. The ritual procedure is now complete;
this is called 'attaining the precepts.'"
(The Dharma Master strikes the wooden gavel and says: "You, sons of the Buddha, relying upon the Triple Gem, have generated the unconditioned precepts (*avijñapti-śīla*).
Having personally heard the *karmavācanā*, you have accomplished wholesome karma. You should from this moment forth maintain them with firm resolve; at all times, do not allow any transgression."

It is better to die with precepts than to live without them. Now, for your sake, I shall once again proclaim the Ten Grave Pārājikas from the "Bodhisattva Grounds" chapter of the Brahmajāla Sūtra, in order to clarify the characteristics of upholding and violating [the precepts].
You must study this thoroughly and reverently uphold it.

(The Dharma Master strikes the ruler and says: The Buddha said: "O Son of the Buddha, whether one kills by one's own hand, instructs others to kill, employs the means of killing, praises killing, rejoices upon seeing it committed, or even kills through incantations—regarding the causes of killing, the conditions for killing, the methods of killing, and the karmic actions of killing—one must not intentionally kill any living being whatsoever.
This Bodhisattva should give rise to a mind of constant compassion and filial obedience."
If one who, with a mind intent on using skillful means to rescue and protect all sentient beings, instead kills living beings at will for their own pleasure,
this constitutes a *pārājika* offense for a bodhisattva.

(The Dharma Master strikes the sounding-block and says: "If a Buddha’s disciple steals themselves, teaches others to steal, uses expedient means to steal, steals by incantation, or through the causes and conditions of stealing..."
Regarding the theft of dharmas, the karma of theft, and even the property of spirits and deities, the goods of bandits, or any material wealth—

down to a single needle or a single blade of grass— one must not intentionally steal them. Yet, if a bodhisattva, who ought to give rise to a mind of filial piety toward the Buddha-nature and a mind of compassion,
and who should constantly assist all people in generating merit and happiness, instead goes on to steal another's property, this is [a transgression].
The Bodhisattva’s *pārājika* offense.

(The Dharma Master strikes the ruler and says: "If a son of the Buddha indulges in sexual misconduct himself, or teaches others to indulge in sexual misconduct—even with any woman—he must not intentionally engage in sexual misconduct.
This includes the causes of lust, the conditions of lust, the methods of lust, and the karma of lust; even with the females of animals, or the females of devas and ghosts."

Furthermore, if a bodhisattva engages in sexual misconduct through improper means— failing to give rise to a heart of filial obedience and instead seeking to rescue and deliver all sentient beings by bestowing the pure Dharma upon them,
yet conversely giving rise to sexual desire toward others, making no distinction between animals and even one's own mother,
daughter, sister, or other members of the six relations of kinship, and lacking any heart of compassion— this constitutes a *pārājika* offense for that bodhisattva.

(The Dharma Master strikes the ruler and says: "If a disciple of the Buddha speaks falsely himself, teaches others to speak falsely, or employs skillful means to speak falsely—whether through the causes of false speech, the conditions of false speech, the methods of false speech, or the karma of false speech—even to the point of claiming to have seen what was not seen, or claiming not to have seen what was seen."

While their own body and mind are characterized by false speech, the Bodhisattva constantly gives rise to right speech and right view, and likewise causes all sentient beings to give rise to right speech and right view;
yet they instead further incite all sentient beings toward wrong speech, wrong views, and wrong actions.
This constitutes a *pārājika* offense for the Bodhisattva.

(The Dharma Master strikes the ruler and says: "O Disciples of the Buddha! To sell alcohol oneself, to teach others to sell alcohol, or to engage in the causes, conditions, methods, and karmic actions of selling alcohol—none of these forms of alcohol may be sold.
Such alcohol gives rise to the causes and conditions for transgression; yet the Bodhi..."
A bodhisattva should give rise to the wisdom of clear penetration in all sentient beings;
yet if, on the contrary, they cause all sentient beings to give rise to perverted thoughts, this constitutes a pārājika offense for that bodhisattva.
(The Dharma Master strikes the sounding-block and says: "If a son of the Buddha, with his own mouth, speaks of the faults of lay or ordained Bodhisattvas, bhikṣus, or bhikṣuṇīs;
or teaches others to speak of their faults, the causes of their faults, the conditions of their faults, the nature of their faults, or the karma of their faults."
If a bodhisattva, upon hearing non-Buddhists, evil persons, or those of the two vehicles (śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha) speak what is neither Dharma nor Vinaya within the Buddha’s teachings,
always gives rise to a mind of compassion and teaches these evil people to produce right faith in the Mahāyāna; yet,
if the bodhisattva instead speaks of faults and transgressions within the Buddha’s own teachings, this constitutes a pārājika offense for that bodhisattva.

(The Dharma Master strikes the ruler and says: "O Sons of the Buddha! To praise oneself and disparage others, or to teach others to praise themselves and disparage others—whether through the causes of disparaging others, the conditions of disparaging others, the methods of disparaging others, or the karma of disparaging others—a Bodhisattva should instead undergo all such insults and humiliations on behalf of all sentient beings.
They should direct evil matters toward themselves and give good things to others. If one exalts one's own virtues..."
To conceal the good deeds of others and cause them to suffer defamation is a *pārājika* offense for a bodhisattva.

(The Dharma Master strikes the ruler and says: "If a son of the Buddha is himself stingy, teaches others to be stingy, or through the causes, conditions, methods, and karmic actions of stinginess—yet when a bodhisattva sees any poor person coming to beg, he should give to that person according to their needs, giving everything."
Furthermore, if a bodhisattva, out of an evil mind or a mind of anger, does not give even a single coin, a single needle, or a single blade of grass; and if, when there is one who seeks the Dharma,
they do not explain even a single word, a single verse, or a portion of the Dharma as small as a speck of dust, but instead reviles and insults them,
this constitutes a *pārājika* offense for that bodhisattva.

(The Dharma Master strikes the ruler and says: "O sons of the Buddha! If you harbor anger yourself, or teach others to be angry—whether through the causes of anger, the conditions of anger, the methods of anger, or the karmic actions of anger—a Bodhisattva should instead cultivate roots of goodness in all sentient beings and engage in matters free from contention, constantly giving rise to a mind of compassion."
One who possesses a heart of filial piety and obedience, yet conversely treats all sentient beings— and even non-sentient things— with an evil mind, insulting and reviling them,
assaulting them with the hands, or striking them with knives and staves, and whose intent still does not cease; if the other person seeks reconciliation,
speaking kindly to offer apology and repentance, yet the offender’s anger still does not stop— this constitutes a *pārājika* offense for a bodhisattva.

(The Dharma Master strikes the ruler and says: "If a disciple of the Buddha personally slanders the Triple Gem, or teaches others to slander the Triple Gem—slandering its causes, its conditions, its teachings, and its karma—and yet a Bodhisattva hears even a single word of slander against the Buddha’s voice from a non-Buddhist or an evil person..."
It is as if three hundred spears were piercing one's heart; how much more so when one speaks such slander oneself?

To fail to give rise to a mind of faith and filial obedience, and instead further assist evil persons and those with wrong views in their slandering—this constitutes a *pārājika* offense for a bodhisattva.
(The Dharma Master strikes the ruler and says: "What has been recited above was specifically for your sake: the proclamation of the characteristics of the ten grave precepts.

You should uphold them and apply your minds in this way; this constitutes the virtuous practice of the Bodhisattva path. (Descend from the seat. Exchange greetings. Strike the chime. Clear the seats.)

(The *Zhengbiao* states: All sentient beings of the six realms within the Dharma-realm, having now received the pure precepts, must first pay homage to the Triple Gem and the assembly of holy ones currently seated at the site of enlightenment;

only then may you proceed forward to participate in this Dharma assembly. I now extol the sublime names of the Triple Gem, hoping that by receiving their majestic power, they will grant their protection and empowerment.
Homage to the Buddha Vairocana, currently seated at the site of enlightenment. Homage to the Original Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha.
Homage to Amitābha Buddha, who extends his light to receive and guide beings. Homage to the Honored Maitreya Buddha, who will descend to be born in the future.
Homage to the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Flower Ornament of the Great Vaipulya; Homage to the Lotus Sūtra of the Sublime Dharma;
Homage to the Śūraṅgama Sūtra of the Great Buddha-Crown; Homage to the Suvarṇaprabhāsa Sūtra, the Sovereign King of Sutras;
Homage to the Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī Sūtra.
Homage to Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva. Homage to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. Homage to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva.
Homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Homage to Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva.
(Strike the chime; ring the bell.)

(The Dharma Master visualizes: The multitudes of sentient beings in the six realms, having received the pure radiance of the Triple Gem which illuminates their consciousnesses, pay respectful homage and enter in succession. Each, according to their name-tablet and axis, stands together before the seats, still not daring to sit.)

(From the *Zhengbiao*): Having received the precepts, one becomes a child of the Buddha. Thus, though possessing the substance of the six realms of ordinary beings, one now receives the radiance of the Triple Gem.
With single-minded devotion, all together perform prostrations; greatly rejoicing in this encounter, their hearts are filled with comfort.
As they prepare to solemnly enter the ritual arena, they further seek the secret support of the power of the Dharma. Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses the true [mantra] for ascending the altar...
Recite as follows: Oṃ miphula padma mudga prasara pramihaṃtu kuru lu svāhā. (Strike the chime; ring the bell.)
(The Dharma Master contemplates: "The spirits of each and every sentient being remain unmoving; they shall now take their seats in order.
(The Assistant Announces: "A mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru; the tip of a single hair manifests the realm of the Treasure King.
This is called an inconceivable matter. What has this to do with a mind that clings to anything? May the great assembly come forth with virtue, and through these auspicious conditions, enter."
Assembly! All shall take their places according to rank and maintain their respective dignified deportment. When my mind is empty, all phenomena are empty;
the myriad things of every kind are all subtle and wondrous. Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for the corresponding seat; I shall now reverently recite it.
Oṃ kārmuka padma sunare dhara dharaṇimaṇḍale hūṃ. (The Dharma Master visualizes:

The newly arrived disciples of the Dharma, by virtue of the power of the Buddha-Dharma, each possess beautiful seats appropriate to their bodies, layered and inexhaustible. Within this vast inner maṇḍala, they all sit calmly according to their respective order.)
(The Master of the Dharma proclaims: "Various and inconceivable, may the light encompass all sentient beings.

The hundreds of thousands of myriads of marks of the Bodhisattvas within meditative concentration, through the majestic power of their merit, arise from the ground of the One Mind. Filling every aspiration of the heart, they fully manifest the Tathāgatagarbha.
Hearing the Dharma, they enter the stages and sit in attendance before the Buddha. May they, with a mind of pure offering, [accomplish this] to the end."

Those born [in this state] seek protection; all that they do is accomplished. They are reborn together with their retinues, their bodies flying throughout the ten directions, skillfully rescuing beings from all sufferings.
(The Dharma Master further said: "You, sons of the Buddha, within this radiance, manifest the causes and conditions of the Buddhas, attaining transcendent liberation, or else give rise to..."
Right wisdom; or the realization of supernormal powers and clarity; or boundless spiritual power;

or non-dual diligence—from now until Buddhahood, throughout this interval, one shall mindfully contemplate the kindness of the Triple Gem and diligently provide protection. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell. Inquire after [the teacher’s] well-being. Exit.)
A Discourse on the Commonality of Nature in the Dharma-Realm Sanctuary for the Universal Benefit of the Great Water and Land Feast for Saints and Mundane Beings, Volume Five.
A Discourse on the Commonality of Nature in the Dharma-Realm Sanctuary for the Universal Benefit of the Great Water and Land Feast for Saints and Mundane Beings, Volume Six.
By the Practitioner of Pure Karma, Zhi Guan, Zheng Yingfang.
Recitation of the Verses of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa Sūtra* (Offering for the Lower Hall), Day Five, Fourth and Fifth Watches.

(The Master of the Dharma enters and announces the white petition: With a sincere heart, we take refuge in the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell. One prostration.)
(Recite the Verse of Radiance once while kneeling. The Radiant One currently dwells throughout the worlds of the ten directions;
To the Ever-Abiding Honored One among Two-Legged Beings, I pray that with a heart of great compassion...
Have compassion and remember me; for sentient beings who have no refuge and no protector, may you act as a great refuge for those such as I.
I now, before the One of Ten Powers, with a sincere heart, repent of all my previously committed sins and most grievous evil karmas.
I do not believe in the Buddhas, nor do I revere my elders or kin; I do not strive to cultivate various virtues, but constantly create all manner of evil karma.

Whether out of self-reliance on my noble status, my lineage, or the abundance of my wealth and rank, I act with heedlessness in my prime years and constantly create all manner of evil karma; My mind perpetually gives rise to perverse thoughts.
Uttering evil words with their mouths, they do not see their own transgressions; Constantly creating various evil karmas, they always perform the deeds of fools.

Their minds are shrouded by the darkness of ignorance, Following along with unwholesome friends, they constantly create various evil karmas— Whether due to various forms of play and pleasure, Or again, harboring sorrow and affliction.

Ensnared by greed and hatred, I have committed various evils; By associating with unwholesome people, and through a mind of stinginess and envy, And by practicing flattery and deception out of poverty, I have committed various evils.
Though I do not delight in these manifold faults, Because of the presence of fear and a lack of self-mastery, [I have done so].
Therefore I have committed various evils, Whether through a restless mind, Or due to anger, resentment, and the afflictions of hunger and thirst;
Therefore I have committed various evils. Driven by food, clothing, and craving for women, Burned by the fires of the defilements, Therefore I have committed various evils.
I now repent of all such transgressions as failing to give rise to a mind of reverence toward the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha;
I now repent of all such transgressions as likewise lacking a mind of reverence toward the Pratyekabuddhas and Bodhisattvas;
And I repent of slandering the True Dharma out of ignorance.
I have been unfilial toward my parents; for all such various transgressions, I now repent them all.
Out of the power of folly and arrogance, as well as greed and hatred, I have committed such various transgressions;
I now repent them all. Throughout the worlds of the ten directions, I have made offerings to countless Buddhas.
I vow to uproot sentient beings and cause them to leave all suffering and hardship behind.
May all sentient beings be established in the ten stages; once their merit and wisdom are perfected, may they attain Buddhahood and guide the deluded masses.
For the sake of all sentient beings, I shall practice asceticism for hundreds of thousands of eons through the power of great wisdom.

May all be caused to emerge from the sea of suffering; for the sake of all sentient beings, I shall expound this most supreme and profound sutra, the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, which is able to eliminate all evil karma.
Even if a person has committed extremely grave sins throughout hundreds of thousands of kalpas, by confessing them for even a brief moment, all evils will be completely eradicated.
Relying upon this *Suvarṇaprabhāsa*, I perform such repentance; by this, I shall swiftly exhaust all karmas of suffering.

Through hundreds of thousands of supreme concentrations, inconceivable dhāraṇīs, the faculties, powers, and factors of enlightenment, I shall practice without ever wearying, until I reach the tenth stage.
Abiding in a place replete with rare treasures, Perfecting the merits of a Buddha, And crossing over the stream of birth and death—
Within the ocean of all Buddhas, The profound treasury of merit, And the wondrous wisdom beyond conception,
May I cause all these to be fully attained. I only pray that the Buddhas of the ten directions Will observe and protectively mind me.
With a heart of great compassion, please accept my repentance with pity.
The various evil karmas I have created throughout many kalpas Give rise to suffering and affliction because of them. Out of pity, I pray that you eliminate the evil karmas I have created;
I constantly give rise to a mind of sorrow and fear Throughout the four modes of deportment.
Never having conceived thoughts of joy, yet possessing great compassion, may the Buddhas remove the fears of sentient beings.
I pray that you accept my repentance and cause me to be free from sorrow and suffering. I have afflictive obstructions as well as various karmic retributions;
I pray that with the water of great compassion, you shall wash them away until they are pure.
All the various sins I have committed in the past, And the evil karma I am currently creating— With a sincere heart, I confess them all;
May they all be cleansed and removed. As for all future evil karma, I shall guard against it so that it does not arise;
Should I ever transgress, I shall never dare to conceal it. The three types of bodily actions and the four types of verbal actions.
Furthermore, there are three types of mental karma that bind all sentient beings; they have been in constant succession since beginningless time.
Through these three kinds of conduct, one commits the ten unwholesome actions.
All such manifold transgressions, I now confess them all. Whatever evil deeds I have committed, I shall myself receive their bitter retribution.
Now, before all the Buddhas, I sincerely repent. All virtuous deeds performed here in Jambudvīpa and in other worlds, I now rejoice in them all.
May I leave behind the ten unwholesome actions and practice the path of the ten wholesome deeds, dwelling securely within the ten stages.
Constantly beholding the Buddhas of the ten directions, with my body, speech, and mind, may the merit and wisdom accumulated through my practice—
by these roots of goodness— may I swiftly attain supreme wisdom. Now,
standing before the One of Ten Powers, I openly confess my manifold sufferings and hardships.
The difficulty of the delusions of the ignorant within the three realms of existence; The difficulty of constantly creating extremely heavy evil karma;
The difficulty of the accumulation of my own desires and perversions; The difficulty of the constant arising of craving and the cycle of transmigration;
The difficulty of being attached to this world; The difficulty of the afflictions of all foolish beings.
The difficulty of a deranged mind, distraction, and perversion; The difficulty of associating with evil friends;
The difficulty of being stained by craving within saṃsāra; The difficulty of committing transgressions through the darkness and dullness of hatred and delusion;
The difficulty of being born in the eight states of non-leisure or evil realms; And the difficulty of never having accumulated meritorious virtues.
Now, before all the Most Victorious Ones, I repent of my boundless sinful karma.
I now take refuge in all the Sugatas; I pay homage to the Unsurpassed Honored Ones, oceans of virtue.
Like great mountains of gold illuminating the ten directions, I pray that you will compassionately accept me with your kindness.
Your physical form is golden light, pure and stainless; Your eyes are like clear, deep-blue lapis lazuli.
O Honored One of auspicious majesty and renown, The sun of great compassion and wisdom dispels all darkness.
The radiance of the Buddha-sun is ever-pervasive, Utterly pure, stainless, and free from all dust.
The Moon of the Sage shines with supreme coolness, Able to dispel the fever of afflictions in sentient beings.
Adorned throughout by the thirty-two marks, And fully perfected with the eighty secondary signs;
His merit is inconceivable and peerless, Like the flowing light of the sun illuminating the world.
Your form is as pure and stainless as lapis lazuli, like the full moon suspended in the void;
a wondrous lattice of crystal reflects upon your golden body, adorned with manifold radiances.
Amidst the turbulent torrent of the suffering of birth and death, you are being swept away by the waters of old age, sickness, and sorrow.
Thus this ocean of suffering is difficult to endure; may the Buddha-sun extend its radiance to cause it to be forever exhausted.

I now bow my head to the All-Knowing One, the rare and honored one within the three-thousandfold world system, whose body of shimmering purple-gold light is adorned with every kind of exquisite excellence.
As the volume of the great ocean is difficult to know, As the atoms of the great earth are incalculable,
As Mount Sumeru is beyond measure, And as space has no boundaries,
So too are the merits of the Buddhas; All sentient beings cannot know them.
Though one were to contemplate with earnest thought for immeasurable eons, no one could reach the limit of the shore of his virtues.
Even if this entire great earth and its mountain ranges were broken down into atoms as fine as motes of dust and counted,
and even if the drops of the ocean could be measured by the tip of a hair, the merit of the Buddha could never be numbered.
May all sentient beings together praise the World-Honored One’s fame,
his various merits, and his pure, wondrously adorned marks and signs— whose limits cannot be measured.
Through all my own roots of goodness, may I swiftly attain the state of the Unsurpassed Honored One.
Extensively expounding the True Dharma to benefit all sentient beings, Causing them all to be liberated from manifold sufferings;
Subduing the hosts of the powerful Māra armies, He shall turn the unsurpassed Wheel of the True Dharma.
Abiding for inconceivable numbers of kalpas, He shall satisfy sentient beings with the nectar of immortality.
Just as the Victors of the past, Who have perfected the six pāramitās,
Extinguished all greed, hatred, and delusion, Subdued the afflictions, and removed all suffering—
May I always attain the knowledge of past lives, And be able to remember hundreds of thousands of previous births.
May I also constantly recollect the Honored Muni, And hear the profound Dharma of all Buddhas.
By means of these various roots of goodness, May I serve the infinite and most supreme Honored One,
Leave behind all causes of unwholesomeness, And always practice the truly wondrous Dharma.
May all sentient beings in every world be entirely freed from suffering and attain peace and happiness;
may those whose sense faculties are incomplete have their physical forms made fully perfect.
If there are sentient beings who encounter the suffering of illness, their bodies emaciated and without support, [may they find relief].
May all illnesses and sufferings be eliminated, And may their faculties, complexion, and strength be fully restored.
If they have violated the king’s law and face execution, Oppressed by manifold sufferings and filled with grief,
When they endure such extreme agony, There is no one to turn to for refuge or protection.
If they are subjected to whips, staves, shackles, and fetters, Or various instruments of torture that pierce their bodies,
And endure immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sorrows and afflictions, Oppressing both body and mind without a moment’s joy—
May they all be freed from such bondage As well as the suffering of whips and staves.
Those facing execution shall obtain their lives preserved, and all sufferings shall be forever and utterly eliminated.
If there are sentient beings oppressed by hunger and thirst, they shall be granted various kinds of sublime flavors.
The blind shall regain their sight, the deaf shall hear, the lame shall be able to walk, and the mute shall be able to speak.
May impoverished sentient beings obtain treasuries, With granaries overflowing so that they lack for nothing;
May they all be enabled to experience supreme and wondrous bliss, Without a single sentient being undergoing suffering or affliction.
May all humans and devas joyfully behold them, Their countenances mild and refined, most dignified and majestic.
All shall experience immeasurable bliss; Abundant enjoyments and merit shall be provided according to the beings' thoughts, with music and song appearing before them.
At the thought of water, cool ponds appear, Upon which golden lotuses float.
In accordance with the thoughts and wishes of those sentient beings, may they be fully provided with food, drink, clothing,
bedding, gold, silver, rare treasures, exquisite lapis lazuli, necklaces, and all manner of ornaments;
may no sentient being ever hear an unpleasant sound, nor shall they ever behold anything discordant.
The physical forms they assume are all dignified and majestic; each possesses a heart of loving-kindness and is filled with joy.
All the worldly necessities of life and various means of pleasure are fulfilled exactly as they wish upon thought.
Regarding the precious wealth they obtain, they have no sense of stinginess, distributing it as gifts to all sentient beings.
Incense, powdered incense, and unguents, A multitude of wondrous flowers of manifold colors, Fall from the trees three times each day; Enjoying them according to one's heart, joy is born.
May all sentient beings universally make offerings To the Most Victorious Honored Ones of the ten directions.
May the pure and wondrous Dharma-gate of the Three Vehicles— The assembly of Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas—
Ever vow not to dwell in lowly or base conditions, Nor to fall among the eight states of no-leisure,
But to be born among those with leisure as noble beings, And always be able to personally attend upon the Buddhas of the ten directions.
May I always be born into wealthy and noble families, With treasuries and granaries all filled to overflowing;
May my countenance and reputation be peerless, And may my lifespan extend through kalpas.
I pray that all women may be transformed into men, Brave, vigorous, intelligent, and possessed of great wisdom.
Constantly practicing the Bodhisattva path, Diligently cultivating the six perfections to reach the other shore,
They constantly behold the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions, Seated peacefully beneath jeweled king trees upon lion thrones of exquisite lapis lazuli,
Ever able to personally receive their turning of the wheel of Dharma.
Whatever karma has been created throughout the three realms of existence in the past and present—
karma that invites rebirth in loathsome and unwholesome destinies— may it all be extinguished without remainder.
May all sentient beings within the ocean of existence be released from the firm bonds of the snare of birth and death.
May I, with the sword of wisdom, sever [all afflictions] and, free from suffering,
swiftly realize the state of Bodhi. Whatever various causes of supreme merit beings have created here within this Jambudvīpa, or in other world-systems, I now rejoice in them all.
By means of this merit from rejoicing, And the various virtues created by body, speech, and mind,
I pray that these supreme deeds may ever increase, And that I may swiftly realize unsurpassed,
great Bodhi. All the merit of praising the Buddhas, With a profound mind pure and free from stain—
Through this dedication and aspiration, merit shall be boundless; One shall transcend sixty kalpas of miserable realms.

Should any man or woman, Or those of noble lineages such as Brahmins, Join their palms with single-minded devotion to praise the Buddha, They shall constantly remember their past lives in every birth.
With all faculties pure and the body perfected, May you achieve all supreme virtues.
In all future places of birth, May you always be gazed upon by gods and humans alike.
Not merely under one or ten Buddhas, But having cultivated various roots of goodness, may you now hear this.
Only by planting roots of goodness in the presence of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas Can one hear this method of repentance.
(Following with the Avataṃsaka Verses: May I always behold all the Tathāgatas, Surrounded by the assemblies of their sons and disciples.
To them all, may I offer vast and great offerings, Without weariness or fatigue throughout all future kalpas. (Strike the chime and ring the bell.)

Now, having prepared this food, I recite the mantra so that all beings throughout the six realms may universally receive this offering. Indeed, the essence of all dharmas is True Suchness (*tathatā*).

Neither form nor emptiness, it is thus able to manifest wondrously. Therefore, from the great chiliocosms to the smallest motes of dust, throughout the past, present, and future, and in every single kṣaṇa and thought-moment, within the One True [Dharmadhātu], both essence and appearance are perfectly luminous;
there is not a single subtle excellence that is not fully possessed therein. We reverently contemplate our World-Honored One, Vairocana Tathāgata, who exhausts the source of the entire Dharma-realm.
The base [of reality] blends the three bodies—the dharma, reward, and transformation—into one. For all sentient beings, it fulfills every request while its own essence never moves.
Therefore, the conceptual measurements of "great" and "small," or "coming" and "going," are already shattered.

Acting spontaneously and effortlessly, there is nothing that cannot be accomplished. Thus, the transformation body was dispatched to proclaim the Dharma gate of offering food, so that within a single...

Empower all things; give rise to the immeasurable; pervade the entire dharma-realm; and universally manifest offerings.

Recite twenty-one times).

(Strike the chime and ring the bell.)

(The Ritual Manual states: "Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra that bestows the nectar of immortality. I shall now reverently recite it. (Sound the great fish-drum; all recite together seven times.)

(The Dharma Master reflects: "Since this water has received the power of the mantra, it is transformed into nectar. These boundless articles of offering are each suited to the heart's desire, and all inspire the aspiration for the Way.")
(The Auxiliary Text states: I now reverently proclaim the holy names of the seven Tathāgatas. Each and every name possesses great power and efficacy.

The Treatise says: The Dharma cannot be grasped as an offering, yet an offering cannot be made without the Dharma.

If one offers the Dharma, what is this Dharma? To present it in the upper hall and again present it in the lower hall—as if there were something truly graspable to be carried and bestowed—is the Dharma really like this? If it were indeed so, then the Dharma...

This is merely the ordinary way of things; how could it be worth taking to provide for offerings? When people of this world lose their minds yet still practice the Dharma, they have in fact lost the Dharma itself.
What is there to maintain when one speaks of "practicing the Dharma"? One who practices offerings while ignorant of the Dharma is but a bhikṣu in name.
Therefore, I have painfully pierced this with a needle. If you do not sever yourself from the Dharma, then cease [these practices] for now.
Carriages and horses: rest your body and mind early, and there shall surely be unexpected good news.
(The Master of the Dharma said: All things are empty; therefore they can manifest as existing. All dharmas are wondrous; what could be considered coarse?
It is not apart from language and writing, yet it is not that either. It is precisely within form, fragrance, taste, and touch. You all should be thus. All...

The Buddha is likewise. Though their stations are divided into superior and inferior, they fully manifest the radiance of the mind. As the vital energies circulate between the holy and the mundane, they eternally abide at the fundamental limit.
Who bestows and who receives? This is difficult to discuss and difficult to conceive. Since all myriad transformations are eternally constant, the One Reality is devoid of delusion.
(Representing the two aspects of the primary Dharma, concentrate the spirit and form the mudrā of dhyāna-concentration.)

(The Master of the Dharma said: "The diverse phenomena appearing before you are fundamentally identical with the Truth. To realize that the nature and characteristics of all dharmas are boundless is to contemplate according to principle within a single thought-moment.
With a mind as empty as a valley, hearing the Dharma is like hearing thunder. When ice reaches spring, every fragment melts away;
when leaves encounter autumn, every petal falls off. Where are the sense bases and their objects? There is only the single true mind, which does not receive [external impressions]."
He deceives none; he thus perfects his own power. Therefore, one should harmonize the mind with the wondrous Dharma, so that our offerings may not be in vain.
(Strike the chime and ring the bell.)

(The Dharma Master’s visualization: The three kinds of giving are simultaneously mobilized, satisfying the hearts of all beings. Worldly dharmas and Bodhi are entirely without differing characteristics; all receive the joy of the Dharma and attain the coolness of liberation.)

The Illumination of Pervasive Radiance: Amitābha Buddha.

(The Dharma Master says: Through such expedient means, if one does not forget them at every meal, one will personally behold Amitābha; one will not be far from the Buddha. Without relying on expedient means, one spontaneously attains the opening of the mind.
