Suffering is difficult to exhaust through ten thousand words; yet these four characters of the Great Name can shatter suffering everywhere. All you sons of the Buddha, listen to the voice of the Buddha!

Through the karmic conditions of self and others, may every thought protect you. Spontaneously, the Buddhas of the ten directions shall guard your body and mind, causing your roots of goodness to increase day and night. (Ring the chime and shake the bell.)
(The Master of the Dharma kneels and proclaims: "The preceding rites of the Water and Land Altar have been completed.
All resulting merit is now dedicated to all sentient beings. May all sentient beings quickly awaken their perfect faculties and swiftly hear the wondrous Dharma.

May their bodies and minds be pure and white, and may they possess radiance day and night. May all enmities and karmic debts be extinguished, may their kin and followers be harmonious, and may they attain supernatural powers."
Swift is the response; the Dharma-lineage is serene and peaceful. All vows are fulfilled, and all undertakings are accomplished. One flies to the Land of Ultimate Bliss and joyfully beholds Amitābha.
For anyone who directs even a single thought of faith toward the Buddha, there shall be no suffering or hardship; they will proceed directly upon the broad highway.
Whenever one gives rise to practice and cultivation, it is entirely sustained by the central point, never falling into extremes.
Whenever a single matter triggers the mechanism for defending the Way, a true spiritual friend appears before them, ensuring they do not encounter demons or heretics.

Whenever a single circumstance happens to enter into principle, the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power protects their life, so that they will surely achieve perfect realization. For the sake of the assembly, I— [have spoken thus].
Life draws forth thread after thread to enter the mechanism. Sentient beings rely upon me; I melt all phenomena into light through transformation.
If there is anything they seek, I vow to fulfill it through skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*) so that their cultivation may be expedited. If there is anything they perceive...
I shall open them all with compassion and rectitude, leading them back to the correct path. I shall serve as a model for all spirits, bringing them to the same wisdom and vision as the Buddha.
Each shall manifest dependent origination, and all shall be made to return to the source. Upon conditions that are without [specific] objects, I first establish universal conditions;
upon weak conditions, I create superior conditions; upon hidden conditions, I reveal manifest conditions; and upon conditions of suffering—
I act as a catalyst for the conditions of happiness. For those who are distant, I lead them toward intimate conditions;

for those who are artificial, I suddenly break through them with genuine conditions. At all times, in all places, with all resources, and regarding all dharmas, I associate with them without suspicion;
I exhort and admonish them without leaving a trace; and I serve as their companion.
Yet they do not realize this; they merely give rise to joy. I establish rules for them all, and they do not transgress them; over time, these become natural.
I attend to their every need and comfort them all, yet their habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*) are not subdued.
I employ the dual conditions of rigidity and flexibility to transform them. Since the root of craving is difficult to uproot, I stir it with the dual mechanisms of adversity and favor.

They fall [from the path]. If one develops even a single heart of reverence toward the True Dharma, or a single heart of attachment toward false cultivation, or performs a single act of offering to celestial deities, or seeks refuge in demons or heretics, the mind-ground remains unclarified.
Hurrying back and forth, I have vainly borne my good intentions while sinking deeply into evil retributions.

Now, by the power of this offering to the Buddhas, Dharma, Sangha, and the immeasurable sages and worthies, may I suddenly possess the numinous roots [of virtue] and be able to respond perfectly to each and every sentient being—
whether in initial matters, intermediate matters, subsequent matters, in hardships, or in dreams— remaining steadfast.
In the midst, he demonstrates the ripening conditions through skillful preaching of the Dharma, fully realizing what is difficult to express and courageously bestowing the grace of fearlessness.
May the essence of the *amṛta* enter the heart, may the *amṛta* be poured as an empowerment, may celestial robes fit the body, and may the jeweled mirror appear before one like the sky.

I pray that the Triple Gem of Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, along with devas, immortals, nāgas, and spirits, will comprehend the minds of sentient beings and fulfill today’s aspiration—whatever is thus contemplated.

May all sentient beings be enabled to cross over. With joy following and compassion responding, when delusion is exhausted and the truth is fully realized, at the end of this single lifetime, they shall certainly be born in the Pure Land.
Any sentient being who wishes to be born in the Pure Land in the same year, month, day, and hour as I—such a wish shall surely be fulfilled;
such a wish shall surely be fulfilled. Within the mirror of empty luminosity, the wondrous emerges from Sahā.

Within the light of compassionate mercy, the Dharma-realm is perfectly realized. (Strike the chime; ring the bell; inquire after their well-being; withdraw. On this day at noon, provide a meal for the Sangha; substitute money for the rice, according to the previous ritual.)

*Discourse on the Commonality of Nature in the Ritual Site for the Universal Benefit of the Great Vegetarian Offering for the Holy and the Profane of the Dharma Realm, Aqueous and Terrestrial Beings*, Scroll Six.

*Discourse on the Commonality of Nature in the Ritual Site for the Universal Benefit of the Great Vegetarian Offering for the Holy and the Profane of the Dharma Realm, Aqueous and Terrestrial Beings*, Scroll Seven.
By the Practitioner of Pure Karma, Zhi Guan, Zheng Yingfang.
The Sixth Day of the Upper and Lower Hall Offerings (Fourth Watch;

the Master of Dharma enters. The Petition Master says: With all sincerity, we take refuge in the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm. (Bowing; strike the chime and ring the bell.)

(The presiding master offers incense for each position in turn. Having finished, he returns to his place and makes this announcement: "The Buddha Tathāgata possesses a mantra for conveying messages by means of burning incense.
I shall now recite it with due reverence" (the presiding master recites it himself).
Oṃ śrīvajramaṇi aprakūṭa suparṇi vikāci hūṃ. (Strike the chime and ring the bell. [Two persons withdraw; one person remains with incense and a lamp to guard the gate.

The Master of the Dharma prostrates three times toward the upper direction, circumambulates three times, and makes this aspiration. (This may be recited silently or composed in prose; it is of esoteric significance and must not be leaked.)
○ (At times, sitting briefly upon a rush mat, he concentrates his spirit and speaks again:
(After the Master has personally finished the blessing, the chime is struck; three prostrations.)
(The two attendants enter to serve. The Master of the Dharma circumambulates while reciting twenty lines of verse; the two attendants join in at a low voice. (Master raises his voice:
A single thought in accord brings an end to the suffering of birth and death; Grasping dissolves, emotions exhausted, the mind, Buddha, and sentient beings are empty.
The wondrous, bright, true, pure, vast, and great mirror opens; Wisdom emits light, penetratingly illuminating the boundless.
The heart-mirrors of the twelve classes of beings, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, reflect within them a profusion of rising and falling transformations;
therein also appear the wondrous reflections of the inexhaustible Triple Gem. The power and function of their majestic spiritual protection are inconceivable;
the precious mirror-altars fill the realm of empty space, a singular path of purity and sublime, wondrous adornment.
Fragrant clouds, rains of flowers, music, fruits, lamps, and ointments—layer upon layer, they enter into the mirror of a single thought-moment.
The light of this mirror shines through, shattering the ten directions and the three periods of time;

it startles the humans, devas, and those of the two and three vehicles, as well as the spirits, immortals, ghosts, and beasts, until all their myriad reflections return to the source. Its majestic roar resounds, causing the hells to open wide and split asunder.
A great lotus flower suddenly appears, surrounded by immeasurable sons of the Buddha seated upon its petals and filaments.
Riding this flower, I perform many deeds of buddhahood; without moving body or mind, I dwell securely in the mirror of bodhi.
(The two parties each recite one verse; the presiding master expresses sympathetic joy.)

Inscription on Faith (Aided by Silent Listening) (The Correct Lifting) The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it only dislikes picking and choosing. Simply do not harbor hatred or love, and you will be transparently clear and bright.
A difference of a hair’s breadth, and heaven and earth are as far apart. If you wish for it to manifest before you, do not maintain compliance or resistance.

When opposition and compliance contend with one another, this constitutes a sickness of the mind. Failing to recognize the profound principle, one merely exerts oneself in vain while striving for stillness.
When the Perfect and the Round are identical to the Great Void, there is neither deficiency nor excess. This is truly due to grasping and rejecting;

therefore, it is not as good as not pursuing external conditions. Do not dwell in the patience of emptiness; maintain a single state of equanimity, where all things are naturally extinguished in stillness.
Ceasing movement returns to stillness; ceasing stillness further increases movement. To remain stuck in these two extremes, how could one know that there is but a single principle?

If one does not penetrate this single principle, one fails in both places. To dispel existence and pursue non-existence, or to follow emptiness while turning one’s back on emptiness—through such excessive words and excessive thoughts, things become increasingly discordant.
When words are cut off and thoughts are extinguished, there is nowhere that penetration does not reach.
Returning to the root, one attains the essential meaning; following after illumination, one loses the source. If you reflect back for even a moment, it surpasses all prior states.
These transformations of emptiness arise entirely from deluded views. Do not seek the truth; simply cease your views.
When these two views do not abide, be careful not to pursue them. As soon as there is right and wrong, the mind becomes chaotic and lost.
Two arise from one; even that one cannot be maintained. When the single mind does not arise, the myriad dharmas are without fault.
Without fault, there are no dharmas; without arising, there is no mind. If you can follow along with the extinction of objects, the objects will sink along with the subject.
Objects arise from the subject, and the subject arises from the objects. If you wish to know these two segments, they are fundamentally one emptiness.
The One Emptiness is identical to the Two; together they encompass the myriad phenomena. When one perceives neither the refined nor the coarse, how could there be partiality?
The substance of the Great Way is vast; it is neither easy nor difficult. Those with narrow views harbor doubts; the more they strive, the slower they progress.
To grasp it is to lose its measure and inevitably enter a deviant path; to let it be natural is for its substance to have no coming or going.
To act spontaneously in accord with the Way is to roam at ease, free from affliction. To fixate the mind is to deviate from the Truth;
dullness and torpor are not good. Why weary yourself? What use is there for intimacy or estrangement? If you wish to attain the One Vehicle, do not loathe the six sense objects.
If you do not loathe the six sense objects, you will be identical to Perfect Enlightenment. The wise act without effort; the ignorant bind themselves.
In the Dharma there is no separate dharma; yet one delusively clings to it with self-attachment. To employ the mind by means of the mind—is this not a great error?
Birth is tranquil, yet one creates confusion; upon awakening, there is neither good nor evil. All dualistic extremes arise simply from grasping at dreams, illusions, and empty flowers;
why labor to seize them? Let gain and loss, right and wrong, be all cast aside at once.
If the eyes do not sleep, all dreams vanish of themselves; if the mind does not differ, the myriad dharmas are one suchness.

The essence of this one suchness is profound and mysterious; suddenly forgetting all conditions, one regards all dharmas as equal. Returning to the natural state, that which grounds it is extinguished;
it cannot be compared by analogy. Cessation within movement is non-movement; movement within cessation is non-cessation.
Since duality is not established, how can there be unity? Reaching the ultimate limit, no rules or patterns remain;
the mind accords with equality. All that is done ceases; doubt is completely purified. Right faith becomes harmonious and upright;
nothing remains to be clung to, and there is nothing to be remembered. Empty clarity illuminates itself spontaneously, without taxing the power of the mind.
Beyond the realm of discursive thought, the conscious mind finds it difficult to fathom. Within the *tathatā* dharma-realm, there is neither other nor self;
one must urgently seek resonance with this. It is spoken of as non-duality alone; in non-duality, all are identical.

There is nothing that is not encompassed. The wise of the ten directions all enter this school. This school is neither extended nor contracted; in a single thought-moment, ten thousand years are contained.
Neither abiding nor non-abiding, the ten directions are before one’s eyes. The extremely small is identical to the great; boundaries and realms are utterly extinguished.
The extremely great is identical to the small; no limit or surface is seen. Existence is itself non-existence; non-existence is itself existence.
If it were not thus, there would be no need to maintain [this practice]. One is all; all is one.
If one can simply act in this way, what need is there to worry that [the goal] will not be accomplished?
With a mind of faith that is non-dual—wherein non-dual faith cuts off the path of words—it is neither past, future, nor present.
(Assistant: Raise this. *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, Chapter on the Goddess Mahāśrī. (Main: Listen in silence.)
At that time, the Great Goddess Śrī arose from her seat, went before the Buddha to prostrate at his feet, joined her palms in reverence,
and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, if I should see any bhikṣu, bhikṣuṇī, upāsaka, or upāsikā who receives, maintains, recites,
and explains to others this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, the King of Sutras, [I shall protect them]."
I shall single-mindedly and with reverence make offerings to these Dharma-preachers— namely, by providing food, drink, clothing, bedding, medicine,
and all other necessary requisites— so that they may be fully provided for and lack nothing. Whether by day or by night,
I shall contemplate and reflect upon all the words and meanings of this King of Sutras, [thereby attaining] peace and happiness.
And may this sutra remain and be widely circulated throughout Jambudvīpa,
so that those sentient beings who have already planted roots of goodness under immeasurable hundreds of thousands of Buddhas may constantly hear it, and it shall not quickly disappear.
Furthermore, for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of kalpas, they shall experience various superior joys among devas and humans;
harvests shall always be abundant, famine shall be forever eliminated, and all sentient beings shall constantly enjoy peace and happiness.
They shall also encounter the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and in future ages, swiftly realize the fruit of unsurpassed, great Bodhi, forever severing the cycle of the three miserable realms.

"O World-Honored One, turn back these hardships! I recall that in the past, there was a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Ratnakusumaprabhābhāsasvastyayanaguṇasāgara, endowed with the ten titles. Under him, I planted various roots of goodness.
By virtue of that Tathāgata’s compassionate concern and his majestic spiritual power, I am enabled today—"
In whatever place they dwell, in whatever direction they look, and in whatever country they arrive,

they are able to cause immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of sentient beings to experience all manner of happiness, including everything necessary such as clothing, food and drink, and the requisites for life.
Gold, silver, lapis lazuli, mother-of-pearl, agate, coral, amber, pearls, and all such treasures shall be made fully available.
Furthermore, if there should be anyone who with a sincere heart recites this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*,
they should also daily burn various famous incenses and exquisite flowers as an offering for me to that mountain of lapis lazuli.
Furthermore, you should daily recite my name during the three periods of the day and separately make offerings to me with incense, flowers, and various fine foods.
You should also listen to and receive this wondrous King of Sutras; by doing so, you shall obtain such merit. Thus, he spoke in verse:
By being able to uphold this sutra in such a manner, one’s own person and retinue will be free from all decline;
there shall never be a time when food, clothing, or other necessities are lacking.
One’s majestic radiance and lifespan will be inexhaustible, the essence of the earth will constantly increase, and the various devas will send down rain according to the seasons.
May all the hosts of devas be filled with joy; may the deities of the gardens, groves, grains, fruits, thickets, and fruit trees all flourish and prosper.
May all crops reach full maturity, and may those who seek precious wealth have their wishes fulfilled;
may everything they contemplate be accomplished according to their hearts' desire.

The Buddha said to the Great Goddess Śrī: "Excellent, excellent! That you are able thus to recollect your past causes, to repay kindness through offerings, and to benefit and bring peace and happiness to boundless sentient beings by disseminating this sutra—your merit shall be inexhaustible."

(The Master of the Dharma said: "The phenomena and their underlying principles interpenetrate; the ten gates are perfectly complete. Like mirrors, minds reflect one another; the single path is pure and void.

Having roughly expressed my sincerity in making these offerings, I venture to fully set forth the vows of my entire life. May the holy and the mundane witness this together, and may the dust-motes and lands shine upon one another.
Thus, facing this Dharma assembly with reverence, I lay bare my accumulated sentiments."

(Orthodox Text) By the merit of this *maṇḍala*, I dedicate it to the *dharmadhātu*. May I and all sentient beings, regarding the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*), have minds that are not startled or disturbed.
Whether within the *maṇḍala* or having emerged from the *maṇḍala*, may we always roam in the Heaven of Meaning (*Arthasvarga*), gloriously propagating the lineage of the Dharma.
May there be auspiciousness and unimpededness; may all that we turn toward be perfected. Adorned with merit, may we never depart from the primordial limit (*koṭi*). [May our] retinue...
Rejoicing, all enter the True Dharma; the Dharma-realm is peaceful and stable, extending to the end of the future (awakening to the ultimate truth).
(The Assistant says: By the merit of this site of enlightenment, I dedicate it to the Dharma-realm. May I and all sentient beings first attain joy.

One attains entry into the Dharma-gate, whereby wholesome conditions immediately arise and wondrous deeds are accomplished. All other evils are extinguished, and the very roots [of affliction] are forever purified.

In a single thought-moment, one enters the subtle; in an instant, one transcends all realms. By means of these four dharmas, one travels throughout the ten directions, serving immeasurable Buddhas and immeasurable Bodhisattvas.
Following their skillful means, one exhausts the very source and bottom of the Dharma, leaving no lingering regrets behind. To the end...
The future limit (self-cultivation).
(Correctly stated: By means of the merit of this *maṇḍala*, I dedicate it to the *dharmadhātu*. May I and all sentient beings, with a single thought-moment, [attain...]
Forming the lotus-seed, the spirit dwells in peace and bliss; entering this stage without doubt, non-retrogression serves as both cause and fruit.
Passing on through continuous transformation, one’s retinue becomes boundless; all vows are fulfilled, and there is nothing that does not reach its destination.

The sublime golden terrace appears miraculously, and one personally traverses the precious ground. Through the gate of skillful means, one attains the ultimate path; saving oneself and saving others, [the work] is complete.
To the future limit (rebirth in the Pure Land).
(The assistant says: By means of the merit of this site of practice, I dedicate it to the Dharma-realm. May I and all sentient beings have the roots of our precepts purified.
Accomplished through flowers of the highest grade, his wisdom and supernormal powers are preeminent in all respects. He manifests emanations throughout the world, transforming according to his will.
Sustained by the Buddha’s power and assisted by divine spirits, he delivers sentient beings without hindrance; defilements and karmic burdens are extinguished.
His skillful means are inexhaustible, extending to the end of the future (as his transformation bodies enter the world).
(Orthodox Text) This merit from the *dharmapūja* site is dedicated to the *dharmadhātu*. May I and all sentient beings, regarding all vows, take the Buddha as our primary principle.
Through many lifetimes in previous kalpas, may they be fused into a single thought-moment.

May evil vows be utterly extinguished, virtuous vows fully perfected, mixed vows dissolved, and true vows alone revealed. At all times and in all places, may the power of our original vows manifest before us. Original Vow.
Within this light, may the assembly of retinues be perfected, and through successive transformations and deliverances, may this continue until the end of the future (the vow of determination).

(The assistant says: By means of the merit of this *dharmamegha* (site of awakening), I dedicate it to the *dharmadhātu*. May I and all sentient beings, within the gates of the Buddha-dharma, [attain realization].
Excellently able to rejoice in others' merit; neither drifting nor falling, and without deliberation, they solely benefit sentient beings, causing all to achieve fulfillment.
Solely upholding right view, they cause all to attain enlightenment. Solely following virtuous capacities, they cause all to increase.

Solely honoring the True Dharma, they cause it to circulate everywhere. Whether manifesting for themselves or for others, whether manifesting emptiness or existence, they may demonstrate universal arrival, or...
Encompassed by this light, I rejoice with a single mind throughout the limits of the future.
(The correct reading says: By means of the merit of this site of enlightenment, I dedicate it to the Dharma-realm; may I and all sentient beings, through transformation bodies, [attain liberation].
Throughout all lands, he extensively practiced giving; whatever was requested, he fulfilled their wishes entirely.

Whether something was obtainable or unobtainable, he first illuminated the situation with the power of meditative concentration and subsequently applied the power of wisdom to satisfy their desires, causing them all to give rise to joy.
Only those who sought with ill intent did he necessarily break apart, so as to serve as a ground for receiving offerings in the future.
He gives with earnest devotion until the end of the future (Siddhānta 1).

[The Assistant says: By means of the merit of this *maṇḍala*, I dedicate it to the *dharmadhātu*. May I and all sentient beings, by means of transformation bodies (*nirmāṇakāya*), [attain liberation].
Before sentient beings, they understand their various languages and gather them in entirely through words of love.
Whether using the sounds of the Dharma or worldly sounds, whether among the great assembly or in secluded places, whether manifesting a physical form or remaining without trace or influence,

they act for all those whose suffering and joy have not yet been expressed, whose emotional attachments have not yet been shattered, and who remain bound by the retribution of karma and lingering in the cycle of cultivation.
Along the way, they stumble through misplaced faith and erroneous doubt; their grief and joy are excessive, and their hearts are filled with trepidation, finding no consolation.
I console them all until the end of the future (Siddhānta II).

(Orthodox Text) By means of the merit of this *dharmapūjā*, I dedicate it to the *dharmadhātu*. May I and all sentient beings, through transformation bodies (*nirmāṇakāya*), act for the benefit of others at all times.

Whether engaged in worldly affairs or establishing a *dharmapūjā*, should our blessings and wisdom not yet be perfected, or if there is a lapse in timing, or a deficiency in human resources, material resources, wealth, land, the Dharma, or favorable conditions—may [all these deficiencies] be fulfilled.
There are many points of discrepancy that lead to calamity and fault; I shall manifest all that they require for them, so as to satisfy their needs.
Whether coarse or refined, everything shall be provided, throughout the limits of the future (Siddhānta III).
(Attendant says: By the merit of this *dharmadhātu* site, I dedicate it to the *dharmadhātu*.
May I and all sentient beings, through transformation bodies (*nirmāṇakāya*), manifest various forms within the realm of sentient beings to act as their companions.

Whether they be those in turmoil or those in tranquility, the insentient or the sentient, matters great or small, and whether their conditions be real or delusive, may I protect their minds in every way and rely upon me for their salvation. I am their protector.
As for its physical form: when its task is finished, it departs; when the time comes, it returns again, continuing until the end of the future (the fourth *siddhānta*).
(The correct reading states: By means of the merit of this *maṇḍala*, I dedicate it to the *dharmadhātu*. May I and all sentient beings, with a mind of ultimate reality, [attain enlightenment].
Yet they exercise great compassion, universally uprooting all sufferings—those of the three miserable realms and the four evil states, as well as those of humans and devas;
whether expressible or inexpressible, visible or invisible—all such sufferings are entirely extracted and rescued, not out of a desire for personal gain.
Not retreating out of resentment, one saves all with equanimity throughout the limits of the future (the first of the immeasurable minds).
(The assistant says: By means of the merit of this *dharmadhātu* site, I dedicate it to the *dharmadhātu*. May I and all sentient beings, with a mind of truth, [attain awakening].

He gives rise to great compassion and universally bestows peace and happiness. Whether small or great, temporary or permanent, provisional or ultimate, subtle or coarse—whosoever is capable of receiving it, all are granted this bliss.

Through these traces he manifests his spiritual power, benefiting sentient beings and extinguishing afflictions, leading them into the True Doctrine for as long as the future reaches (the two immeasurable minds).
(Orthodox Text) By means of the merit of this *dharmadhātu* site, I dedicate it to the *dharmadhātu*. May I and all sentient beings, with a mind of truth, practice great joy.
Whatever good there may be—whether it be the initial arousal of the aspiration for enlightenment or the completion of its fruition—may its radiance fill the *dharmadhātu*.
I shall, with a heart as vast as the entirety of space, rejoice. Whether manifest or through secret empowerment, may it be so.
May those sentient beings increase their power of progress and have their spiritual consciousness remain untiring throughout the limits of the future (the third of the immeasurable minds).
(The assistant says: By means of the merit of this *dharmadhātu* site, I dedicate it to the *dharmadhātu*. May I and all sentient beings, with a mind of truth, [attain enlightenment].

Yet I practice great equanimity. For all sentient beings, as long as their consciousness has not yet been transformed and their capacity for awakening has not yet matured, they remain in a state of confusion and mutual entanglement where the two paths have not yet diverged.
Whether due to residual false habits or attachment to perverse conditions, they fail to enter true cultivation and instead compete in producing unwholesome thoughts.
Although I clearly perceive them and abide before them, I do not give rise to even a single thought of haste. Thus...

It increases their suffering. Yet, by means of divine light, one establishes the protection of the outflow-free (*anāsrava*). Until the end of the future limit (the fourth of the immeasurable minds). (Correctly stated:
By means of the merit of this *maṇḍala*, I dedicate it to the *dharmadhātu*. May I and all sentient beings, by means of the body of wisdom...
There appear clouds of pavilions in empty space, layered high and low, encompassing both the coarse and the subtle.

They cause all sentient beings to roam their spirits within these realms: those who maintain a pure mind ascend to the wondrous state, while those who give rise to mixed thoughts retreat into the coarse realm.
Although there is thus progress and regression, it is because the spirit is fundamentally the Reward Body (saṃbhogakāya) that remains within the six paths of existence. However—
Regarding those in their retribution bodies—whether they have entered meditative concentration, dreams, deep sleep, or intoxication—I employ my supernatural powers to gather them into the clouds.
Within various pavilions, I manifest diverse forms to serve as their companions and preach the essentials of the Dharma for them.

This is because all those who have not yet been born into a Buddha-land, nor yet shattered ignorance, possess strong habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*) and extremely inferior retributive environments; thus, their physical forms and spirits [are constrained].
There is no obstruction. This [consciousness] matures here while that [body] is born there. Once the summoning is efficacious, a long-standing attachment is formed.

If those of sharp faculties awaken, they do not enter the intermediate state (*antarābhava*), but manifest transformation bodies (*nirmāṇakāya*) that endure until the end of the future, like a pavilion in space.
(Attendant said: "By the merit of this dharma-assembly, I dedicate it to the Dharma-realm.

May I and all sentient beings, throughout the atoms of lands in the ten directions, universally manifest clouds of bodies—neither existent nor non-existent, neither coming nor going, neither other nor self, neither one nor many.
With wondrous reflections vast and profound, like mirrors and like the moon, may they manifest my physical forms in accordance with the mental capacities of others. True.
The opportune moment will surely be met; the numinous realm is not separated [from us]. As habitual perfuming matures and transforms, what need is there for further action or effort?
Perfectly interfacing with the boundless, one extends throughout the limits of the future, universally manifesting clouds of bodies.
(Orthodox Text) By means of the merit of this *dharmadhātu*-maṇḍala, I dedicate it to the entire *dharmadhātu*.

I vow that I and all sentient beings, throughout the atoms of lands in the ten directions, shall manifest formless bodies to preach the Dharma. Whether through sound, form, taste, fragrance, touch, or mental objects;
whether as earth, water, fire, or wind—may these stir the numinous mind and bring about the perfect fulfillment of wondrous encounters, thereby uprooting [afflictions].

Delusion is awakened, laxity is dispelled; concentration subdues chaos and eliminates depravity. The response to conditions is inexhaustible, extending to the end of the future (manifesting as the bodies of insentient things).
(The assistant says: By the merit of this *dharma-cakra* (place of practice), I dedicate it to the *dharmadhātu*.

May I and all sentient beings, throughout the atoms of lands in the ten directions, manifest bodies of empty space and preach the Dharma for them. May we transform our environments and metamorphose our bodies and minds, making them serene.
That which is dense is made sparse; that which is obscure is made manifest. Without being spoken of, it is understood; one has already entered the True Dharma.

Body and spirit find rest, and wondrous practice is fully revealed. As the sense bases and their objects dissolve, the power attained becomes ever greater. The empty and numinous spirit is brought forth, extending through the bounds of the future (manifesting the body of empty space).
(Orthodox Text) By means of the merit of this *dharmadhātu*-maṇḍala, I dedicate it to the entire *dharmadhātu*.
May I and all sentient beings, at all times and in all places—whether in the mundane or the supramundane—completely eliminate the defects of all various *dharmamukhas*.

Through manifold powers and skillful means, may we thoroughly dismantle and refine the defective causes, defective conditions, defective phenomena, and defective karmas, so that they return to a great sameness through the six aspects (*ṣaḷlakṣaṇa*).
Lingran: The single reality is unimpeded throughout the limits of the future.
(The assistant says: By means of the merit of this *dharma*-field, I dedicate it to the *dharmadhātu*.

May I and all sentient beings, at all times and in all places, whenever we wish to make offerings to the Buddhas or wish to benefit living beings, may infinite sublime realms arise one by one, like the banners of stars.

Cloud-belted attendants come and go amidst them, so that all necessities are perfectly fulfilled with spiritual wonder. Whatever one wishes for is surely obtained; whatever one desires follows one’s thoughts.
It is like springtime in its blossoms, like autumn in its moon; harboring the single-minded resolve of a parent, it shall bring forth benefit throughout the bounds of the future.
