With single-minded devotion, we offer this to the Fourth Seat: the Patriarchs of the Chan and Pure Land schools, the masters of the Teachings and Vinaya, the various sects of the Qu and Zhi lineages, the divisions of the Xing and Xiang schools, and all monks who turn the Wheel of Dharma.
We pray that each of you, together with your retinues, may dwell in peace within this sacred precinct.
At this very moment today, we receive this Dharma-offering. (Ring the chime; shake the bell; perform one prostration together. (The Master of the Rite says:

With single-minded devotion, we present this offering to those in the fifth seat: those of the nine grades of superior goodness who have attained rebirth in the ten directions, the non-retrogressive Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas, and those who are in their final birth before Buddhahood.
We pray that you will each come with your retinues and dwell peacefully within this sacred precinct.
At this very moment today, we receive this Dharma offering (strike the chime; ring the bell; prostrate together). (The Master of the Dharma says:
With single-minded devotion, we present this offering. To the Sixth Seat: The Flower Treasury is translucent and vast, its wondrous adornments presided over by the World-Honored One.
Neither ordinary nor holy, you have entered the stream of the Buddha-dharma. We pray that you, together with your retinues, will dwell peacefully within this sacred site. At this very moment today...
Receiving this Dharma offering (strike the chime; ring the bell; perform one prostration together). (The Ritual Master says:
With single-minded devotion, we present this offering to the seventh seat: You who are either immortals or the Immortal One, who are the Immortal One and the Buddha;

you who have deeply entered the ocean of Dharma and manifested traces within the ranks of the immortals; you, the sons of the Buddha among the immortals—may you each, together with your retinues, dwell peacefully in this place of practice.
On this day, at this hour, we receive this Dharma offering (strike the *qing*, ring the bell; perform one prostration). Question:
Why does the Immortal wear the Buddha’s [attire]? The Master of Treatises says: "If he did not wear it, he would descend from the hall.

In ancient texts, the Immortal was confused with those ascending the hall, while the Confucian was suppressed as descending from the hall; it is better to treat them both equally and harmoniously. Question: Regarding the monk...
"One does not bow to Heaven; why, then, do you bow to Confucianism? The Master replied: "It is not that I bow to Confucianism; it is merely the Sangha of ultimate truth (paramārtha-saṃgha).

The dregs and the provisional teachings are entrusted to the lower hall, where they undergo diligent refinement. Those who now ascend to the upper hall have all deeply entered the Dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) and are people who have realized their nature (darśana-dharmatā);
they share the same realm as the Buddhas. It is for this reason that 'Buddha' is mentioned seven times, yet not mentioned eight times."
Why is this? The Master of the Treatise said: "The immortals take speaking of the Buddha as an honor; the Confucians take speaking of the Buddha as a shame.
As they accord with worldly conventions, the name appears or remains hidden therein; this is precisely what makes the Buddha the Buddha."

(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this service. To those of the eighth seat: the sages and worthies among men; who penetrate the Three Powers, establish the ultimate for the myriad people, and overcome themselves through the Way.
We pray that you, together with your retinues, may dwell in peace within this sacred precinct at this very hour and on this very day.
[Ring the chime. Shake the bell. Inquire after their well-being. Prostrate. (The Ritual Master says:
With single-minded devotion, we present this offering to the Ninth Seat: the Tathāgata’s Manifestation, the Vajra Honored Deities, the Ten Great Vidyārājas, and the assembly of Bhadrakanyās.
We pray that you, together with your retinues, will dwell peacefully within this maṇḍala at this very hour and on this very day.
Receiving this Dharma-offering (strike the *qing*, ring the bell, inquire after their well-being, and prostrate).
(The presiding master says: With single-minded devotion, we present this offering to the tenth seat, situated near the Tathāgata’s throne.

All you spirit-kings who protect the Buddha, protect the Dharma, protect the Sangha, and protect the nation—may you each, together with your retinues, dwell peacefully within this sacred precinct. On this day, at this very hour...
Receiving this Dharma offering (strike the chime, ring the bell, inquire after their well-being, and prostrate).
(The presiding master says: With single-minded devotion, we present this offering to the eleventh seat.

For the sake of the causes and conditions of the Great Water-Land Retreat, may the kings, scholars, officials, and śramaṇas, together with all their retinues, take their peaceful place within this sacred precinct. On this day, today...
At that time, having received this Dharma-offering (the sounding of the chime, the ringing of the bell, the inquiry after one's well-being, and the prostration), someone asked:
"The śramaṇa places himself after the king; is this not a reversal of the proper order? The Master of Treatises replied:
"This is to first attend to those within the mundane world and subsequently to those beyond the mundane world. As it is also said in the Great Sūtra: "Brahmā, Śakra, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas..."
As for the "Gates," they do not rigidly distinguish between the holy and the mundane, but explain according to the text.

(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this twelfth seat to the various devas of the realm of emptiness and form, those of the six heavens of desire and the nine stages of the formless, the sun, moon, and constellations—those who practice the Dharma to benefit living beings.
We pray that you will each come with your retinues and dwell peacefully within this sacred precinct. On this day...
At this time, receive this Dharma offering (strike the chime, ring the bell, inquire after their well-being, but do not prostrate).

(The presiding master says: With single-minded devotion, we present this offering to the thirteenth seat. You who transcend the divine and enter transformation, refine the vital breath to return to the source, and belong to the nine grades of immortals—whose initial harmony with the Buddha’s melody is peerless—we pray that you, together with your retinues, may dwell peacefully within this sacred precinct. On this day, now...
At that time, having received this Dharma-offering (the chime was struck, the bell was rung, and greetings were exchanged;

no prostrations were made). He asked: "Regarding the nine stages within the heavens, what are they? The Master of the Treatise replied: "Four of the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*), four of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), and one of the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*).

As for the immortals (*ṛṣi*) who preside over the heavens, why are they excluded? If they are indeed excluded, then ten types of erroneous cultivation should have been listed; why then do you contradict the Buddha’s sincere teaching?"
[The interlocutor] says: "They are arbitrarily divided into nine grades. The Master of the Treatise replies: "That which is listed in the scriptures of the immortals (ṛṣi) is detailed as nine grades.

To rely on the words of the immortals and follow them is also one way of conforming to sentient beings; it is not a turning away from the Buddha. When the Buddha speaks of a ruler of a state, he also refers to him as a 'Great King' (Mahārāja), yet does not refer to him as a 'Lord of the World' (Lokapati);
this is likewise an example [of such conformity]. Question: Why not [refer to them] by titles such as 'Imperial Lord' (Dijun) or 'True Person' (Zhenren)?"

"Regarding the 'Divine Lord' (Shenjun), there are three levels of high and low. The Master of the Treatise says: In that teaching, celestial beings and immortals are conflated into a single path of ascent and descent;
now that they have been distinguished, their common title is no longer applied."

(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this service. To the fourteenth seat: the eight classes of majestic spirits, whose numinous power is equal to that of the heavens, yet who, not having fully perfected their saintly merit, dwell in the station of ordinary beings.
We pray that each, together with your retinues, will rest peacefully within this site of practice.
On this day, at this very hour, may you receive this Dharma offering. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell. Perform the inquiry after bowing; do not prostrate.)

(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this service. To those on the fifteenth seat: the four kinds of Universal Monarchs (*cakravartin*) throughout the worlds of the ten directions, who manifest majestic spiritual power and travel through the air to teach and transform beings—we pray that you each come with your retinues and dwell peacefully within this *maṇḍala*.
On this day, at this very hour, may you receive this Dharma offering. (Ring the chime, shake the bell, inquire after their well-being, but do not prostrate.)
Question: Why are the eight classes not divided into superior and inferior groups? The Master of the Treatise said:
"The inferior ones include non-humans, hungry ghosts, animals, and asuras. Question: Since devas and asuras are already treated separately, there would only be six classes among the superior eight.
The Master of the Treatise said: "This assembly was established on the basis of eight classes; their names cannot be changed."

Question: Why does the Wheel-Turning King specifically represent the ten directions? The Master of the Treatise says: It is because one laments that there is currently no Wheel-Turning King in this world-system.

(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, offer worship. This is the sixteenth section: "The Superiority and Inferiority of Microscopic Particles," wherein each category of human condition may be considered as sacred.
It may be ordinary, yet now it transcends the past and overcomes decline. We only pray that each of you, together with your retinues, will dwell peacefully within this site of enlightenment.
At this very day and hour, accept this Dharma-offering. (Strike the chime; ring the bell; inquire after their well-being; do not prostrate.)
(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this service. To the seventeenth seat: the four classes of great-bodied Asura hosts.
May your anger be momentarily subdued and the power of forbearance arise within you. We pray that each of you, together with your retinues, may dwell peacefully in this sacred precinct.
On this day, at this very hour, receive this Dharma offering. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell. Inquire after their well-being; do not prostrate.)
(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this service. To the eighteenth seat:

You who manifest as spiritual beings, sporting with supernatural powers, appearing in non-human forms, newly awakened to the Buddha’s transformation—may you each, together with your retinues, dwell peacefully within this sacred precinct.
On this day, at this very hour, accept this offering of the Dharma. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell. Inquire after their well-being; do not prostrate.)

(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this service. To those in the nineteenth seat, whose spirits are dimmed and who belong to the ranks of superior or inferior ghosts:
upon first hearing the sound of the Dharma, you shall transcend your current state. We pray that each of you, together with your retinues, may dwell peacefully within this sacred precinct.
On this day, at this very hour, receive this offering of the Dharma. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell. Inquire after their well-being; do not prostrate.)

(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this service. Twenty-first seat: Beings of a thousand kinds and ten thousand varieties, formerly termed "animals," differing in their spiritual and physical capacities, now return to this single station.
We pray that each, together with their kin, may dwell peacefully within this sacred precinct.
On this day, at this very hour, receive this Dharma offering. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell. Inquire after well-being; do not bow.)
Question: "Who is this person of a single station? The Master of the Treatise said: "I fear you will fall into error with your words. He further said:
"When a gentleman contemplates this, a sense of unbearable compassion arises spontaneously within him.

Those who of old painted the various forms of the three evil realms were like geese passing over the Yangtze River leaving their reflections; they possessed little of the power of spiritual transformation."
(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this service. For the twenty-first seat: Cease swallowing iron balls; desist from drinking molten copper.

Having already escaped the shackles of the iron chain, you now partake of the refined essence of *sarpis*. We pray that each of you, together with your retinues, may dwell in peace within this *maṇḍala*.
On this day, at this very hour, receive this Dharma offering. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell. Exchange greetings; do not prostrate.)

(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we present this offering. To the twenty-second seat: The intermediate state between death and birth is a temporary dwelling, not permanent.

In a single thought-moment one enters the subtle; may you no longer undergo rebirth in the various realms. We pray that you, together with your retinue, will dwell peacefully within this sacred precinct.
On this day, at this hour, receive this Dharma-offering. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell. Inquire after their well-being. No prostration.)

(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this service. To the various deities who serve within and without the ritual site, throughout the eight directions, above and below—whose minds rely upon the True Dharma—we pray that each, together with their retinues, will dwell peacefully within this ritual site.
On this day, at this very hour, may you receive this Dharma offering. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell. Inquire after their well-being; do not prostrate.)

(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, offer this service. To the twenty-fourth seat: You have received the transmission according to your capacity; you have come for the sake of the Dharma.
Cultivate yourself through right mindfulness and transcend all numerical measures instantaneously. We pray that you, together with your retinue, may dwell peacefully within this sacred precinct.
On this day, at this very hour, receive this Dharma offering. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell. Inquire after their well-being. No prostration.)

(The Master of the Dharma says: With single-minded devotion, we offer this service. To those at the twenty-fifth seat: you possess the most profound affinity; though you have not yet realized the outflow-free state (*anāsrava*), your cultivation of hearing has reached maturity.
Your spiritual lineage shares the same causal roots. We pray that each of you, together with your retinues, may dwell peacefully within this sacred precinct (*maṇḍala*).
On this day, at this very hour, receive this offering of the Dharma. (Strike the chime. Ring the bell. Inquire after their well-being. Do not prostrate.)
(The *Zhengbiao* states: "Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for making offerings.
I shall now reverently recite it: OṂ GAGANA SVABHĀVA ŚUDDHA SVĀHĀ. (Ring the chime and shake the bell.
[The Dharma Master visualizes: May all the holy altars receive these offerings and, filled with joy, protect and mindfully regard this site of practice."
(The assistant recites: "The secret empowerment and inconceivable power permeate all things; their exquisite beauty is inexhaustible.

Universally honoring the Buddhas and devas, equally nourishing both ordinary beings and sages, we take refuge in the Dharma-realm to manifest our utmost sincerity. (Ring the chime, shake the bell, and perform three prostrations together.)

(The assistant says: Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for offering incense. I shall now reverently recite it. (In general, when making an offering, one should specifically raise both hands at the altar of universal offerings to express reverence.)
Oṃ sarvatathāgata dhūpa vyūha-maṇḍala samudra spharaṇa samaye hūṃ. (Ring the chime and shake the bell.
The Dharma Master visualizes that clouds of incense fill twenty-five seats before all ordinary and holy beings.)
(The Ritual Manual states: "Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for offering flowers.
I shall now reverently recite it: Oṃ sarvatathāgata puṣpa pūjāṅga samudra spharaṇa samaye hūṃ. (Strike the chime; ring the bell.)
(The Dharma Master visualizes: clouds of flowers fill twenty-five seats before all ordinary and holy beings.
(The Assistant Proclaims: "Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for offering lamps; I shall now reverently recite it."
Oṃ sarvatathāgata-nīva-pūjā-maṅgala-samudra-supraraṇa-samaye hūṃ. (Strike the chime; ring the bell.
[The Dharma Master visualizes that clouds of lamps fill twenty-five seats before all ordinary and holy beings.]
(The *Zhengbiao* states: Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses mantras for offering food and offering clothing. I now reverently recite them:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatānugrahapradīpamānasamādhi pūjāvaśana vañcana puṣpa.
JAMMIGA SAMUDRĀ SŪPHARANA SAMAYE HŪṂ. (Strike the chime; ring the bell. (The Dharma Master visualizes:
various garments, foods, drinks, teas, and fruits arise like clouds of exquisite jewels, pervading the twenty-five seats before all ordinary and holy beings.)
(As the assistant recites: The Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses the Mantra for Offering Jewels. I shall now reverently proclaim it:
Oṃ sarvatathāgata-mahāvajra-upamānāpāramitā-pūjāṅga-samudra-spharaṇa.
Samaye Hūṃ. (Strike the chime; ring the bell.
[The Dharma Master visualizes: clouds of jewel-colored light pervade the twenty-five seats before all ordinary and holy beings.]
(The *Zhengbiao* states: The Dharma-gate has no exterior; the function of the mind is most supernal. Upon what do form, sound, fragrance, taste, touch, and phenomena rely?
It is through the manifesting of the general and the particular, the same and the different, and formation and disintegration that the single ground of mind constitutes all wondrous gates.

This offering is like the ocean, yet it is but a single drop among the hundred rivers. This offering is like a mirror, wherein a thousand li are contained within a square inch. This offering is like gold, its true color...
It does not shift. This offering is like a lamp: distinct lights dwell together. This offering is like a single crescent moon in an autumn night:
light and shadow interlace. This offering is like a full mustard seed contained within a crystal vessel: high and low appear simultaneously.
This offering is like a net of a thousand pearls: light within the reflections, and reflections within the light. This offering is like a single-finger meditation:

it is not, yet it is; it is non-being, yet it is precisely being. This offering is like wealth and nobility in a dream: a mere moment, yet spanning a hundred years. This offering is like the stars in the heavens:
reflected upon ten sides, even a small thing is not insufficient; thus, it is called a manifold rite. I pray that—
To partake of this present offering, one may perfectly accomplish the Dharma-seal (the Master forms the seal of meditative concentration,
focusing the spirit to enter the realm of samādhi, so that the Dharma-ocean of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra manifests directly and without obstruction).
(The assistant says: "The Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for the Dharma-offering. I shall now respectfully recite it. (The Dharma Master remains in the *dhyāna-mudrā*;
both assistants speak the mantra together.)
Oṃ sarvatathāgata-avahiyā mahāparipūripramitā bhujamga samudra spharaṇasamaye hūṃ. (Strike the chime; ring the bell.)

(The Dharma Master contemplates: The boundless Dharma-realm consists of the subtle and wondrous six sense-objects. Offerings are made to both the holy and the ordinary, intermingling and penetrating one another. Whether one or many, large or small, preceding or following, short or long—all are entirely absorbed into the True Doctrine, beyond the reach of finger-pointing or verbal designation.
Infinite categories of beings are all molded and refined by it; seams vanish and edges dissolve, perfectly realizing the single horizon).

(The Master of the Dharma said: "This mind has no exterior; when the Dharma is applied, it becomes numinous. Before the Three Honored Ones and the successive sages, and extending universally to the assemblies of those ready for the teaching across the seven realms of existence, the falling flowers and the jingling bracelets all enter the true mechanism. Human forms and the fragrance of robes alike wander within the mirror of the Dharma.
One awakens to the fact that birth and death are like illusions and realizes that Bodhi is not empty. Through hearing, perfuming, reflection, and cultivation..."
Regarding this single matter of opening, showing, awakening, and entering, how could there be two causes?

Though I have exhausted all that I wished to say throughout my life, I rely upon the Buddha, the World-Honored One, and do nothing of my own making; may we together bestow our protective mindfulness and collectively celebrate its perfect fulfillment.
A single thought of aspiration; boundless Dharma activities. (Ring the chime. Shake the bell. ○ (Exit. Unlock the gate. Upon reaching the appointed hour, re-enter. One prostration.)

(Recite the intent of the main text. Recite the commentary as an auxiliary. When finished, the presiding master kneels and says: The rites of the Upper and Lower Halls for the Water and Land Ritual have now been completed in full.
All accumulated merit is dedicated toward the Flower Adornment and the Land of Ultimate Bliss, and toward the Land of Ultimate Bliss and the Flower Adornment.
May all sentient beings quickly awaken their perfect faculties and quickly hear the wondrous Dharma; may their bodies and minds be pure and white, and may they be radiant day and night.
Enmities shall vanish; kin and retinues shall be harmonious; spiritual powers shall be swift; the lineage of the Dharma shall be peaceful.
All aspirations shall be fulfilled; all undertakings shall be accomplished. May those who fly forth to Sukhāvatī behold Amitābha with joy.

For all who direct even a single thought of faith toward the Buddha, there shall be no suffering or distress, but a direct path to the broad highway. For all who give rise to practice and cultivate throughout their lives—entirely...

Holding the central point, one does not fall into extremes. Whenever an event arises that triggers the defense of the Way, a true spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) appears before them, ensuring they do not encounter demons or heretics.
Whenever a single circumstance happens to enter into principle, the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power protects their life, so that they will surely achieve perfect realization.
For the sake of sentient beings, I draw the thread to lead them step by step into the inquiry; as for sentient beings...

Because of me, the phenomena of the Dharma melt together and transform into light. If there is anything sought, I shall fulfill it through skillful means and expedient wisdom so that their cultivation may be swift.
If there is anything perceived, I shall open it all with compassion and rectitude to lead it back to the correct path.
I shall serve as a model for all spirits, bringing them to share the Buddha’s knowledge and vision; each shall manifest dependent origination, and I shall cause all to return [to the source].

The Source: First, one establishes universal conditions upon those that are conditionless; for weak conditions, one generates superior conditions; for hidden conditions, one reveals manifest conditions;
for conditions of suffering, one transforms them into conditions of bliss. Those who are distant are led into intimate conditions;
those who are false are suddenly severed by means of true conditions. At all times, in all places, with all resources—[one acts] as one.
With all phenomena, I interact with them completely, yet without suspicion; I exhort and warn them all, yet without leaving a trace;
I act as their companion, yet they do not perceive it, but instead give rise to joy;
I establish rules for them all, yet they do not transgress them, until these become natural over time; I serve them all. I...
I comforted them all. When their habitual tendencies were not subdued, I shifted them by means of the two conditions of rigidity and flexibility.
Since the root of craving is difficult to uproot, I caused it to fall away by means of the two impulses of adversity and favorability.
Whether it was a single thought of reverence toward the True Dharma, or a single thought of affection toward a false practice, or an act of offering to a celestial deity, or—
Māras and externalists establish a single refuge, yet they do not understand the ground of the mind; they come and go in haste, vainly bearing good intentions, and mostly sink into evil retributions.
Now, by the power of this offering to the Buddhas, Dharma, Sangha, and the infinite noble ones, [may I be liberated].
Suddenly endowed with spiritual faculties, they are able to respond perfectly and universally to such and such sentient beings—at the beginning of an event, during the event, or after the event;
in times of difficulty, in dreams, or within meditative concentration—manifesting as matured conditions and skillfully expounding the Dharma.

The profound mysteries of Siddhārtha are difficult to express; the fearless grace of Vīradatta is beyond compare. The essence of *amṛta* enters the heart, and the nectar of immortality is poured upon the crown.
Celestial robes fit the body, and the precious mirror hangs in the sky. One must surely pray to the Triple Gem of Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, as well as to the celestial beings, *devas*, and *nāgas*.
I shall realize the minds of sentient beings and fulfill my vow for this day. May all those whom I have in mind attain liberation.
Following joy and responding with compassion, when delusion is exhausted and the ultimate truth is realized, at the end of this single lifetime, I shall certainly be reborn in the Pure Land.
Any sentient being who wishes to be born in the Pure Land in the same year, month, day, and hour as I shall surely obtain their wish; they shall surely obtain it.
As wished. Within the clear mirror of emptiness, the wondrous emerges from Sahā; amidst the light of compassionate mercy, the Dharma-realm is perfectly realized.
(Strike the chime. Ring the bell.)
(On this day at noon, the monks are provided with a vegetarian meal. Money is used in lieu of rice, following the ritual procedures as described above.

To escort the Sage (all trays and other items are prepared and arranged before the universal offering table; each tray contains one portion of paper flowers, silver foil, and so forth). ○ (Separately, one copy of the draft of the *yìzhǐ* [intentional statement] and one copy of the draft of the memorial petition are included).

On the seventh day, during the hours of Wei and Shen (approximately 3–5 PM), those with the means should prepare twenty-four paper pavilions. Take twenty-four copies of the final fascicle of the *Pratītyasamutpāda-sūtra* (Xingyuan pin) and unroll them to be mounted within these pavilions.

Adorn the interior and exterior with blue, yellow, and red lines, using circles, dots, and hook-strokes; this is called the "Huayan Anle Pavilion" (Huayan Anle Ting) and is most excellent. If a pavilion is not used, a large jar (gāng) may also suffice.

Alternatively, one may burn precious silk and other items according to their inscriptions, while using only a single pavilion specifically for burning the name-plates and petitions to signify that at the end, all are shown to return to the same destination.

(The time has arrived. The Master of the Dharma enters the inner altar. First, he makes a formal inquiry and stands with his mind concentrated. Second, he arranges the ritual implements and makes an inquiry, saying: "I now universally observe all that fills empty space and pervades the Dharma-realm."
All holy ones and ordinary beings with one mind take refuge in the Flower Adornment Sukhāvatī and the Sukhāvatī Flower Adornment;
in the Mind-Mirror Amitābha and Amitābha the Mind-Mirror. (Three prostrations. Rise. Ring the chime. Shake the bell.)
(From the *Zhengbiao*: "The Tathāgata, our Buddha, possesses the *phala-praṇidhāna-mantra*. I shall now reverently recite it:
*Namo ratnatrayāya | namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya* ||
mahākāruṇikāya sarvanīvāsūdanāya siddhe samayasamaya nupara prabhuje samantabhadraprasādine gayanamīśuddhe mūrtiparvate.
Jaye mijaye kalyāṇasambhāvanīye niṣpādaya me siddhiṃ śodhaya śodhaya sarvavighnān gatān sthāpayitvā padmaśodhanīye svāhā. (Ring the chime; shake the bell.)

(The Dharma Master contemplates: "May I and all the sages and ordinary beings of the nine dharma-realms never regress from the realm of the Buddha. May we all be reborn in the Buddha-lands according to our vows. May those who share my vow each realize their fruition. For the sake of sentient beings, I give rise to various vows."

Uprooting all various sufferings, they are led into Bodhi; ultimately following the mind, each and every one attains the fruit. The iron chain of the six realms is ultimately entirely empty, and the stages of the Lotus Division clearly manifest.
(Second Announcement: The various empowerments are completed; the successive vows are fully fulfilled. Finally, holding up the incense, I take refuge in the One Buddha.
(Sound the fish-shaped gong. Recite the Buddha’s name together: Homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Flower Adornment Land of Peace and Bliss, whose light is unimpeded.
Forty-eight sounds. (Ring the chime. Shake the bell. (The Director of Rituals says:
The Great Water and Land Feast for the Saints and the Common People throughout the Dharma Realm has been established; the site of practice for universal benefit is now complete after seven days.
The formal petition (shu-wen) is present; it shall now be read aloud.

(The presiding petitioner and the assistant petitioner kneel together. The presiding petitioner reads the intent of the main petition, while the assistant petitioner reads the formal petition. When finished, they rise, the chime is struck, and they perform three prostrations and inquire after one another’s well-being.)

(2) Regarding the two types of tablets (*biao*) that enclose the commentary text: place a name tablet at the top and a paper or silk backing at the bottom, wrapping them in yellow paper. Secure both ends with strips of red paper and silver foil, and insert two red paper flowers. Place them on a tray; provide one tray for each seat.
First twenty-four, then twenty-three, down to the first. Those accompanying the seats do not enter the tray area; the trays are placed upon the tables at each seat.

(The assistant *hyō* chants: "Those holding the trays, enter. (Twenty-four people enter in succession. They perform a greeting (*monjun*). The two *hyō* arrange them, and they stand facing one another.
The two *hyō* hand the trays to each of them one by one—first the twenty-four, and finally the first.)
(From the *Zhengbiao*: "With a sincere heart, we take refuge and entreat the Buddhas, Dharmas, and Sanghas of the ten directions and the entire Dharma-realm. [The *Zhubiao* join in chanting.
"Constantly" [bow] "abiding" [rise] "inquiry" "Three" [strike the chime, ring the bell].)
(Stage Directions: When the musicians open the session for rest, eight persons stand outside the enclosure and play the music in unison.

First, one person carrying incense and a lamp leads the way; next, the banner-bearer; next, twenty-four lamps; next, twenty-four trays; next, twenty-three lamps; next, twenty-three trays, continuing in this manner down to the second tray; next, the first lamp; and finally, the lamp-bearer.

Next, lift the incense burner. Next, the two representatives. Next, the first tray. Next, the presiding ritual master. Next, the fourfold assembly. Proceeding to the outer altar, circumambulate three times and enter through the middle gate.
(The lamps, music, banners, and incense burners do not enter. The two outer insignia [biao] set out the trays. The presiding ritual master inquires after their well-being.

○ (The music ceases. (The main insignia says: "I pay homage to the musicians. (Eight persons enter the gate, four on each side, standing in a single file line. They perform three prostrations. Having finished, they inquire after one another's well-being and exit through the outer altar gate to rest in another location for a short while.)
(The assistant announces: The attendants prostrate (the incense-burner and lamp-bearer, the banner-bearer and censer-bearer—eight persons in total enter the hall and prostrate as above).
○ (Next, each successive group, eight persons at a time, proceeds in order until all have completed their prostrations).

(The Director of Ritual says: The fourfold assembly prostrates. (The assembly, eight persons per row, prostrates according to the previous method. When finished. ○ (Strike the chime three times; lower the curtain).
(The assistant announces: "The holy and the ordinary have assembled; the fourfold assembly remains silent. We reverently recite the mantra to manifest purity.
(Thereupon, four persons remain to strike the fish-drum while chanting the Great Compassion Mantra.)
(The Dharma Master’s Invocation. Proceeding to the desks of the Judges, the two invocations state: We respectfully invite the Judge of the Merit Office of the Celestial Bureau;
the Judge of the Merit Office of the Intermediate Realm; the Judge of the Merit Office of the Netherworld; the Judge of the Literary Treasure Office of the Upper Hall;
and the Judge of the Literary Treasure Office of the Lower Hall. The construction of this Water and Land Ritual Site has been completed for seven days, as follows:

The Text for Recitation: We respectfully announce it for reading. (Chant "Zhengyi" once; "Zhu" twice. (When finished, burn the text, the memorial tablet, and the precious silk plaque all at once. (The presiding master bows in greeting;
the ritual director bows in greeting; they then withdraw.)

(Beyond the main gate for incense and lamps, twenty-four jars are arranged in rows. Those who have paid their fees in silver coins place them outside the jars; according to the seating arrangement, each person provides a certain number of gold and silver ingots, all totaling ten units per jar.

Each jar is clearly labeled with the seat number, and attendants are stationed to guard them. Upon entering, one informs the presiding master of the Dharma. Then, the bells and drums are struck. The presiding master and the ritual reciter enter together. The curtains are rolled up. Those carrying the trays stand one by one before their respective trays, facing each other.

When the incantation ceases, the ritual reciter chants the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* three times. After a brief pause, they exchange greetings. (If there is a single pavilion, the name tablets and written petitions are brought inside the pavilion, while the jars are arrayed around the exterior. The lamps are again arranged in a circle outside the outer perimeter.)
(Namo to the One Vehicle’s Ever-Abiding Triple Gem. [Recite] three times. (The Master of the Dharma performs three prostrations and kneels. (The Assistant Reciter says:
"I bow my head to the Bhagavān, the Perfect Sūtra, and the Bodhisattva Saṃgha of the One Vehicle; may you all receive us with compassion.
The aforementioned construction of the Water-Land Ritual Site has been completed over seven days. There is a preface to be proclaimed. (Three)
Within the precious light, we humbly entreat you to look upon us with clear discernment.

(The ritual director reads the *zhengbiao* [main petition] to convey the intent; the assistant ritual director reads the *shubiao* [commentary]. When finished, the chime is struck, the bell is rung, and all rise together for three prostrations. ○ (This is read using a separate manuscript copy. ○ (The one holding the tray holds it while standing.)
(From the *Zhengbiao*): All phenomena are without birth; all phenomena are without cessation. If one can understand them in this way, the Buddhas are ever manifest before one.
This single assembly is serene and still; light and wind move with natural ease. The ten directions are clearly present; the Dharma-realm is perfectly realized.
Only the Honored Sages abide eternally in quiescence, fundamentally transcending coming and going, so as to enable ordinary beings to awaken thoroughly to the true home. How could it be otherwise?

Through the power of the Dharma supported by skillful means and enveloped in the Buddha’s light, they are guided from the left and supported from the right, showing compassion to those of the three capacities—whether of sharp or dull faculties.
Whether advancing from behind or hastening from the front, they all enter the subtle and wondrous ranks of the nine lotus assemblies.

They swiftly return to the Pure Land, perfectly awaken to the True Principle, draw near to Amitābha of the Fruitional Stage, and suddenly realize the Dharmadhātu of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra. Constantly...
Together with the three classes of new kinsmen, they come in unison to this Great Assembly of Universal Radiance.
(The assistant states: Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, possesses a mantra for escorting [the deceased]; I shall now reverently recite it.
Oṃ mārala mukhaṣa muḥ. (The Ritual Manual states:
The aforementioned construction of the Dharma-realm for the holy and the mundane, the Great Water and Land Feast, has been universally beneficial and completed in seven days at this site of practice.
Now, as we escort the sacred procession on its celestial journey, may the assembly with one mind chant the name of the Buddha to lead the way.
(The Assistant Announcer says: "The Music Master begins the performance. (Eight persons perform the music in unison.

(The Ritual Master performs a formal greeting toward the upper direction. The trays emerge in succession. The procession ranks as before and proceeds slowly, winding and turning to reach the full measure of the ritual. They exit through the main gate, again winding and turning to reach the full measure of the ritual.
They lead the procession before the oil lamps; the trays halt according to their assigned positions, and the lamps stand outside the containers for a brief moment.)
(The Master faces outward and recites the hymn of praise to the Buddha.
(All chant together: Fragrant light pervades the oceans of lands; this is the one ultimate True Doctrine. The jeweled royal palace manifests in its entirety throughout the ten directions;
Coming and going, it delivers all sentient beings from ignorance. Great vows are inexhaustible; the scope of the mind fills the void of space.

(The Master of the Dharma observes the twenty-four cauldrons. When finished, one person collects the large banner; another person leads the fire in succession. The Master of the Dharma faces the cauldrons from a distance, performs three prostrations with implements, and one inquiry. He then retreats several paces and stands still. When the twenty-four cauldrons are finished, he burns the scattered rice-offerings and the ritual tablet.
The music ceases. The Master of the Dharma does not move. The two representatives likewise face outward and perform an inquiry.)
(From the *Zhengbiao*): I take refuge in the Buddha; I take refuge in the Dharma; I take refuge in the Sangha.

Having completed the taking of refuge in the Triple Gem of Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, the aforementioned construction of the Great Water-Land Feast for the holy and the mundane throughout the Dharma-realm has reached its full completion over seven days at this universally beneficial site of practice (*bodhimaṇḍa*).

Through the refinement of ritual texts and the gathering of offerings, boundless roots of goodness have been established, their grace extending across the sands of the universe. I pay respectful homage to the assembly of sages.

(The Master of the Dharma makes a formal inquiry toward the outside. First he enters; the two attendants follow him. Once the incense and lamps have been inspected for their flames, they enter. Regarding all matters of the inner altar, the ritual implements and arrangements must be stored with reverence and care. The memorial scrolls and silk cloths for the auxiliary positions are burned within the enclosure below the altar).

(On this day, the *yogācāra* *yankou* rite was performed. At the hour of Hai, the side-tablet was withdrawn. ○ (If the occasion is long-term, one may transcribe the names of the most essential persons from the primary altar to the side seats, so that they may permanently attend the Dharma assembly.)
*Discourse on the Commonality of Nature in the Ritual Site for the Universal Benefit of the Great Water and Land Feast for the Holy and the Mundane of the Dharma Realm*, Scroll Eight.
*Discourse on the Commonality of Nature in the Ritual Site for the Universal Benefit of the Great Water and Land Feast for the Holy and the Mundane of the Dharma Realm*, Scroll Nine.
By the Practitioner of Pure Karma, Zhi Guan, Zheng Yingfang.
Iconographic Representations (with Praises), First Series (from the first to the eleventh seat; all have circular halos above their heads, with abundant gold and minimal color).
In the center of the design, paint a great Buddha. Use pale gold for the body, pale colors for the robes, and pale silver for the halo.
Within and without the body, manifest immeasurable Buddha-bodies and Buddha-lands; specifically, let one Buddha appear at the chest.
He grew slightly larger and sat upon a thousand-petaled lotus flower. Within each petal was a single Buddha, who praised him, saying:
"Vast indeed is the ocean of wisdom, entirely without bounds; resplendent indeed is the torch of knowledge, entirely without smoke. How serene and solitary!"
How vast and remote! The flute has no holes and the zither has no strings;
yet, layer upon layer, dense and thick, it seems to interpenetrate with all lands and atoms, and to revolve through the cycles of thought and eons.

Furthermore, it is helpless in its lack of beginning or end, lack of emotion or nature, lack of form or emptiness, and lack of correctness or partiality—yet it is called the "spiritual manifestation of the ten bodies."
It is all in vain. It is neither an ordinary person nor an immortal.
The second section consists of three tiers: first, the sutra scrolls; second, the vinaya scrolls; third, the śāstra scrolls. Sutra [Ten].
The two divisions are arranged side by side, with a third division added in the center, titled *Mahāvaipulya-buddhāvataṃsaka-sūtra*. The Vinaya is divided into the Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna;

the Śāstra is divided into fundamental treatises (*mūla-śāstra*) and commentaries (*vyākhyā-śāstra*). Adjacent to these are added the Miscellaneous Piṭaka (*kṣudraka-piṭaka*), such as ritual manuals for incantations, as well as the writings composed by the sages and worthies of India and China.
The eulogy says:
How could there be a body that attends the upper seat? Among the stalwarts at the Dharma assembly, you are the foremost.
Teacher of the Buddhas, mother of the sages; yet deluded people, lacking wisdom, seek you in emptiness and existence.
The Third Arrangement consists of three tiers: the upper tier for Bodhisattvas, the middle for Pratyekabuddhas, and the lower for Arhats.

To these are added images of all lay practitioners who possess the Way, regardless of whether they are male or female, or old or young, to represent the Saṅgha of Ultimate Meaning (such as the families of Pang, Li, and others).
The eulogy says:
Heavenly robes and jeweled necklaces; Wealthy, noble, and intelligent. Yet craving the small fruits, His spirit was somewhat lacking.
Among those in between, there was one man Like a unicorn with its single horn; A monk apart from the rest, Whose realization of the ultimate truth was transcendent and peerless.
The fourth seating arrangement consists of various distinct forms: those who deliver, receive, translate, edit, recite, or lecture upon the sutras;
those who practice asceticism; those who exercise spiritual powers; those who practice the Dharma; and those who rescue others from suffering, or who point to the moon.
As for their forms: some enter the mountains; some travel as wandering monks; some circumambulate stupas; some practice seated meditation; some recite mantras;
some perform prostrations and repentance; and some practice mindfulness of the Buddha for rebirth in the Pure Land.
The Praise says:
The eight classes assist the heavens; The six ministers govern the world. How bitter is the plight of common folk!
How sublime are the Bodhisattvas, spread out like stars upon a chessboard! With their precious minds serene and clear, They dwell in accordance with the Truth, Without distinction of past or present.
The Fifth Arrangement:
It consists of two tiers. On the upper tier, there is a pond with lotus flowers; one Buddha and two Bodhisattvas sit upon a flower pedestal.
Nine people kneel amidst the flowers to listen to the Dharma, surrounded by celestial music and auspicious birds. Below are the multitudes from the ten directions.
The signs of approaching death appear: first, the fourfold assembly; then, various other beings.

Above each one’s head is a single ray of light, and within the light is a lotus flower. Upon the flower sits a person kneeling with palms joined, their head encircled by a halo, as they are reborn toward the West.
To the West stands a Buddha and two Bodhisattvas, earnestly welcoming and guiding them. Between the Buddha’s eyebrows...
After five transformations of the light, it divides into hundreds of thousands of millions; within each individual ray of light, all those who have attained rebirth are gathered, beyond all counting.
The eulogy says:
Within nine lotus flowers is one *kumārabhūta*; Each and every *kumārabhūta* shares a single cause.
Hearing it said that the True Spirit has no second path, There is no need for immortal incantations to attain Eternal Spring.
Sixth, regarding the style of the seating arrangement: based on the *Avataṃsaka* and the *Lokeshvararāja*, it is best to depict each figure distinctly, with lively adornments and precise settings.
As there are many figures in this seating arrangement, they should be painted with meticulous care.
The eulogy says:

Venerable and divine, wealthy and noble, Great deity, sagacious and intelligent, With the majestic brilliance of precious gems, I have exhaustively examined my entire life to find its origin, Yet it is utterly impossible to discover; Only upon meeting Sudhana Did I find my true spiritual friend.
The Seventh Arrangement:
Depict various forms of ṛṣis, each with a circular halo around the head, signifying their entry into the realm of the Buddha.
The Praise says:
A single thread of the turning mind— Do not crave past delusions. With a cool, refreshing urging forward, The entire home mountain appears in its fullness.
Ten billion suns and moons are but a single realm of dust; Looking out to the infinite horizon, Where is there any place for a host of immortals?
May each and every world become my girdle and rings; come to partake of this Dharma-offering, reflected like images in a mirror within the eighth seat.
Although these [verses] belong to the Confucian masters of successive generations, they must possess a divine resonance; do not adopt the form of a pedantic scholar—a "fou ru" (腐儒).
This is what is gathered by those of the lower class of humanity; it is not for this seat. Upon the crown of the head is a golden circular mark, which is a radiance arising from being fully replete.
The eulogy says:
Who knows its joy? Vainly one sighs, "How virtuous! Grasping at principle and phenomena, One falls into both wheels of saṃsāra.
There is no need even to raise these two words, "saṃsāra. Deeply entering the Dharma-realm, One wishes to remain wordless.
The Ninth Section:
The Various Great Vidyārājas. All are wrathful in form and extremely terrifying (some wearing human-head rosaries, or having four heads and eight arms, with blue bodies and red hair, etc.).
There are also benevolent goddesses, whether civil or martial, all of whom possess supreme liberation and majestic radiance. Each...
The divisional sections were arranged, and the retinue gathered around.
They praised him, saying:
"Glorious Wrathful One, Heroic Roarer, Perfect in Compassion, Manifestation of the Goddess."
The One Buddha is majestic and sublime; above the heavens and below the heavens, he turns all according to the mind. The tenth seat-pattern of the eight trigrams of hardness and softness:
some are armored, some wear caps and robes; some are even, some are extraordinary; there are men and women, or celestial immortals, gods, and spirits.
The Rhyme: Or spirits and deities, majestic and awe-inspiring, each attended by many followers.
The eulogy says:
Concealing their forms, they stand in guard; Their retinue is exceedingly vast. They manifest transformations along every path, Like reflections in a mirror, never erring.
Golden walls and moat-like ditches; in the Buddha-land there are no demons. Where can one establish merit? In one's own nature lies Amitābha.
(The Eleventh Seat, Shi) Whether as a sovereign king, a high official, a bhikṣu, or a scholar, each harbors intentions of management and planning. As for the sovereign king...
The officials and scholars of the Liang dynasty wore their court robes; those of the Song dynasty numbered one or two kings and three or four officials.
There were also more than ten bhikṣus, each with their own retinues.
The eulogy says:
How excellent is this Dharma assembly! Even now it remains serene; its brilliance and essence are revealed as fragrant clouds and jeweled rains fly past the nine heavens.
All together they attend the Dharma feast; the lotus flowers seem about to speak, and the transformed birds harbor no resentment.
The twelfth seat (from this point downward, there is no light upon the crown; gold is scarce and colors are abundant; the body is not golden, though the robes contain a slight trace of gold).

Thus, among the heavens of the three realms: the realm of emptiness (*ārūpyadhātu*) is extremely subtle; the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) is extremely pure; and the realm of desire (*kāmadhātu*) is extremely flourishing.

Only in the realm of desire are there men and women, sovereigns and ministers, civil and military officials. Those in the realm of form all abide in meditative concentration (*dhyāna*); their emptiness is like that of a soul or spirit, sitting indistinctly in white robes.
In the heavens of form, the color is white like silver, and their faces and features are clearly manifest.
The Praise says:
Human speech from the edge of heaven, Not separated by so much as a hair’s breadth. In harmonious accord within one hall, The spirit transcends even the work of the Creator.
This natural state is unconfused; How many have missed it? Their idle chatter cuts like a blade.

The thirteenth posture is that of the Immortal of Immeasurable Life. It depicts figures of men and women, old and young, as well as teachers and disciples. Sometimes there are tortoises, deer, white cranes, and numinous fungi as accompanying motifs;

there may be an alchemical furnace for refining elixirs, the visualization of circulating the vital breath (*qi*), the inhalation of the radiant essence of the sun and moon, or the writing of talismans and the holding of them.
Wielding a sword, playing the lute, composing poetry, leaning on a cassia staff and carrying a gourd—his body dwelling among the rocky crags. In various forms, he is praised thus:
"Are you the Lord of the Clouds? Or a man of the mountains? Grasping this illusory reflection, The multitude cry out, 'Is this the Real'?"
Equal in renown to the Buddha, are you perhaps a Wheel-Turning King? Neither ordinary nor a sage, are you truly a guest of Reality?
(14th Seat) [The forms of] Yakṣas, Nāgas, Gandharvas, Mahoragas, Kimnaras, Garuḍas, Kumbhāṇḍas, and Rākṣasas. (8)

[The section on] the classes [of spirits]: Devas and Asuras are divided; the inferior eight classes also enter the realm of hungry ghosts (or alternatively enter the realm of animals), such as crows, dragons, pythons, and so forth. On their heads, one should paint their original forms and shadows:
the *yaksas* are suspected of having two horns; the *yakṣas* fly; the *rākṣasas* are fierce; the *kumbhāṇḍas* are ugly; and the *gandharvas* possess musical instruments.
The eulogy says:
Dragons, birds, pythons, and spirits; Music performed by the musical troupes; Rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, and yakṣas even more outstanding;
The sovereign, ministers, men, women, and the multitudes— Each one’s majestic power is briefly described.
Divine majesty fills the void; this matter may be deliberated upon.

(Fifteenth Seat Form) There are those who arrive with the initial wheel of sensation; there are those who rise into the air, about to move; and there are those who descend from mid-air, circling around.
The defenses were strict and formidable. Those from various states who submitted in awe included some who were currently flying through the air.
The wheel-marked jewel led the way before the King, followed by the ceremonial insignia; all other precious treasures were likewise fully prepared.
The eulogy says:
The Lord of Men who soars through the air— Never has anyone ever disobeyed him. The ten wholesome virtues are harmoniously refined;
His spiritual chariot and fragrant renown— Throughout the myriad lands, How many mental machinations there are! All at once they are set in motion, Awaiting the Buddha’s command.
Sixteenth, the Style of Seated Figures:
Although these are human forms, there is within their countenances and expressions a sense of spiritual resonance and communication; yet this is not the result of supernatural transformations.
Their essence has not yet been fully manifested, yet their divine spirit seems ready to take flight—this is what constitutes attaining the ideal.
The Praise says:
Body, face, and speech— A single stimulus draws forth the six. Born again and again within the tip of a snail’s horn, Who can serve as family or state?
Alas for these wretched insects! Their spiritual pulse flies through space; In a single thought-moment, they enter the subtle. Within the light, they receive blessings.
Seventeenth Seat: Asuras. The males are ugly and the females are beautiful. Their kings possess a fierce and heroic form; they are adorned with martial trappings and lack refinement.

Among them, some occasionally manifest their true forms with three heads and six arms, while others appear solemnly in the guise of devas. The females— *Note: The original text appears to be incomplete at the end.*
All were images of celestial bodies.
The eulogy said:
A single arousal of the mind of forbearance Fully opens the sublime realm; Failing to enter the ranks of the heavens Is due to being caught in the wind and thunder.
Water is inherently still; mountains naturally revolve. They are like reflections in a mirror or flowers in the sky. To perceive the world and know its ultimate return—this is the eighteenth seat.
Although he has assumed human form, among his intelligence there is little of an upright character, as his habitual tendencies have not yet been [transformed].
This is because, at one time, they were all transformed and exhausted. Yet, within that interval, there were one or two who possessed an air of integrity and uprightness;
this was because they had seen the shadow of the whip while riding a fine horse.
The eulogy says: Within illusion there is no affliction; this is the wayfarer. When the spiritual causes are complete, do not violate the mundane dust.
Wind and fire are not constant; supernatural powers are not the ultimate truth. When the real persists and the delusive is exhausted, there exists a distinct spirit.
Nineteenth, regarding the seating arrangement:
among the forms of humans and devas, there is no uniformity in terms of clarity and vigor or turbidity and inferiority;
however, their faces and garments should mostly be rendered in blue to represent their path of origin—this suffices. They must not be depicted as ghosts.
The eulogy says:
Inferior in nature, Suffering in body, With the dark winds howling, They deceive my true and eternal nature;
yet it is never deceived. If the fruit is mistaken, it is due to the cause; Swiftly it changes and departs.
The twentieth seat-style for the *Samāna-kṛta-prabhā-maṇḍala*:
the iconography of the deities. Their garments are of various colors with red predominating; their faces and eyes are likewise. These are the divine beings.
He still possessed but little spiritual acuity.
The eulogy says:
Śākyamuni, the Great Dragon King, was a white dog in his previous life; now he acts as the Teacher of Gods and Humans.
Majestic spirit encompasses the Buddha-land; A cicada is yet the heavens, a capacity is yet the abyss.
Transformation is non-transformation; The brush and ink are but clouds and mist.
The Twenty-first Section.

Generally, the forms and features of humans and devas—both their clothing and facial expressions—are mostly dark and only slightly white, signifying that the path they have traveled was extremely arduous.

This is because their injuries have only recently been removed and their habits of suffering have not yet long since passed. Nevertheless, among them there are also those who stand out as extraordinary;
such as the devas of Tuṣita Heaven and those newly emerged from Avīci Hell, who immediately transcend the mundane and enter the sacred, teaching billions of people.
Heaven! This is the realization of the stage of the Golden Wheel of the Ten Grounds (*daśabhūmi*).
It is praised thus:
The Linglong Hell is like a lapis lazuli vase; Each and every mustard seed is entirely the true spirit.
In a single morning, they burst through the void and fly forth, together entering the courtyard of Vairocana.
I have heard that in ancient times, beings from the Avīci hell were born in heaven, realized the Way, and transformed sentient beings until all attained the rank of a Golden Wheel-turning King;
even now, they appear as shimmering points of light, fluttering and moving like stars.

The twenty-second tableau depicts the forms of humans and devas. Their facial features are indistinct; their garments are pale white. Their expressions are flickering, appearing as if they have no support, yet appearing as if they do have support.
The Praise says:
How can one endure the cycle of rebirth? Before death and birth have even begun, one mounts the conditions to enter the assembly.
Like reflections in a mirror or the sound of a bell, light and sound shatter delusion; they strike down ignorance. How timely! How timely! Gloom and distraction are both purified.
The twenty-third seat-style:
A miscellaneous array of civil and military deities and spirits, including both men and women, as well as the noble and the humble.
With banners and pennants, jade pendants, talismans, seals, servants, and horses—their spirits, whether coarse or subtle, each distinct—all manifesting forms of swift and keen efficacy.
The eulogy says:
Adorning the void, the star-bannered constellations come and go; their forms are unseen, yet they cause people to reflect upon them.
Within this lies a subtle mechanism: neither extending nor contracting, acting according to its station, it has never once left its proper sphere.
Twenty-fourth Seat:
Amidst clouds and mist, there appear figures as if riding dragons or spanning cranes, traveling in carriages or walking through the air, manifesting postures of flight or poised stillness.
All are surrounded by their retinues; their features are indistinct, for as they hear the Dharma and receive its transformative influence, their ultimate state cannot yet be predetermined.
Regarding the superiority or inferiority of their retribution: Alas! When gold is melted in the furnace, who provides the mold?
The eulogy says:
Transverse and vertical, all-pervasive, A single star is occasionally revealed; Dissipating the specks of dust, The Dharma-realm is empty and numinous.
Who is near? Who is distant? The Buddha’s eye looks down with favor; I ask you to go straight ahead to the courtyard of peace and bliss.
(Twenty-fifth: Seating Arrangements).
Most are depicted facing forward; most are depicted in full body. Always according to the dharma assembly, their bodies and minds are virtuous, gradually revealing themselves.
The Symbol of Perfect Radiance.
The eulogy says:
Intricate veins interlaced, Neither born nor Buddha, A single expanse of numinous mechanism— How magnificent, how lushly flourishing!
Among them was one who was clever; He applied the "eye" [of life] and flew into the void. May he assist me in my governance, To save these masses of ignorant beings.
Plaque Format, First Seat, Ten Plaques: ○ The Ten Bodies of the Spiritual Characteristics of the Dharmakāya, Saṃbhogakāya, and Nirmāṇakāya of All Buddhas (the same for all ten plaques).
Second row, ten tablets: ○ The subtle and wondrous all dharmas of the past, present, and future (same as above).
Third row, ten tablets: ○ The various assemblies of the Sangha from the ten directions belonging to all vehicles (same as above).
Fourth row, ten tablets: ○ The ancestral masters and great spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) of the ten schools (same as above).
Fifth Row, Ten Tablets: ○ The Various Superior and Virtuous Persons Who Have Been Reborn in the Pure Realms of the Ten Directions (same as above).
Sixth Row, Ten Tablets: ○ The World-Ruling Lords of the Lotus-Treasury Wondrous Adornments, as numerous as the atoms in ten lands (same as above).
Seventh Row, Ten Tablets: ○ The Immortals Who Have Entered the Realm of the Buddhas of the Ten Directions and Are Stationed at Their Respective Ranks (same as above).
The eighth row, ten tablets: ○ The Ten Directions Entering the Buddha’s Realm, All Confucian Patriarchs (same as above).
The ninth row, ten tablets: ○ The Ten Great Vidyārājas, Female Deities Manifesting Throughout the Ten Directions (same as above).
The tenth row, ten tablets: ○ The Ten Lands’ Flying Bodies, Successive Layers of Dharma-Protecting Deities (same as above).
The eleventh seat, ten tablets: ○ The successive virtuous teachers (kalyāṇamitra) of the various lineages of the Water and Land (Shuilu) tradition (as above).
The above concludes the ascent to the hall;
the following is the arrangement of seats for the descent from the hall.
The twelfth seat, ten tablets: ○ The infinite, all-encompassing celestial spirits of the ten directions (the same applies to all ten tablets).

(Appendix) Form for Supplementary Petitions for the Water and Land Ritual (*Shuilu Daochang*).
The Śramaṇa respectfully submits this petition before the seats of the Triple Gem, the Dragons and Devas, and all true spirits within the Inner Altar of the Water and Land Rite.

I humbly submit that within the unimpeded realm of the *dharmadhātu*, the manifold aspirations of the multitude arise in succession. Having gathered all that is excellent, one must necessarily eliminate all afflictions;
by conforming to the nature of reality, one pervades the entire *dharmadhātu*, and by following the mind, one accomplishes meritorious deeds. Since there is resonance, there is penetration;

thus, through sincere emotion, one may reach upward to the ultimate. Now, there are faithful followers who rejoice in this *dharmadhātu* (the names and specific aspirations of those listed below), who, relying on the power of the Triple Gem, hope for—
"May your wishes be fulfilled," and so forth. We, the undersigned, having received the petition submitted by [Name], hereby respectfully submit this memorial for your wise discernment.
May your true compassion shine brightly, universally illuminating the dark alleys of the world; may the Dharma-position remain eternally secure, forever fulfilling the aspirations of the multitude.

By uniting the power of the great compassionate deities of the ten directions, we seek to rescue sentient beings from the conditions of mental suffering. May all that is deficient be made complete, and all that is obstructed...
Those who have been liberated are blessed; those still in the realm of birth attain transcendence. May they forever part from the myriad sufferings and fully manifest the one true reality.

With all our humble feelings, we humbly entreat you to provide comprehensive protection and sustenance, so that the full measure of this site of practice may be perfected. This is respectfully inscribed.
On the [day] of the [month] of the [year], the monk who officiates the ritual services of the Water and Land Retreat (Shuilu Daochang) respectfully submits this memorial.
[Seal of the] Donor. On the tally-stick, write:
"The Triple Gem of Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha of the Water and Land Retreat."
The Ritual for the Water and Land Path (Shuilu Daochang), with appended procedures for the *Yankou* (Feeding the Hungry Ghosts) according to the intent of various schools.
The Śramaṇa who upholds the teachings and performs the ritual services, humbly reflects: The karma manifested from the mind is both one and three;
when delusion is shattered and the truth revealed, who ascends and who descends? Because the multitude are deluded and fail to awaken, the Buddhas have therefore...

You have descended. Your wisdom awakens all without exception; your light shines with brilliant majesty. As the conditions for your guidance are nearing ripeness, the efficacy of your transformations becomes ever more manifold.
We reverently uphold the true mantras and scrupulously observe the ritual protocols, universally bestowing *bali* offerings to fully deliver all sentient beings.

Now, [listing names and aspirations], we rely upon the spiritual power of the Buddha’s grace to enable them to transcend this world and attain liberation, that all may be fulfilled according to their wishes. Thus it is said... We, [the undersigned], having already...

Having received this petition, it is appropriate to act in accordance with the Dharma and report the circumstances to those above. We humbly pray that those still living may receive blessings, and those who have passed away may transcend to higher realms.
May they be entirely freed from all suffering and the One True Reality be fully manifested. May there be not even a hair’s breadth of separation between Amitābha’s mirror-like mind and these beings;
may the lotus flowers of Sukhāvatī be completely open to receive their news.
